requirements.why: Stops a forged or replayed return from writing another organisation's address, or any address, into a notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today in address-return/controller.js (repo-frontend-p9-140, repo-frontend-p9-142, repo-frontend-p9-144).

requirements.statement: When a return cannot be completed, the trader goes back to the role's picker: an address that is not found or is deleted shows 'The address could not be found in your address book. Select another address or try adding it again.', and an address book that cannot be reached, or a save that fails, shows 'The address book could not be reached. Your answers on this page have been saved. Try again in a few minutes.'
requirements.why: A failed return must leave the trader somewhere they can carry on, with a reason they can act on.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today (repo-frontend-p9-145, repo-frontend-p9-146, repo-frontend-p9-150, repo-frontend-p9-151).

requirements.statement: A trader with no INS session who follows 'Add a new address' signs in through Defra ID first and then lands on the INS add page with the handshake intact.
requirements.why: The INS frontend owns its own session and stays the address book's only writer (c-106); crossing to it must not lose which notification and role the address is for.
requirements.deltaNote: Seen today end to end (trace-e2e-p9-052).

requirements.statement: The add-address page reached from the journey is headed 'Add address and contact details', with the browser title 'Add address and contact details - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's heading says the page collects contact details as well as the address.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the INS add page reached from the journey is headed 'Add address details' (trace-e2e-p9-055, repo-tests-p5-027).

requirements.statement: The add-address page shows the caption 'Add new address' above its heading.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 captions the page.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's INS add page has no caption (trace-e2e-p9-055).

requirements.statement: The add-address page shows the notification's status block, a 'Draft' tag and the notification reference, as the other journey pages do.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps the trader oriented in their notification while they add an address.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's INS add page sits in the INS layout with Address book marked in its navigation, and no notification status (trace-e2e-p9-055-m1).

requirements.statement: The add-address page has a Back link to the picker of the role the address is being added for.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives the trader a way back to the page they came from.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's INS add page reached from the journey has no back link (trace-e2e-p9-055).

requirements.statement: The add-address page's first section heading is 'Address'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the heading is 'Enter address details' (trace-e2e-p9-057).

requirements.statement: The add-address page's second section heading is 'Contact details'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the heading is 'Enter contact details' (trace-e2e-p9-057).

requirements.statement: The add-address page's name field is labelled 'Name or organisation'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the label is 'Name or organisation name' (trace-e2e-p9-058).

requirements.statement: The add-address page keeps the labels 'Address line 1', 'Address line 2 (optional)', 'Town or city', 'Postcode or Zip code' and 'Country' (a select), and address line 2 may be left blank.
requirements.why: These labels already match Design Release 2.1.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's INS add page already carries these labels (trace-e2e-p9-059, trace-e2e-p9-060, trace-e2e-p9-061, trace-e2e-p9-063, trace-e2e-p9-064).

requirements.statement: The add-address page has no County field.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's add form asks for no county.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's INS add page offers 'County (optional)' (trace-e2e-p9-062). The address book record keeps its optional county, left empty.

requirements.statement: On the place of origin and consignor add-address pages the Country select's first option reads 'Select one'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the first option reads 'Select a country' (trace-e2e-p9-064).

requirements.statement: The manual-entry Country select offers Design Release 2.1's 42 countries: the EU member states, their outermost regions (such as Azores, Canary Islands, Ceuta), the Crown Dependencies, Republic of Ireland and United Kingdom.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets an origin or consignor address sit in a region or territory the real list does not hold.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the list holds 32 sovereign states, United Kingdom first then EU and EFTA countries (trace-e2e-p9-064).
requirements.blockedBy: The MDM master reference-data integration supplies the country list (DR1 ruling, Rhys 2026-09-07); the hard-coded frontend list is not edited before then.

requirements.statement: Under 'Contact details' the add-address page asks for 'Email address' then 'Phone number', with the phone hint 'For international numbers include the country code'.
requirements.why: These fields and their order already match Design Release 2.1.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's INS add page asks for Email address then Phone number with the same hint (trace-e2e-p9-065, trace-e2e-p9-066).

requirements.statement: Place of origin and consignor addresses are entered by hand for any country, with every field shown at once; consignee, importer and place of destination addresses are UK addresses, whose Country select holds only 'United Kingdom', preselected, and whose saved country is always United Kingdom.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 splits the roles: origin-side parties can be anywhere, destination-side parties are in Great Britain.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the INS add page is the same for every role, with the full 32-country select (trace-e2e-p9-064).

requirements.statement: Every add-address page that searches (the consignee, importer and place of destination pages reached from the journey, and the address book's 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' add-details step) starts with a UK address search: a text field labelled 'Search for an address', placeholder 'Start typing...', browser autocomplete turned off, and a search icon button whose accessible name is 'Search'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 finds UK addresses by search rather than typing them in.
requirements.deltaNote: No address search exists today: the INS add page is typed in by hand (trace-e2e-p9-058).

requirements.statement: Typing in the address search lists matching UK addresses as the trader types, under 'Address search results', each a button showing the organisation name and the full one-line address with the typed text in bold; Northern Ireland addresses are not offered.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's search behaviour.

requirements.statement: The address search announces its result count to screen readers through a polite live region, such as '1 result available'.
requirements.why: Screen reader users must hear that results have appeared.

requirements.statement: Picking a search result hides the search box, reveals the address form and fills name, address line 1, address line 2, town or city and postcode with country United Kingdom, all still editable; email address and phone number stay empty for the trader to complete; any earlier error messages stay until the next submit.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's pick behaviour.

requirements.statement: Picking a search result never drops part of the address the lookup returned: a locality (such as Kirkby in 'Depot road, Kirkby, Liverpool') is kept in the filled form.
requirements.why: The prototype loses the locality because its form has no field for it; a saved address missing part of itself is a real data constraint the prototype cannot express.

requirements.statement: Below the address search, an 'Enter address manually' link-styled button reveals the address and contact fields without picking a result.
requirements.why: A trader whose address the search does not find must still be able to add it.

requirements.statement: On the search pages the address fields and the 'What else should this address be used for?' checkboxes stay hidden until the trader picks a result or chooses to enter the address manually, and are shown again after a failed submit when anything was entered or picked.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 reveals the form only once there is an address to complete.

requirements.statement: Submitting a search page before picking or entering anything shows the six field errors in order ('Enter a name or organisation name', 'Enter address line 1', 'Enter a town or city', 'Enter a postcode or Zip code', 'Enter an email address', 'Enter a phone number'), with no country error and no error of the search's own, and reveals the fields so each error summary link reaches a visible field.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's messages; the prototype's summary links point at hidden fields, which the GOV.UK error summary pattern does not allow.

requirements.statement: The add-address page asks 'What else should this address be used for?' as a checkbox fieldset.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets one new address be saved for more roles than the one it was added from.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's INS add page has no such question (trace-e2e-p9-058 to trace-e2e-p9-067).

requirements.statement: The uses question's hint reads 'This address is being added as a <Role> address. Select any other roles or addresses this address should be used for.', naming the role's own label (Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer or Place of destination) and using 'an' before Importer.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy; it tells the trader the role they came from is already implied.

requirements.statement: The uses checkboxes offer only the other roles on the same side, each labelled with the role name alone: place of origin offers 'Consignor'; consignor offers 'Place of origin'; consignee offers 'Importer' and 'Place of destination'; importer offers 'Consignee' and 'Place of destination'; place of destination offers 'Consignee' and 'Importer'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 never lets an origin-side address be marked for a destination-side role, or the other way round.

requirements.statement: No uses checkbox is preselected, ticking none raises no error, a value not offered for the role is discarded, and the ticked uses are kept when the page is shown again with errors.
requirements.why: The role the trader came from is implied; the extra uses are optional.

requirements.statement: An address added from the journey is saved in the address book carrying the role it was added for plus every use ticked, so the address book record holds its roles.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 saves the address with its types; today's record has no field to hold them, so the address book's persistence changes.
requirements.deltaNote: Today an address book record holds id, name, address fields, countryCode, phone, email, organisationId, deleted and timestamps, with no role or type (trace-e2e-p8-012).

requirements.statement: On the add-address page a blank name shows 'Enter a name or organisation name', linked to the name field.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's address book rules, which the journey copies, say 'Enter a name' (repo-frontend-p9-105, repo-frontend-p9-106); the INS add page's messages were never driven (trace-e2e-p9-069).

requirements.statement: On the add-address page a blank address line 1 shows 'Enter address line 1'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy, already used today.
requirements.deltaNote: The address book rules already say 'Enter address line 1' (repo-frontend-p9-108).

requirements.statement: On the add-address page a blank town or city shows 'Enter a town or city'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy, already used today.
requirements.deltaNote: The address book rules already say 'Enter a town or city' (repo-frontend-p9-111).

requirements.statement: On the add-address page a blank postcode shows 'Enter a postcode or Zip code'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's address book rules say 'Enter a postcode' (repo-frontend-p9-114).

requirements.statement: On the add-address page no country chosen shows 'Select a country'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's address book rules say 'Enter a country' (repo-frontend-p9-116).

requirements.statement: On the add-address page email address is required, and a blank one shows 'Enter an email address'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy, already used today.
requirements.deltaNote: The address book rules already require email with 'Enter an email address' (repo-frontend-p9-119).

requirements.statement: On the add-address page phone number is required, and a blank one shows 'Enter a phone number'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's address book rules say 'Enter a telephone number' (repo-frontend-p9-117).

requirements.statement: A failed submit of the add-address page shows an error summary titled 'There is a problem' listing every error in field order (seven on a blank manual page), each repeated inline with a visually hidden 'Error:' prefix and the field in its GOV.UK error style, and keeps everything the trader entered.
requirements.why: The GOV.UK error pattern, which Design Release 2.1 and today's address forms share.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's address forms already use this pattern (trace-e2e-p8-054, repo-tests-p5-067).

requirements.statement: The add-address page keeps the address book's length and format checks beyond the required-field checks: name and address lines 255 characters or fewer, town or city and county 100, postcode 12, phone 20, email 254 and in a valid format, each with today's message (such as 'Postcode must be 12 characters or fewer' and 'Enter an email address in the correct format').
requirements.why: The address book stores and validates these limits; a real validation constraint the prototype cannot express overrides its required-only checks.
requirements.deltaNote: The address book rules already carry these checks and messages (repo-frontend-p9-105, repo-frontend-p9-115, repo-frontend-p9-120; trace-e2e-p8-049, trace-e2e-p8-050).

requirements.statement: A refused add-address submit answers HTTP 400 and prefixes the browser title with 'Error: '.
requirements.why: The GOV.UK error pattern tells assistive technology the page holds errors; today's address forms already do it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's address forms answer 400 with an 'Error: ' title (repo-frontend-p9-124, trace-e2e-p8-047-m1, trace-animals-fit-p15-062).

requirements.statement: The add-address page's fields carry browser autocomplete hints: organization for the name, address-line1, address-line2, address-level2 for town or city, postal-code, email and tel.
requirements.why: GOV.UK and WCAG 1.3.5 ask personal-data inputs to identify their purpose; the prototype leaves them out.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's INS add page sets autocomplete only on the email field (trace-e2e-p9-065); the journey's edit page already sets them all (repo-frontend-p9-103-m1).

requirements.statement: The add-address page's primary button reads 'Save and select'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the primary button reads 'Save and continue' (trace-e2e-p9-067).

requirements.statement: 'Save and select' saves the new address to the address book, puts a copy of it on the notification for the role it was added for, and returns the trader to the Consignment addresses page, where the role shows the address with a 'Change' link.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 finishes the role in one step.
requirements.deltaNote: Today saving returns the trader to the role's picker with the new address preselected ('Selected address: <name>'), and they press Save and continue to reach the hub (trace-e2e-p9-071, trace-e2e-p9-073, repo-tests-p5-029, repo-tests-p5-030).

requirements.statement: A secondary 'Save and return to address page' button saves the new address to the address book without selecting it, and returns the trader to the role's picker, where the new address is listed first.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader add an address and still choose among the book.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the only secondary action is 'Cancel and return to address page' (trace-e2e-p9-067).

requirements.statement: After either save, the page the trader lands on shows a success banner titled 'Success' reading '<Name> address added to your address book'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 confirms the address went into the address book.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the picker shows only the 'Selected address: <name>' inset, no banner (trace-e2e-p9-072).

requirements.statement: The add-address page offers a 'Cancel and return to hub' link to the notification's hub, which saves nothing.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy and destination.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a secondary 'Cancel and return to address page' button returns the trader to the role's picker, saving nothing (trace-e2e-p9-075, trace-e2e-p9-076, repo-tests-p5-031).

requirements.statement: An address added from the journey is saved into the signed-in organisation's address book with its email and phone, and is then listed in the address book and in every role picker.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree that a journey-added address joins the shared book.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the INS save creates the record in the organisation's book and the picker count rises (trace-e2e-p8-011, trace-e2e-p9-074).

requirements.statement: The add-address page is built from GOV.UK Frontend components (input, select, checkboxes, hint, error summary, notification banner, buttons, back link, width classes); the address search is the one component outside the toolbox, because GOV.UK Frontend has none.
requirements.why: The prototype's app-* field and heading classes are its own implementation, not a difference a trader sees.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's INS add page uses only GOV.UK Frontend components (trace-e2e-p9-068).

requirements.statement: The add-address round trip (both saves and cancel) is proven end to end from every role picker, not only the consignor's.
requirements.why: Today only the consignor picker's round trip is proven, only on the compose stack, and no fit spec covers it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the handshake specs drive only the consignor picker (repo-tests-p5-033, trace-e2e-p9-077) and only on compose (repo-tests-p5-032).

requirements.statement: A picked or added address is copied onto the notification, not linked: renaming, moving or deleting the address book record later leaves the draft's copy as it was, with no error, and the picker then neither preselects nor offers a deleted record.
requirements.why: A notification must hold the address it was made with; Design Release 2.1 also stores a copy on the section.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (repo-tests-p5-037, repo-tests-p5-042, repo-tests-p5-044, trace-e2e-p8-001, trace-e2e-p8-006).

requirements.statement: On the review page each consignment party and the contact address read back as the name followed by the address lines and country (GB shown as 'United Kingdom'), each on its own line, without the telephone number or email address.
requirements.why: The trader checks the copy the notification holds before submitting.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the review shows each copied address as a block, name in bold then each non-empty field on its own line, telephone and email included, under the 'Roles and addresses' and 'Contact address for this consignment' cards.

requirements.statement: Each role and the consignment contact has its own page for editing the copy the notification holds: place-of-origin/edit, consignors/edit, consignees/edit, importers/edit, destinations/edit and consignment/contact/edit, reached from the hub's and review page's 'Edit details' links.
requirements.why: The address book accepts records that break the notification's address rules, so a notification needs a way to correct its own copy without touching the book: a real validation and cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today (repo-frontend-p9-091, repo-tests-p5-053, trace-e2e-p8-031). Design Release 2.1 shows no such page in this area; it is kept because rule-breaking copies need it (req-694).

requirements.statement: The edit page is headed 'Edit address details', captioned with the role ('Consignor or exporter', 'Place of origin', 'Consignee', 'Importer', 'Place of destination' or 'Contact address for consignment'), titled 'Edit address details - Import notification service - GOV.UK', below the notification's journey strip.
requirements.why: Today's edit page copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today (repo-frontend-p9-092, trace-e2e-p8-032).

requirements.statement: The edit page explains 'Changes apply to this notification only. Your address book is not changed.'
requirements.why: The trader must know the edit does not reach the book.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today (repo-frontend-p9-093, trace-e2e-p8-033).

requirements.statement: The edit page asks for 'Name or organisation name', 'Address line 1', 'Address line 2 (optional)', 'Town or city', 'County (optional)', 'Postcode or Zip code' (width 10), 'Country' (a plain select, 'Select a country' then United Kingdom and 31 European countries by ISO code), 'Phone number' (hint 'For international numbers include the country code') and 'Email address'; only address line 2 and county are optional.
requirements.why: Today's edit page fields.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today (repo-frontend-p9-094 to repo-frontend-p9-103, trace-e2e-p8-035 to trace-e2e-p8-044).

requirements.statement: The edit page's buttons are 'Save changes' and a secondary 'Cancel'.
requirements.why: Today's edit page copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today (repo-frontend-p9-104, trace-e2e-p8-045).

requirements.statement: The edit page opens pre-filled with every field of the notification's copy, the country select set to its code; before any address is picked for the role it sends the trader to the role's picker and saves nothing.
requirements.why: There is nothing to edit until a copy exists.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today (repo-frontend-p9-122, repo-tests-p5-058, trace-e2e-p8-034).

requirements.statement: The edit page applies the address book's rules and messages: 'Enter a name', 'Enter address line 1', 'Enter a town or city', 'Enter a postcode', 'Enter a country' (blank or unlisted), 'Enter a telephone number', 'Enter an email address', plus the length and email-format checks.
requirements.why: The copy must meet the same rules the address book sets, so a corrected copy is valid.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today (repo-frontend-p9-105, repo-tests-p5-063, repo-tests-p5-066, trace-e2e-p8-048, trace-e2e-p8-051).

requirements.statement: A refused edit answers 400, re-renders 'Edit address details' with the error summary and an error on each field, keeps what was typed (the country select resets to 'Select a country' for an unlisted value) and saves nothing; browser validation is off.
requirements.why: A refused edit must leave the notification's copy as it was.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today (repo-frontend-p9-124, repo-tests-p5-068, trace-e2e-p8-047).

requirements.statement: A valid edit replaces only this notification's copy of the role: the address book record and any other notification holding a copy of it are unchanged, the picker no longer preselects the source record, and no banner is shown.
requirements.why: The copy belongs to the notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today (repo-frontend-p9-125, repo-frontend-p9-127, repo-tests-p5-061, repo-tests-p5-062, trace-e2e-p8-028).

requirements.statement: Save, Cancel and Back on the edit page return to where the edit was started, named by its return parameter from a closed list (the addresses hub, the review page or the contact picker), falling back to the role's own return page and keeping change context; Cancel discards what was typed.
requirements.why: The trader comes back to the page they left.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today (repo-frontend-p9-129, repo-tests-p5-070, repo-tests-p5-071, trace-e2e-p8-057, trace-e2e-p8-058).

requirements.statement: If saving an edit fails with a recoverable backend error, the edit page re-renders with status 500 and the recoverable-error message, and the held copy is unchanged.
requirements.why: A failed save must not lose or corrupt the copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today (repo-frontend-p9-130).

requirements.statement: The edit page has Welsh copy ('Golygu manylion cyfeiriad', 'Cadw’r newidiadau', 'Canslo'), marked as a machine draft not yet reviewed by a translator.
requirements.why: Today's Welsh copy, which needs Welsh Language Standards sign-off before it ships to users.
requirements.deltaNote: Present today (repo-frontend-p9-132).

requirements.statement: The edit page is built only from GOV.UK Frontend components and has no axe violations against WCAG 2.2 AA.
requirements.why: Accessibility.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (repo-frontend-p9-193, trace-animals-fit-p15-067).

requirements.statement: A copy is checked against the notification's address rules: the address book accepts a record the rules refuse (such as a country name instead of a listed code), the picker lets the trader pick it, and its edit form then opens with no country selected.
requirements.why: The address book only checks a country is present, so the notification must catch a copy that breaks its rules.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today (repo-frontend-p9-131, repo-tests-p5-045, trace-e2e-p8-013).

requirements.statement: The review keeps today's validation errors that Design Release 2.1 cannot show: an answered party whose copied address breaks the address-book rules is named in a 'There is a problem' error summary ('Correct the address details for the <role>', 'Correct the contact address details for this consignment') linked to that party's edit page with return=notification-view and repeated inside the role's row, a stored answer that is no longer valid is named on its card, these come before the unfinished-card entries, and either stops Continue.
requirements.why: The trader must see which copy to correct and get straight to it.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (repo-tests-p5-046, repo-tests-p5-050, trace-e2e-p8-015, trace-e2e-p8-016).

requirements.statement: While a copy breaks the rules, Continue on the review page is refused (400, same error summary) and a direct declaration submit is refused and sent back to the review page.
requirements.why: A notification with an invalid party address must not be submitted.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (repo-tests-p5-048, repo-tests-p5-049, trace-e2e-p8-021).

requirements.statement: Correcting the copy on its edit page and saving returns to the review page with the error gone, after which the trader can continue to the Declaration and submit to 'Import notification submitted'.
requirements.why: Correction must unblock submission.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (repo-tests-p5-051, repo-tests-p5-052, trace-e2e-p8-024).

requirements.statement: Once a notification is submitted its copied addresses are frozen: renaming, moving or deleting the address book record changes neither the submitted view (status 'Submitted', no Change or Edit details links) nor an amendment, neither shows an error, and cancelling the amendment restores the submitted copy.
requirements.why: A submitted notification is a record of what was declared.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (repo-tests-p5-082, repo-tests-p5-085, trace-e2e-p8-081, trace-e2e-p8-084).

requirements.statement: The CPH number question applies to every live-animal commodity except horses (0101), cats, dogs, ferrets and other live mammals (01061900), 05111000 and 05119985: cattle, pigs, sheep, goats, poultry, rabbits, camels, ostriches, parrots, reptiles, bees and fish all get it. Where it does not apply, the CPH page cannot be opened and sends the user to the consignment addresses page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks for a CPH number for every species kept on a holding, not only the few on today's list, and keeps the page out of reach for consignments that have no holding.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the CPH question applies only when a commodity line's commodity is on the frontend's CPH commodity list (repo-frontend-p10-003): cattle bring it in and cats leave it out (trace-e2e-p6-068, trace-e2e-p6-070), but nothing shows pigs, sheep, goats, poultry and the rest on it, and no source shows what the page does when opened for a consignment it does not apply to.

requirements.statement: On the consignment addresses page the CPH section is headed 'County parish holding (CPH) number', described 'The county parish holding (CPH) number identifies the holding where the animals will be kept.', sits after the place of destination, and before a number is saved offers the link 'Add a CPH number'.
requirements.why: The link text is Design Release 2.1's; today's bare 'Add' action reads as nothing on its own.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the heading, description and position already match (trace-e2e-p6-071, trace-e2e-p6-072); the empty row's action is an 'Add' link with the hidden suffix ' county parish holding (cph) number' (trace-e2e-p6-073) instead of the link text 'Add a CPH number'.

requirements.statement: A saved CPH number is shown on the consignment addresses page and on the review page as county/parish/holding with slashes, such as '12/345/6789', with a 'Change' link back to the CPH page.
requirements.why: The slashed form is how traders read and check a CPH number, and it is how Design Release 2.1 shows it everywhere.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the addresses page shows the saved number as nine bare digits, '123456789' (trace-e2e-p6-075); the Change link already exists (trace-e2e-p6-076).

requirements.statement: A valid CPH number is stored as nine bare digits, the three parts joined with no separators, and is split back 2/3/4 into its boxes when the page is shown again.
requirements.why: The stored shape is a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express: today's record, and every stored notification, holds nine digits, so only the display gains slashes.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-038 and trace-animals-fit-p13-025: the frontend joins the parts and stores 123456789.

requirements.statement: The CPH page has the caption 'Consignment parties', the single h1 'Add the county parish holding number (CPH)', and the browser title 'Add the county parish holding number (CPH) - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on the page's identity.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p13-002, trace-animals-fit-p13-003 and trace-animals-fit-p13-004 show the same heading, caption and title today.

requirements.statement: The CPH, permanent address and contact address pages show the notification's 'Draft' tag and reference above the content.
requirements.why: The trader always sees which notification they are changing.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p13-023 and trace-e2e-p7-008: the journey strip with the Draft tag and reference is on the CPH and contact pages today; the permanent address page gets it when it is built.

requirements.statement: A collapsed 'What is a CPH number?' details component sits above the CPH inputs and, when opened, says 'A county parish holding (CPH) number is a unique 9-digit number used to identify land and buildings where livestock are kept, moved or handled.'
requirements.why: Traders who do not know their CPH number need to know what it is before they look for it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-007, repo-frontend-p10-008 and trace-animals-fit-p13-017 show the same summary and definition today.

requirements.statement: The CPH help's second paragraph reads 'You can find your CPH number on documents from the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA) or by checking your holding details on GOV.UK.', in English and Welsh, with 'checking your holding details on GOV.UK' as a link to the GOV.UK 'Get a county parish holding (CPH) number' guidance (https://www.gov.uk/guidance/get-a-county-parish-holding-cph-number).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 adds a second place to find the number and the prototype wins; its href is only a placeholder, so the link opens the GOV.UK page its text names (c-117).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the paragraph ends after '(APHA).' with no GOV.UK clause or link (repo-frontend-p10-009, trace-animals-fit-p13-018).

requirements.statement: The CPH number is asked as one fieldset with the small legend 'CPH number', not as a heading.
requirements.why: One question, one legend, so the page keeps a single h1.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-011 and trace-animals-fit-p13-006: a role=group fieldset with the small legend 'CPH number' today.

requirements.statement: The CPH question's hint reads 'For example 12/345/6789', with no comma and no full stop, and describes the whole group.
requirements.why: This is Design Release 2.1's wording of the hint.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the hint reads 'For example, 12/345/6789.', with a comma and a full stop (repo-frontend-p10-012, trace-animals-fit-p13-007); it already describes the group and never shows 123/456/789.

requirements.statement: The CPH number is entered in three boxes in one row, laid out with the GOV.UK date-input pattern, with visible labels 'County' (2 wide, at most 2 characters), 'Parish' (3 wide, at most 3) and 'Holding number' (4 wide, at most 4), each asking for a numeric keypad.
requirements.why: A CPH number is three parts of 2, 3 and 4 digits; boxes sized to the parts make each part easy to enter and check.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-014 to repo-frontend-p10-020 and trace-animals-fit-p13-010 to trace-animals-fit-p13-015: the same three labelled, sized boxes in the date-input layout today.

requirements.statement: Each CPH box has autocomplete turned off and the pattern [0-9]* as well as the numeric input mode.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sets both so browsers do not offer unrelated saved values and phones show the digit keypad.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each box has inputmode numeric and spellcheck off, but no autocomplete=off and no pattern (repo-frontend-p10-017, trace-animals-fit-p13-014).

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, each CPH box drops any non-digit as the trader types and stops at its maximum length.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps stray characters out of the boxes as they are typed; the server checks stay as the backstop. The digit filtering is built, but not the automatic focus moves the same prototype script makes (c-006).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the boxes are plain text inputs with no script (trace-animals-fit-p13-014 shows the attributes only), and non-digits are caught only on save.

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, pasting into a CPH box keeps only the digits and spreads them across that box and the ones after it (2, 3 then 4 digits), so pasting 123456789 or 12/345/6789 into County fills all three boxes.
requirements.why: Traders often copy the whole number from an APHA document; Design Release 2.1 lets one paste fill the three parts.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a whole slashed number pasted into County stays there and is rejected on save with 'County must be 2 digits' and the missing-part errors (repo-frontend-p10-033); without JavaScript that stays the case.

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, focus moves to the next CPH box once a box is full, and Backspace in an empty box moves focus back to the previous box and deletes its last digit.
requirements.why: Moving focus while the trader types is a change of context that accessibility guidance warns against, and the accessibility duty overrides Design Release 2.1 here: the CPH boxes keep the digit filtering and paste spreading but not the automatic focus moves (c-006).
requirements.deltaNote: Today nothing moves focus between the boxes.

requirements.statement: Saving the CPH page with all three boxes empty raises no error: it saves no CPH number (clearing any saved before), the trader moves on, and the CPH section stays incomplete, so the notification cannot be submitted until a number is added.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader move on and holds the gap at submission instead; required-to-proceed is a design choice the prototype can express, not a constraint it cannot.
requirements.deltaNote: Today an empty submit is refused with 400 and the single error 'Enter a CPH number' linked to the County box.

requirements.statement: A partly filled or wrongly formed CPH number is refused with one error per wrong part, in county, parish, holding order: 'Enter the county', 'Enter the parish' or 'Enter the holding number' for a missing part; 'County must be 2 digits', 'Parish must be 3 digits' or 'Holding number must be 4 digits' for a wrong length; 'County must only contain numbers', 'Parish must only contain numbers' or 'Holding number must only contain numbers' for a non-digit. Parts are trimmed first, and a whole slashed number typed into one box is refused.
requirements.why: Validation is a real constraint the prototype cannot express: Design Release 2.1 silently drops a part-entered number, which loses what the trader typed.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-023 to repo-frontend-p10-033 and trace-animals-fit-p13-035 to trace-animals-fit-p13-041: these per-part messages are the frontend's today.

requirements.statement: CPH errors re-render the page with status 400 and every typed value kept: an error summary titled 'There is a problem' links each error to its box and moves focus there, one inline message on the whole question lists every error (with a hidden 'Error:' prefix, between the hint and the boxes), each wrong box gets the error border, and the group's description includes the error.
requirements.why: A three-part question needs one message on the question and a border on each wrong part, so the trader sees which part to fix.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-034 to repo-frontend-p10-037 and trace-animals-fit-p13-042: the error presentation is the frontend's today.

requirements.statement: A stored CPH number that is not nine digits is flagged on the page with 'The saved CPH number is no longer valid. Re-enter the county, parish and holding numbers.', linked to the County box, with all three boxes shown empty.
requirements.why: Stored data can predate today's rules; the trader is told to re-enter it rather than shown stray digits.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-041 and repo-frontend-p10-042.

requirements.statement: The CPH page opens with three empty boxes when nothing is saved, and with the saved parts filled back in (County 12, Parish 345, Holding number 6789) when a number is saved, however the page is reached.
requirements.why: The trader can check and change what they entered.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-039, repo-frontend-p10-040 and trace-e2e-p6-077.

requirements.statement: The CPH page's back link always goes to the consignment addresses page.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 the CPH page is a step of the consignment addresses section, opened from it and returning to it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the back link goes to the addresses page only when reached with return=addresses (repo-frontend-p10-043, trace-e2e-p6-078); reached any other way it goes to the notification overview.

requirements.statement: 'Save and continue' on the CPH page always returns to the consignment addresses page, never on to the contact address page or the notification overview.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 returns every consignment-addresses step to the addresses page, from where 'Save and continue' moves on.
requirements.deltaNote: Today saving returns to the addresses page only when reached with return=addresses (trace-e2e-p6-074); in the opening run it continues to the contact page, and otherwise it goes to the notification overview.

requirements.statement: The CPH page ends with the primary 'Save and continue' button alone, with no return-to-hub button and no cancel link.
requirements.why: DR1's inc-161 judgement (rule b): only pages the task-list overview links to end with the three return controls, and the CPH page is reached from the consignment addresses page.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-047, trace-animals-fit-p13-020 and trace-e2e-p6-089: the CPH page ends with 'Save and continue' alone today.

requirements.statement: 'Save and continue' on the consignment addresses page goes on to the contact address page, whether or not the CPH number applies; the CPH page is reached only from its own link on the addresses page.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 the contact address follows the consignment addresses, and the CPH number is one of the addresses page's sections, not a step after it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the addresses page's 'Save and continue' goes to the CPH page when a CPH-triggering line exists, and otherwise to the notification overview.

requirements.statement: The CPH and contact address forms post back to their own URL with a CSRF crumb and the notification's concurrency token, and a failed save re-renders the page with status 500, the recoverable-error banner and the trader's values kept.
requirements.why: Real persistence and concurrency constraints the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p13-024, repo-frontend-p10-048 and repo-frontend-p10-078.

requirements.statement: The CPH, permanent address and contact address pages have no serious or critical WCAG 2 A/AA axe violations, clean and in their error states, and each radio group's description names its hint and, on error, its error.
requirements.why: The service must be accessible; the prototype does not test this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-049 and repo-frontend-p10-082 for the CPH and contact pages today; the permanent address page needs the same check when it is built.

requirements.statement: Every English string changed or added on the CPH, permanent address and contact address pages gets a Welsh version in the same change, marked as a machine draft that must not ship without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
requirements.why: Both pages already carry a Welsh version of every string, so a changed English string without its Welsh would leave the Welsh page wrong.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the CPH and contact pages have machine-draft Welsh for today's strings (repo-frontend-p10-051, repo-frontend-p10-084); the new and changed strings have none yet.

requirements.statement: Cats, dogs and ferrets need a permanent address; 'Other live mammals', which shares their commodity code 01061900, does not.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks for a permanent address only for pets that APHA must be able to check.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the frontend asks for a permanent address for cats and dogs only (trace-e2e-p6-028; DR1 inc-057 records the same); ferrets are not in today's commodity catalogue.

requirements.statement: The permanent address is its own page in the consignment parties section, opened from the consignment addresses page: caption 'Consignment parties', heading 'Permanent address', browser title 'Permanent address - Import notification service - GOV.UK', and a back link to the consignment addresses page. It applies only when the consignment holds commodity 01061900 with at least one species that needs a permanent address; otherwise the page cannot be opened and sends the user to the consignment addresses page. The address fields leave the animal identification form.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 (and DR1 before it) asks for the permanent address as its own step, so a trader can answer it, leave it and come back, instead of reopening animal identification.
requirements.deltaNote: Today there is no permanent address page: the address fields sit inside the animal identification form after the identifier fields (trace-e2e-p6-028, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-058).

requirements.statement: When the permanent address applies, the consignment addresses page has a 'Permanent address' section explaining 'A permanent address is where an animal:' with the bullets 'will permanently reside' and 'can be checked by the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA)', and the link 'Add a permanent address' to the permanent address page; for cats it has no CPH section.
requirements.why: The section is how the trader reaches the permanent address step in Design Release 2.1.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the addresses page has no permanent address section (trace-e2e-p6-068 lists its rows for cats).

requirements.statement: Once permanent addresses are saved, the consignment addresses page shows the one address with a 'Change' link when every animal is 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' or only one animal has an address; otherwise it shows 'Permanent addresses added for N animals', where N is the number of animals that need one, with a 'Change' link. The Change link goes straight to the permanent address page.
requirements.why: The trader sees at a glance what was given for the section, without one row per animal.

requirements.statement: The permanent address shows the GOV.UK warning 'Providing a false address is an act of fraud', with no full stop.
requirements.why: Traders must know a false address is fraud before they give one.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p6-029: the identification form's permanent address block shows the same warning, with no full stop, today; it moves with the fields to the new page.

requirements.statement: The permanent address explains 'A permanent address is where an animal:' followed by the bullets 'will permanently reside' and 'can be checked by the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA)', then asks 'Where will their permanent address be?'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on the explanation and the question.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p6-030 and trace-e2e-p6-031: the same copy on the identification form today (the question an h3 there, an h2 on the new page).

requirements.statement: The permanent address page shows one card for each animal that needs a permanent address, as many as the number of animals entered for that species, each headed with the species' scientific name and a running number, such as 'Felis catus 1'; species that do not need one get no cards.
requirements.why: Each animal can live at a different address, and the page asks for all of them in one place.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the address is asked once per animal record inside the identification form, which opens one animal at a time ('Enter details for Felis catus 2 of 2', trace-e2e-p6-044).

requirements.statement: Each animal card shows, in inset text, the identifiers already entered for that animal as 'label: value' (such as 'Microchip: MICROCHIP-1'), leaving out blank ones, and no inset when none are entered.
requirements.why: The trader can tell which animal each card is for.

requirements.statement: Each animal card has a radio group with the legend 'Select an address' and two options, 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' and 'Enter a new address', with neither chosen when the page first opens.
requirements.why: Most pets live at the place of destination; reusing it saves the trader typing the same address again.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the address fields are always shown, with no choice to reuse an address already given (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-004).

requirements.statement: Once a place of destination is given, the 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' option shows that address on one line as its hint, such as 'Riverside Holding Facility, East Farm Road, Leeds, LS25 3EB, United Kingdom'.
requirements.why: The trader sees which address they are reusing.

requirements.statement: The 'Enter a new address' option has the hint 'This is where they will stay after spending 48 hours at the place of destination.'
requirements.why: It tells the trader what the permanent address means for a pet that moves on from the place of destination.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the frontend carries the 48-hour hint nowhere (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-006-m1).

requirements.statement: Choosing 'Enter a new address' reveals that animal's own address fields inside its card, as a GOV.UK conditional reveal.
requirements.why: The fields are only needed when the place of destination is not reused.

requirements.statement: A new permanent address asks for 'Name or organisation name', 'Address line 1', 'Address line 2 (optional)', 'Town or city', 'County (optional)', 'Postcode or Zip code', 'Email address' and 'Phone number' (hint 'For international numbers include the country code'), and has no country field.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today ask for the same fields.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p6-032 to trace-e2e-p6-035: the identification form asks for the same eight fields with the same labels and phone hint, and no country, today.

requirements.statement: In a new permanent address, 'Email address' comes before 'Phone number'.
requirements.why: This is Design Release 2.1's field order.
requirements.deltaNote: Today 'Phone number' comes before 'Email address' (trace-e2e-p6-032).

requirements.statement: When 'Enter a new address' is chosen for an animal, its name, address line 1, town or city, postcode, email address and phone number are required, showing 'Enter a name or organisation name', 'Enter address line 1', 'Enter a town or city', 'Enter a postcode or Zip code', 'Enter an email address' and 'Enter a phone number' on the blank fields; address line 2 and county are optional; and email, phone and postcode are only checked for being blank.
requirements.why: The choice decides whether an address is needed, so the fields are required exactly when the trader says they will enter one.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the same field messages exist, but they fire whenever any part of the address is given, with no choice behind them (trace-e2e-p6-036 to trace-e2e-p6-042); no source shows today's message for a blank name.

requirements.statement: On the permanent address page, each address error in the error summary names its animal, such as 'Enter a name or organisation name for Felis catus 1' and 'Enter address line 1 for Felis catus 1', and links to the field; the inline message on the field leaves the animal out.
requirements.why: With several animals' forms on one page, the summary must say which animal each error is about.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the error summary repeats the field message without naming the animal ('Enter address line 1', trace-e2e-p6-037), since one animal's form is shown at a time.

requirements.statement: Choosing 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' for an animal before a place of destination is given shows 'Add a place of destination before you can continue' on that animal's radios and in an error summary titled 'There is a problem', linked to the radios.
requirements.why: There is nothing to reuse until the place of destination exists.

requirements.statement: An animal left with no option chosen raises no error: the page saves the other animals and moves on, and the permanent address section stays incomplete until every animal that needs one has an address with a name.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader save what they know and come back; completeness is checked at the section and at submission.

requirements.statement: When the permanent address page shows errors, each animal's chosen option stays selected and a chosen 'Enter a new address' keeps its fields open with what was typed; when the page is opened again, each animal's saved choice is selected and its saved address filled back in.
requirements.why: The trader never has to re-enter what they already gave.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the identification form keeps typed values on a failed add (trace-e2e-p6-043); the new page needs the same per animal.

requirements.statement: When no animals that need a permanent address have been counted, the permanent address page shows 'Add the number of animals on consignment details before you can continue.', with 'consignment details' linking to that page, instead of the animal cards; saving from that state saves nothing and returns to the consignment addresses page.
requirements.why: The cards depend on the number of animals, which is given on the consignment details page.

requirements.statement: Saving 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' for an animal copies the place of destination's name, address lines, country, email, phone and address-book id into that animal's permanent address; saving 'Enter a new address' stores the animal's own name, address lines, town or city, county, postcode, country United Kingdom, email and phone.
requirements.why: Each animal's permanent address must be stored with the notification, whichever way it was given.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each animal record stores the address typed on the identification form; nothing copies the place of destination.

requirements.statement: A new permanent address keeps every field in its own place: the county is saved, and a saved address with no address line 2 opens with the town in 'Town or city' and the postcode in 'Postcode or Zip code'.
requirements.why: Persistence is a real constraint the prototype cannot express: Design Release 2.1 loses the county and shifts fields on return, which the real service must not copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's identification form stores each field by name (trace-e2e-p6-032); the new page must keep that.

requirements.statement: The permanent address page ends with the primary 'Save and continue' button alone, which saves and returns to the consignment addresses page.
requirements.why: DR1's inc-161 judgement (rule b): a page reached from another page, not from the task-list overview, ends with the primary button alone, like the CPH page and the party pickers.

requirements.statement: The review page shows the permanent address as one row per animal, labelled with the species' common name and number (such as 'Domestic dog 1'), whose value is that animal's saved address; with no animals counted it shows a single row 'Address'.
requirements.why: The trader checks each animal's permanent address before submitting.
requirements.deltaNote: No today source shows the permanent address on the review page.

requirements.statement: The prototype's own permanent-address routing is not reproduced: /permanent-address resetting the answer and redirecting to /permanent-address/select, the unused 'Are all the animals going to the place of destination?' page, and the retired /permanent-address/enter-address redirect.
requirements.why: These are prototype internals with no behaviour a trader sees beyond landing on the per-animal page; the real service has none of these routes to retire.

requirements.statement: The prototype's custom heading, card and layout classes on the contact and permanent address pages, and its /design-release-2.1 mount paths, are not reproduced.
requirements.why: They are how the prototype is built, not behaviour a trader sees; the real pages use GOV.UK Frontend components.

requirements.statement: The contact address page has the h1 'Contact address for consignment', no section caption, and the browser title 'Contact address for consignment - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on the page's identity.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-058 and trace-animals-fit-p12-041: the same heading and title, with no caption, today (as the radios legend).

requirements.statement: Directly under the contact page's heading, body text reads 'This is the contact address of the person responsible for the consignment from when it enters Great Britain until authorities complete their checks.', replacing the hint 'Selecting a contact copies their name and address into this notification.'
requirements.why: It tells the trader whose address this is; DR1 inc-046 judged the copy sentence loses nothing the trader can act on.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page carries only the fieldset hint 'Selecting a contact copies their name and address into this notification.' (trace-e2e-p7-006, trace-animals-fit-p12-042).

requirements.statement: Below the intro, the contact page has the sub-heading 'Select an address' (an h2), and the radios' fieldset legend 'Select an address' is visually hidden, so the h1 is no longer the radios legend.
requirements.why: This is Design Release 2.1's page structure: a heading for the page and a heading for the choice.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the radios legend is the page's h1 and there is no 'Select an address' heading (repo-frontend-p10-058).

requirements.statement: Under 'Select an address', the contact page says 'If the correct address is not shown, add a new branch address, then return to this page.', with 'add a new branch address' as the link to add an address, replacing today's 'Add a new address' link above the heading.
requirements.why: The contact must be one of the trader's own branches, so the page tells them how to add a missing branch.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a paragraph link 'Add a new address' sits above the heading, before the fieldset (trace-e2e-p7-031, trace-e2e-p8-075).

requirements.statement: The contact page's add link opens the address book's add-address page set to add a branch address, and the address book returns the trader to the contact page when the address is saved.
requirements.why: The new address must be a branch address to appear in the contact list, and the copy promises a return to this page.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the link goes to the INS address book's add page through the handshake (journey-type gbn-ag, notification-id, fulfilment-id, handshake-token) with no address type and no return path of its own (trace-e2e-p7-032, trace-e2e-p7-080).

requirements.statement: Back on the contact page after adding a branch address, the new address is in the list, selected as the contact address, and the page shows the success banner '<name> address added to your address book' once.
requirements.why: The trader added the address to use it here, so it is chosen for them and they are told it was saved.
requirements.deltaNote: No today source shows the contact page after the add handshake returns successfully.

requirements.statement: Coming back from the address book add with a not-found error, the contact page shows 'The address could not be found in your address book. Select another address or try adding it again.' in the error summary; with an unavailable error it shows 'The address book could not be reached. Your answers on this page have been saved. Try again in a few minutes.' and the recoverable-error state.
requirements.why: The round trip to the address book crosses services and can fail; the prototype cannot express that.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-069 and repo-frontend-p10-070.

requirements.statement: When the animals frontend runs in stub mode, the contact page offers no link to add an address.
requirements.why: Stub mode has no address book to add to.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-068 and trace-animals-fit-p12-048.

requirements.statement: The contact page offers only the signed-in organisation's own branch addresses, newest added first, not every record in its address book.
requirements.why: The contact is the trader's own branch responsible for the consignment in Great Britain; offering overseas consignors and other parties is a live defect DR1 recorded.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page lists every record in the organisation's address book, overseas ones included (13 in the fit stub, 28 end to end), newest first (trace-e2e-p7-014).

requirements.statement: Each contact address radio is labelled with the address's name and has its address lines, joined with commas, as its hint, without the country, such as '15 Union Street, Aberdeen, AB11 5BN'.
requirements.why: This is Design Release 2.1's hint; branch addresses are all in Great Britain, so the country adds nothing.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the hint ends with the country, joined with commas (repo-frontend-p10-062, trace-e2e-p7-011); the label is already the name (trace-e2e-p7-010).

requirements.statement: The contact addresses are one list of radios whose value is the address record's id, with no search box, no pagination and no manual entry of its own.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree: new contacts come only through the address book.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p7-012 and trace-e2e-p7-013: one unpaginated radio list keyed by record id today.

requirements.statement: No contact address is chosen when the page first opens; on return, the saved contact's radio is selected while it still matches a record in the list.
requirements.why: The trader makes the choice, and sees it again when they come back.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p7-017 and trace-e2e-p7-029.

requirements.statement: 'Save and continue' on the contact page with no address chosen shows 'Select a contact address' in the error summary and on the radios, linked to the first radio, and saves nothing.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 requires the contact address before the trader moves on to review.
requirements.deltaNote: Today saving with nothing chosen is allowed, shows no error and exits to the overview with the task still 'To do'.

requirements.statement: Submitting a contact id that is not in the list shows 'Select a contact address' in the error summary and on the radios, answers 400, selects no radio and saves nothing; the error link focuses the first radio.
requirements.why: A forged or stale choice must not be saved.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-071 and trace-animals-fit-p12-051 to trace-animals-fit-p12-053.

requirements.statement: Choosing a contact address and pressing 'Save and continue' saves it and goes to the review page ('Review your notification').
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 the contact address is the last step before review.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a saved contact redirects to the notification's overview, not the review page.

requirements.statement: The contact page's back link goes to the consignment addresses page, or to the review page when the page was opened from review.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 the contact page follows the consignment addresses page.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the back link goes to the notification overview.

requirements.statement: Choosing a contact saves a copy of that address's name and address into the notification, remembering which record it came from; the held copy stays valid, and the task complete, even if the address-book record later changes or is deleted.
requirements.why: Copy semantics is a real persistence and cross-service constraint: the address book is another service, and a submitted notification must keep the address it was submitted with.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-074 and repo-frontend-p10-075: a copy with pickedFromId, never flagged invalid on return, today.

requirements.statement: The contact page shows the radios list alone, with the current contact pre-selected, and no 'Current contact address' summary card or 'Edit details' link.

requirements.deltaNote: Today, once a contact is held, the page shows a 'Current contact address' card with an 'Edit details' link below the radios (trace-e2e-p7-026).

requirements.statement: There is no 'Edit details' route to /consignment/contact/edit: the notification still stores the chosen contact as a copy taken from the chosen address-book record, and the review's contact row shows it.

requirements.statement: The animals and packages totals add up only counts that are positive whole numbers, and a card reads '0' when its total is not above zero: commodity details refuses any number of animals or packages that is zero, negative or not a whole number, so only blank or positive counts reach the totals, and a blank count adds nothing.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 counts only positive entries, so a card never shows a negative or odd total.
requirements.deltaNote: Already met: commodity details refuses a number of animals below 1 or not whole and a number of packages that is not a whole number of 1 or more (repo-frontend-p5-067, repo-frontend-p5-068, proved by trace-animals-fit-p9-050 and trace-animals-fit-p9-052), and templates are seeded from the same checked answers, so no zero, negative or non-numeric count can reach the hub. Blank counts add nothing (repo-frontend-p4-010), lines are summed (repo-frontend-p4-009) and both totals read 0 before any line exists (repo-frontend-p4-011, trace-animals-fit-p4-067). Today's arithmetic would subtract a negative count, but no path can save one, so nothing changes.

requirements.statement: The plants section's heading reads 'Plants, plant products or' with a line break before 'other objects', and the section carries its plants style modifier.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows plants as the third category on the home with its own styling.

requirements.statement: The plants section's 'View dashboard' link goes to the real high-risk plants dashboard on the plants frontend (its /high-risk-plants set base).
requirements.why: The prototype's '#' is a placeholder; the real plants dashboard exists on its own origin, and a cross-service constraint overrides the prototype under the ruling.
requirements.deltaNote: The target exists (trace-e2e-p15-117); the INS front door has no link to the plants frontend today (repo-insfrontend-p1-051).

requirements.statement: The plants section shows three glance cards linking like the live-animals and germinal-products ones: 'Action needed' ('View tasks', to /actions?category=plants), 'Status updates' ('View updates', to /changes?category=plants) and 'Inspection required' reading 'Consignments due at the BCP' ('View requirements', to the Inspection required drill-down at /inspection). The cards and their counts are built with the plants section once plants notifications reach the INS read model.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's '#' plants links are placeholders for a cross-service flow the prototype cannot express, so the real service follows the pattern Design Release 2.1 sets for every real section; what remains waits on the plants services, not on a design choice (c-152).
requirements.blockedBy: The plants services (trade-imports-plants-frontend and trade-imports-plants-backend, outside this programme's repos) must publish their notifications to the INS read model in trade-imports-ins-backend before the plants glance cards can count or list anything.

requirements.statement: The Action needed drill-down is served by the INS front door at /actions with the browser title 'Tasks requiring your attention - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 opens the Action needed list from the home's glance cards.

requirements.statement: The Action needed drill-down shows the caption 'Action needed'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the glance card the page came from in its caption.

requirements.statement: The Action needed drill-down's h1 reads 'Tasks requiring your attention'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's heading for the page.

requirements.statement: The Action needed drill-down's description reads 'Add missing information or upload documents to prevent your consignment from being delayed.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 tells the trader what to do about the listed notifications.

requirements.statement: The Action needed and Status updated drill-downs' 'Back' link goes to the category's notification list when ?category= names one (for live-animals, the /live-animals list in the INS frontend) and to the home when there is no category; an unrecognised category lists every category.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 returns the trader to wherever the glance card was.

requirements.statement: The Action needed drill-down lists only notifications needing action, across every category with no ?category= and only that category's with one. A submitted notification needs action when it is still missing a required document (no ITAHC or health certificate attached) or its required animal identifiers are incomplete; this is worked out in the animals backend from the notification's own record and carried into the INS read model. Authority-flagged actions are not part of it until an outcome feed from the authorities exists.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's list is the set the Action needed card counts, filtered to the card's category, and Design Release 2.1 itself works the status out from the notification's own outstanding items; the cross-service constraint decides only where it is worked out (c-149).

requirements.statement: The Action needed list sits under a visually hidden h2 'Notifications needing action'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives screen-reader users a heading for the list.

requirements.statement: The Action needed and Inspection required drill-downs have a GET search form to their own page with a 'Search by' field and the hint 'Keyword, notification number, commodity, consignee or consignor', keeping the page (when above 1) as a hidden field, and on Action needed the category as a hidden field so a search stays in that category.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader search within a drill-down without losing its category.

requirements.statement: A drill-down search matches the text against each notification's number, commodity, consignee and consignor and lists only the matches, ignoring surrounding spaces and treating a blank search as none.
requirements.why: The prototype's search box does nothing, which a real service cannot ship; the ruling lets the real constraint override, and the hint says what a search covers. The read model needs the consignee and consignor to search them.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's INS search matches only a whole reference number (repo-insfrontend-p1-015) and the read model carries no consignee or consignor (repo-tests-p4-081).

requirements.statement: The Action needed and Inspection required drill-downs have a 'Sort by:' select offering 'Newest first', 'Oldest first' and 'Arrival date', always applied, with 'Newest first' selected by default and no 'Select one' unsorted option.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers these sort orders; DR1 ruled the dashboard stays always sorted with no unsorted state, and a real sort must be applied, not only preselected.

requirements.statement: The Action needed drill-down has no Additional filters, no tabs and no delay filter (Today, Next 3 days, Already delayed), and ignores ?delayFilter=.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 drops the delay filter that Design Release 2 had.

requirements.statement: The Action needed and Inspection required drill-downs show a results line 'Show <first>-<last> of <total> results' above the list, or 'Show 0 of 0 results' when there are none.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's results wording on the drill-downs.

requirements.statement: The Action needed drill-down pages its list 8 notifications at a time, its page links keeping the sort and the category.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's page size for the drill-downs; the INS front door must ask the read model for that size, which today it leaves to ins-backend.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the INS front door sends no page size and uses ins-backend's 25 (repo-insfrontend-p1-057).

requirements.statement: Each notification on a drill-down is shown with the same notification card as the category dashboard, carrying its status tag and any error message (such as 'ITAHC is missing'), and keeping the card's status-driven links rather than a fixed 'Copy as new' and 'View'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lists drill-down notifications as dashboard cards; DR1 already ruled that the dashboard card keeps its status-driven links.

requirements.statement: The Status updated drill-down is served by the INS front door at /changes with the browser title 'Changes in past 24 hours - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 opens the Status updated list from the home's glance cards.

requirements.statement: The Status updated drill-down shows the caption 'Status updated'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's caption for the page.

requirements.statement: The Status updated drill-down's h1 reads 'Changes in past 24 hours'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's heading for the page.

requirements.statement: The Status updated drill-down's description reads 'Notifications that have progressed, or been validated, rejected, cancelled, or replaced in the past 24 hours.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 tells the trader what counts as a change.

requirements.statement: The Status updated drill-down groups the category's notifications whose status changed in the past 24 hours under h2 sections in the order 'Passed inspection', 'Needs inspection', 'Delayed', leaving out any section with none.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 groups recent changes by kind; the outcomes they rest on come from the authorities' systems.
requirements.blockedBy: The authorities' import-checking systems, outside this programme, must send inspection and delay outcomes (passed inspection, needs inspection, delayed) for each notification to the services; no service in the workspace receives them today and the INS read model holds no such state (DR1 inc-014).

requirements.statement: The Status updated drill-down has no search, sort, results count or pagination.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the recent changes as grouped sections only.

requirements.statement: Sections for the other changes the Status updated description names (validated, rejected, cancelled, replaced) are not built.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 never renders them, so their headings and order are not designed; only the three sections it shows are built.

requirements.statement: The Inspection required drill-down is served by the INS front door at /inspection with the browser title 'Consignments due at the border control post (BCP) - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 has an Inspection required list of consignments due at the BCP.

requirements.statement: The Inspection required drill-down shows the caption 'Inspection required'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's caption for the page.

requirements.statement: The Inspection required drill-down's h1 reads 'Consignments due at the border control post (BCP)'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's heading for the page.

requirements.statement: The Inspection required drill-down's description reads 'Consignments that must go to your chosen BCP for inspection.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 tells the trader what the listed consignments need.

requirements.statement: The Inspection required drill-down has a GOV.UK details component 'What to do at a border inspection', closed until opened, reading 'If your consignments need to have sanitary or phytosanitary checks, you or the transporter must take it to your chosen border control post (BCP).'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives traders the inspection guidance on demand.

requirements.statement: The border inspection details end with 'Read the guidance on what you need to do at a border inspection', linking to https://www.gov.uk/guidance/sanitary-and-phytosanitary-sps-checks-at-border-control-posts-bcps in a new tab (rel noreferrer noopener), with no '(opens in new tab)' text.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 points traders to the GOV.UK SPS checks guidance.

requirements.statement: The Inspection required drill-down's 'Back' link always goes to the home, whatever the category.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 returns from this page to the overall home.

requirements.statement: The Inspection required drill-down lists the signed-in organisation's notifications chosen for inspection across every category, with no category filter, including ones whose status has moved on (such as Completed).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lists every consignment due at the BCP in one place; whether a notification is chosen for inspection is an outcome the authorities set.
requirements.blockedBy: The authorities' import-checking systems, outside this programme, must send which notifications are chosen for inspection to the services; no service in the workspace receives that today and the INS read model holds no such state (DR1 inc-014).

requirements.statement: The Inspection required list sits under a visually hidden h2 'Notifications chosen for inspection'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives screen-reader users a heading for the list.

requirements.statement: The Inspection required drill-down pages its list 8 notifications at a time, its page links keeping only the sort.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's page size for the drill-downs.

requirements.statement: The drill-down pages hold only their intro and their notifications: no 'Create new' or 'Use template' button and no glance cards.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps those actions on the home.

requirements.statement: The drill-down intros use Design Release 2.1's intro block: a caption paragraph, an h1 and a description in its own styling rather than govuk-caption and govuk-heading classes.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's styling for the drill-down intros; the prototype wins over today's components-only convention.

requirements.statement: /dashboard with no query redirects to the home; /dashboard with a query redirects to the live animals notification list at /live-animals in the INS frontend, keeping the query (for example ?tab=drafts).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps the old dashboard address working, sending queries meant for the live-animals list there.

requirements.statement: The prototype index page listing design releases ('Choose a prototype version to work on...', 'Start design release 2.1') is not built.
requirements.why: It is the prototype kit's own version picker, not part of the service; the goal brings the real services up to one release.

requirements.statement: The prototype's fixed glance counts and seeded demonstration notifications (such as GBN-AG-26-7K8M2W and GBN-GP-26-7K8M2T) are not reproduced.
requirements.why: They are prototype data, not behaviour: the real home and drill-downs show the organisation's real notifications.

requirements.statement: The home's counts and every drill-down list count and show only the signed-in organisation's notifications.
