requirements.why: Who may see which notifications is an authorisation constraint the prototype cannot express; today the INS list is not scoped at all, and the read model carries no organisation to scope by.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the INS request for notifications carries no organisation or user (repo-insfrontend-p1-068) and a fresh organisation sees the same notifications as another (trace-ins-fit-p4-046).

requirements.statement: Signing in to the INS front door lands the trader on the home, which only a signed-in trader can open.
requirements.why: The home is the signed-in landing page in Design Release 2.1 and today.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-ins-fit-p4-001: sign-in redirects straight to the service root.

requirements.statement: The home's counts and the drill-downs read from the INS aggregated read model, which holds one document per notification, created when the notification is created and updated as it is edited and submitted, and which can lag the journey a little.
requirements.why: The read model is the cross-journey source the home was handed off to; its eventual consistency means a count can briefly trail a change.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p4-080 and repo-tests-p4-088: one aggregated document per notification, updated on submit, polled because it is eventually consistent (repo-tests-p4-090).

requirements.statement: The INS front door reads the home's counts and the drill-down lists from ins-backend, carrying the request's trace id, and from its built-in stub when stub mode is on (never in production).
requirements.why: The front door already reads the read model this way for its table; the home and drill-downs need new reads (counts by category, filtered lists) on the same terms.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the front door makes one read, GET /notifications with page, sort and referenceNumber (repo-insfrontend-p1-062, repo-insfrontend-p1-063).

requirements.statement: If the read model cannot be loaded, the home and drill-downs still render their heading, flag a recoverable error, respond with HTTP 500 and log the failure; an error already shaped for the framework is passed on.
requirements.why: A failure in another service is a constraint the prototype cannot express; the front door already handles it this way for its table.
requirements.deltaNote: Today this handling covers only the table on / (repo-insfrontend-p1-058); the home's counts and the three drill-downs need it too.

requirements.statement: The home and drill-downs carry Welsh copy with the same keys as the English, marked as a machine draft not to ship without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
requirements.why: The front door keeps Welsh copy beside every English copy file; Design Release 2.1 shows only English.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's Welsh dashboard copy covers the table page's keys (repo-insfrontend-p1-086); the home and drill-downs need their own.

requirements.statement: The home and each drill-down have no serious or critical axe violations against the WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 A and AA tags, proven by a fit test.
requirements.why: The front door proves its dashboard accessible today and the new pages must hold the same bar.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the axe fit test covers the table page at / (repo-insfrontend-p1-079); the drill-downs have none.

requirements.statement: The home and drill-downs keep the standard GOV.UK header (logo to gov.uk, service name to the service root), the 'Skip to main content' link and the standard GOV.UK footer.
requirements.why: The shared layout already provides them on every INS page.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-ins-fit-p4-006-m1: every INS page has the GOV.UK header, the skip link and the GOV.UK footer.

requirements.statement: Following a link from the home into the animals or plants frontend lands the trader there signed in, without a second sign-in, once they have a session with that service; each service keeps its own session cookie.
requirements.why: The home links across service origins, so the cross-service sign-in must hold for the links to work.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p4-067 and repo-tests-p4-076: sessions in animals, INS and plants hold together and INS links land in animals signed in.

requirements.statement: This area does not change the category dashboards' own content (the animals and plants dashboards' intro text, filters, sort options and empty states).
requirements.why: The home stops at a category's notification list; those pages are the notification-list area's to reconcile.

requirements.statement: This area does not change the submission confirmation page, the read-only notification view or the declaration step seen while proving the read model.
requirements.why: They belong to the live-animals journey's own areas; here they only show how a notification reaches the read model.

requirements.statement: This area does not change the address book pages reached from the home's navigation.
requirements.why: The address book is its own area.

requirements.statement: DR1's 'At a glance' band (Alerts, Errors and Messages cards with 'View alerts', 'View errors', 'View messages') and its 'Create a new notification' button label are not built.
requirements.why: The DR1 parity backlog is not a source of requirements; Design Release 2.1's per-category glance cards and 'Create new' replace that earlier design.

requirements.statement: The INS frontend serves the category notification lists at /live-animals and /germinal-products, in the same service as the overall home, reading the INS backend read model; the animals frontend's own dashboard at its set root sends the trader to the INS frontend's live animals list, and the animals backend's GET /notifications is left as it is until nothing calls it.
requirements.why: Rhys's DR1 judgement (2026-08-28) moves the temporary animals-frontend dashboard to the INS frontend, Design Release 2.1 puts the lists in the same service as the overall home, and the animals backend's list is due to be replaced by the event-populated read model (c-159).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the dashboard is the animals frontend's GET route at /live-animals, backed by the animals backend's GET /notifications; the INS backend read model exists but serves the INS frontend's own dashboard.

requirements.statement: The list page's browser title is 'Dashboard - Import notification service - GOV.UK', with the caption 'Dashboard' above an h1 naming the category: 'Live animals' on the live animals list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 titles every list 'Dashboard' and heads it with the category, so a trader can tell which category's notifications they are looking at.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the animals dashboard's browser title repeats the service name: 'Import notification service - Import notification service - GOV.UK' (trace-animals-fit-p1-003, trace-e2e-p1-033).

requirements.statement: The list page has no introductory paragraph and no Messages link: the heading is followed directly by the 'Create new' and 'Use template' buttons.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's category list goes straight from its heading to its actions; the service explanation and messages live on the overall home.
requirements.deltaNote: Today one paragraph about telling the authorities about imported live animals sits under the heading.

requirements.statement: The list page has a 'Back' link to the overall dashboard home at the service root (/).
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 a category list is reached from the overall home, and the back link returns the trader there.

requirements.statement: The list page has a primary 'Create new' button that links to the start of the create journey carrying the list's category (create-notification?category=live-animals on the live animals list), instead of a 'Start a new notification' form that creates a draft on the click.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 starts a notification by asking its type first, carrying the category the trader was looking at; today's button creates a draft and its reference straight away, with no question asked, and every press makes another draft.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a GOV.UK start button 'Start a new notification' POSTs to /live-animals/notifications, which creates a draft and redirects straight to its origin page.

requirements.statement: The list page has a secondary 'Use template' button beside 'Create new' that links to the templates page, without a category.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers starting from a saved template from every category list.

requirements.statement: The list page has an h2 'Summary' section with two glance cards: 'Action needed' with 'Tasks requiring your attention' and a 'View tasks' link to the action-needed page filtered to the category, and 'Status updated' with 'Changes in the past 24 hours' and a 'View updates' link to the changes page filtered to the category.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts what needs the trader's attention at the top of each category list.

requirements.statement: The list's 'Action needed' glance card shows a live count for the category: the notifications showing the 'Action required' tag (a 'Delayed' one does not count), matching the Action needed list its link opens.
requirements.why: The count is only useful if it agrees with the drill-down page; a notification is action-required when it is missing a required document or required identifiers, as Design Release 2.1 works it out (c-149).

requirements.statement: The list's notifications sit under an h2 'Notifications', replacing the h2 'Your notifications'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 heads the list section 'Notifications'; DR1's 'My notifications' row was only deferred, never judged.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the list heading is the medium h2 'Your notifications' (Welsh 'Eich hysbysiadau'), also used as the breadcrumb label on the delete and cancel-amendment pages.

requirements.statement: The search, sort and additional filters sit in one column above the tabs inside the 'Notifications' section, with no 'Filter notifications' heading and no separate one-third filter aside beside the results.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lays the list out as one column: search and sort, then the filters disclosure, then the tabs and cards.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the list is two columns: a one-third aside headed 'Filter notifications' (h3) holding the search, and a two-thirds column holding the results count, sort and cards.

requirements.statement: The search field is labelled 'Search by'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label; today's 'Keyword or reference' promises a keyword search the service does not give.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the field is labelled 'Keyword or reference' (small bold label) and named referenceNumber.

requirements.statement: The search field has the hint 'Keyword, notification number, commodity, consignee or consignor'.
requirements.why: The hint tells the trader what the search matches.

requirements.statement: The search is submitted by an icon-only button showing a magnifying glass, whose accessible name is 'Search'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's search control; today's is a standard primary button reading 'Search'.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the button is a standard GOV.UK button with the visible text 'Search'.

requirements.statement: A search lists the notifications whose reference number, commodity, consignee or consignor contains the searched text, ignoring case, rather than only an exact, whole reference number.
requirements.why: The hint promises a keyword search over those facts. The prototype cannot persist or query, so its search is inert; a real search box that does nothing would mislead the trader, so the real service applies it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the term is passed to the listing only as referenceNumber, an exact match on a complete reference, so a commodity or a party name finds nothing.

requirements.statement: After a search the field keeps the searched text, and searching with an empty or whitespace-only field clears the search and lists everything again.
requirements.why: The trader can see and change what they searched for; both Design Release 2.1 and today keep the text.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-016 and repo-frontend-p3-015: the field is filled with the current term, and a blank or whitespace-only term means no filter (proven by repo-frontend-p3-114).

requirements.statement: Search, sort and every additional filter are one GET form to the list's own path, submitted by the search button; it carries the current tab (unless 'In progress') and the current page (when above 1) as hidden fields, so the result stays on that tab.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts sort and filters inside the search form with one submit control; today search and sort are two forms and a search always restarts at page 1.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the search form carries only the sort as a hidden field (no page, no tab), and the sort is a separate form.

requirements.statement: The sort select is labelled 'Sort by:'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label for the sort control.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the select is labelled 'Sort by' with no colon (small bold label).

requirements.statement: The sort select offers exactly 'Newest first', 'Oldest first' and 'Arrival date', in that order, with no unselected 'Select one' option.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's three orderings replace today's four; DR1 already rejected an unsorted 'Select one' state, so the list is always sorted.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the options are 'Arrival (newest to oldest)', 'Arrival (oldest to newest)', 'Date created (newest to oldest)' and 'Date created (oldest to newest)'.

requirements.statement: The list is always sorted and the sort is applied for real: 'Newest first' and 'Oldest first' order by when the notification was created, 'Arrival date' orders by arrival date newest first, and with no sort chosen the list is ordered by arrival date newest first with 'Arrival date' selected.
requirements.why: DR1 judged the list always sorted; the prototype never orders its list, so the real service applies the orderings, keeping today's default order (which the prototype's completed tab also shows).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the default is 'Arrival (newest to oldest)' and any unknown value falls back to it; the stub orders every option by creation date, and no test proves the order of the cards.

requirements.statement: There is no 'Update sort' button: the chosen sort is applied by the search button with the rest of the form, and the chosen option stays selected after the page reloads.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's sort has no button of its own; DR1 only deferred this difference.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a separate GET sort form with a secondary 'Update sort' button applies the sort, carrying the page and the search as hidden fields.

requirements.statement: The list has a collapsible 'Additional filters' section with a chevron, closed on load and open whenever an arrival-date, date-range or status filter is set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps the extra filters out of the way until the trader needs them.

requirements.statement: The additional filters have a 'By arrival date' column of small radios 'Today', 'Tomorrow' and 'Next 7 days' (legend visually hidden, the same words shown as its heading); choosing one lists only notifications arriving in that range, and the choice stays checked.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets a trader find what is arriving soon; the prototype's filter is inert, so the real service applies it.

requirements.statement: The additional filters have a 'By date range' column with the hint 'For example, 27/3/2026' and two MOJ date pickers, 'Start date' and 'End date' (a 'Choose date' calendar opening on the current month, weeks starting Monday); the list shows only notifications arriving between the two dates, and the entered dates are kept.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's date range; it sits beside the arrival-date radios, so it filters the arrival date, as DR1's row also read it.

requirements.statement: When the start or end date cannot be read as a date, or the end date is before the start date, the list shows a GOV.UK error summary and an inline error on the date field ('Enter a real start date', 'Enter a real end date' or 'End date must be the same as or after the start date'), opens 'Additional filters', keeps the entered text in the 'Start date' and 'End date' pickers, and lists notifications without the date-range filter.
requirements.why: Validation is a real constraint the prototype cannot express, so a date the filter cannot use is answered with an error rather than silently ignored; the prototype still sets the labels and keeps the entered dates, and the GOV.UK date-input error pattern supplies the messages (c-166).

requirements.statement: The additional filters have a 'Status' select offering exactly 'Select one', 'Action required', 'Submitted' and 'Completed'; choosing a status lists only notifications in it, and the choice stays selected.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's status filter offers the statuses a trader acts on; drafts have their own tab, so Draft is not offered.

requirements.statement: The list has three tabs, 'In progress', 'Draft' and 'Completed', each a link that loads the page ('In progress' the list path, 'Draft' ?tab=drafts, 'Completed' ?tab=completed); an unknown or missing tab shows 'In progress', and following a tab drops the search, sort and filters.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 separates work in flight, unfinished drafts and finished notifications; drafts keep a home on the list, which DR1 said must not be lost.

requirements.statement: The 'In progress' tab lists submitted and action-required notifications, 'Draft' lists drafts and 'Completed' lists completed notifications.
requirements.why: Each tab holds the notifications at that stage, as Design Release 2.1 sets them out; a notification being amended goes in 'In progress' (c-165).

requirements.statement: A notification being amended is listed in the 'In progress' tab with today's yellow 'Amending' tag and its status-driven actions (Resume, Copy as new, Cancel amendment, Delete).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 has no amending state and its catch-all status mapping would file one as a draft only by fallback, while the backend persists an amendment as a submitted notification in AMEND that never returns to DRAFT and publishes it as an amendment of a submission: a persistence and cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express (c-165).
requirements.deltaNote: Today an amending notification is listed with every other notification, with a yellow 'Amending' tag; there are no tabs.

requirements.statement: Only the 'In progress' tab shows a count, in bold brackets, such as 'In progress (2)'; 'Draft' and 'Completed' show none, even when selected.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 counts only the notifications in flight.

requirements.statement: Under the tabs the cards sit under an h3 naming the tab: 'Notifications in progress', 'Draft notifications' or 'Completed notifications'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's subheading for each tab panel.

requirements.statement: The list shows 8 notifications a page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's page size for every list.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page size comes from the listing: 25 from the real backends (end-to-end) and 20 from the frontend stub (fit).

requirements.statement: A list of more than one page shows GOV.UK pagination with numbered page links, a 'Previous' link from page 2 and a 'Next' link before the last page; a list of one page, or no results, shows no pagination.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses numbered pagination; today there are only Previous and Next.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the block-style pagination has only Previous and Next links, with no page numbers.

requirements.statement: A page number below 1 or not a number shows page 1, and a page past the last shows the last page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 clamps the page, so a stale or hand-typed page never shows an empty list.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a page past the last shows an empty page with 'Showing 0 of T Results' and only a Previous link; the INS backend answers 400 for a page below 1 and an empty page past the end.

requirements.statement: Page links keep the tab (unless 'In progress'), the sort (unless the default), the search text and every additional filter.
requirements.why: Because the real search and filters apply, a page link that dropped them would show a different, unfiltered list on page 2.
requirements.deltaNote: Today Previous and Next keep the sort (unless the default) and the reference search; there are no tabs or filters to keep.

requirements.statement: The list shows no results count: the 'Showing 1 Result', 'Showing S to E of T Results', 'Showing N of T Results' and 'No Results' line goes.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's category list shows no results count; DR1 only deferred its rewrite of the count.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a small bold line above the cards reads 'No Results', 'Showing 1 Result', 'Showing N of T Results' or 'Showing S to E of T Results'.

requirements.statement: A search or filter that matches nothing shows an empty list with no message: the 'No notifications found' line goes.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 has no empty-state message on any list.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a search with no match replaces the results line with 'No notifications found' and shows no cards.

requirements.statement: A tab with no notifications shows an empty list with no message: the sentence 'You have not started any notifications in this session.' goes.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 has no empty-state message; today's sentence also wrongly says the list is session-scoped.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a user with no notifications who is not searching sees 'You have not started any notifications in this session.' below the sort.

requirements.statement: Each notification card is labelled for screen readers 'Notification <reference>' and has the reference as its h3.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's card names itself to assistive technology; the reference heading already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each card is a GOV.UK summary card with the reference as its level-3 title, but no 'Notification <reference>' accessible name.

requirements.statement: A card shows its facts in two rows: 'Commodity', 'Arrival date', 'Consignee' and 'Notification status', then the quantity, 'Origin', 'Consignor' and, when inspection is required, 'Inspection'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's card leads with what is coming, when, to whom and its status.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the card shows eight facts in three rows: Commodity, Origin, 'Arrival at destination'; Consignee, Consignor, Status; 'Date created', 'Date submitted'.

requirements.statement: The card labels the arrival date 'Arrival date'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label; DR1's own rename row was deferred, not judged.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the label is 'Arrival at destination'.

requirements.statement: The card labels the status 'Notification status'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label for the status fact.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the label is 'Status'.

requirements.statement: A live animals notification's card shows its quantity as 'Number of animals', from the notification's own count.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows how much is coming on every card; today no card shows a quantity.

requirements.statement: The card shows no 'Date created' and no 'Date submitted'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's card has no dates other than arrival; today's 'Date submitted' is also blank on every card, submitted ones included.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the card's third row shows 'Date created' and 'Date submitted' (the latter blank in every end-to-end trace).

requirements.statement: The card writes the arrival date as the day, the full month name and the year, such as '21 June 2026'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's card writes the arrival date with the full month name, in its code and its render alike, and nothing overrides the prototype here (c-164).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the arrival date is written as day, short month name and year, such as '7 Nov 2026'.

requirements.statement: A card whose notification has no commodity, no arrival date or no quantity yet shows 'Not applicable' for that fact instead of a blank value.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 never shows an empty fact; today a draft card is mostly empty labels.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a field with no answer yet is shown with an empty value and no placeholder.

requirements.statement: The card's commodity is the notification's commodity name.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the commodity as the trader chose it; germinal products need the product type as well as the species.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the card shows the commodity's common name for its code (a commodity chosen as Bos taurus shows 'Cow'), and the INS read model keeps only the first commodity's common name. The germinal products form of the name is req-1738.

requirements.statement: A draft's status is a 'Draft' tag and an action-required notification's an 'Action required' tag, while 'Submitted' is plain styled text, not a tag.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses a tag only for statuses that ask something of the trader.
requirements.deltaNote: Today every status is a tag: Draft blue, Submitted green, Amending yellow (Deleted grey, never shown). The 'Completed' style is req-1739.

requirements.statement: A delayed notification shows a 'Delayed' tag on an error card with the reason for the delay; the prototype's placeholder text 'Error message' is not copied.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows delays on the list; its message is placeholder copy.
requirements.blockedBy: The authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sends post-submission outcomes (action required with its reason, inspection required, delayed, completed) back to the notification record; no delay status or reason reaches the service today.

requirements.statement: A notification the authorities have finished with shows the status 'Completed' and is listed in the 'Completed' tab.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 moves finished notifications out of the in-progress list.
requirements.blockedBy: The authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sends post-submission outcomes (action required with its reason, inspection required, delayed, completed) back to the notification record; no completed status reaches the service today.

requirements.statement: A notification chosen for inspection shows an extra 'Inspection' fact with a 'Required' tag at the end of the card's second row.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 warns the trader on the list that the consignment will be inspected.
requirements.blockedBy: The authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sends post-submission outcomes (action required with its reason, inspection required, delayed, completed) back to the notification record; no inspection decision reaches the service today.

requirements.statement: A card keeps its status-driven actions, each named for screen readers with ' notification <reference>': a draft offers Resume, 'Copy as new' and Delete; a submitted notification offers View, Amend, 'Copy as new' and Delete; a notification being amended offers Resume, 'Copy as new', 'Cancel amendment' and Delete. Amend and 'Copy as new' stay link-styled buttons that post, in the same typeface as the links.
requirements.why: DR1 judged that the card keeps its status-driven links rather than DR1's flat 'Copy as new' and 'View', and that judgement wins over Design Release 2.1's same flat pair. Without it a trader could not resume a draft from the list.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-047, p3-050 and p3-052 (proven by trace-animals-fit-p2-037, p2-042 and p2-044): the card already offers these sets in this order, with visually hidden ' notification <reference>' text.

requirements.statement: A card in a status the real service does not have today (action required, delayed or completed) offers 'Copy as new' then 'View', View opening the notification's review page.
requirements.why: DR1's judgement covers only the card links built today; for the new statuses nothing overrides Design Release 2.1, whose card offers 'Copy as new' and 'View'.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a notification in any status other than Draft, Submitted or Amending has no actions on its card.
requirements.blockedBy: The authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sends post-submission outcomes (action required with its reason, inspection required, delayed, completed) back to the notification record; until it does, no card is in these statuses.

requirements.statement: After an action that sends the trader back to the list (such as a delete), the list shows a GOV.UK success notification banner with role alert, titled 'Success', carrying that action's message.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses one success banner titled 'Success'; the message itself is set by the action.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banners are titled for the action: 'Notification deleted' with 'The notification has been deleted.' and 'Notification copied' with 'A new draft notification has been created.' (the copied one is never reached).

requirements.statement: The success message is held for the trader and shown once, then cleared, rather than shown whenever the list's address carries a flag such as ?deleted=1.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 clears the message after showing it, so reloading or sharing the address does not repeat it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banners show whenever the dashboard is opened with ?deleted=1 or ?copied=1.

requirements.statement: The notification list's success banner, the deletion message included, does not dismiss itself: it stays until the trader leaves or reloads the page.
requirements.why: A message that disappears on a timer can vanish before a screen reader or a slow reader reaches it; this accessibility duty overrides Design Release 2.1's 5-second auto-dismiss, and everything else about the banner follows Design Release 2.1 (c-006).
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p3-019 shows today's deletion banner is a GOV.UK success banner with role alert that stays on the page.

requirements.statement: The list keeps its stale-action banner ('The notification has been updated' / 'This notification was updated since you opened it. Review the details and try again.') and its 'There is a problem' banner when a copy from the list fails.
requirements.why: Concurrency and failure handling are real constraints the prototype cannot express, so they stay although Design Release 2.1 shows neither.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-067 and repo-frontend-p3-066: the dashboard shows the stale-action banner with ?staleAction=1 and the 'There is a problem' banner with HTTP 500 after a failed copy.

requirements.statement: Every list string has a Welsh version, marked as a machine draft that ships only after a translator signs it off under the Welsh Language Standards.
requirements.why: The real service is bilingual and its dashboard Welsh is an unreviewed machine draft; Design Release 2.1's new strings need Welsh twins too.
requirements.deltaNote: Today every English dashboard key has a machine-drafted Welsh twin in copy.cy.js, not yet reviewed by a translator.

requirements.statement: The list has no serious or critical WCAG 2 A or AA axe violations, empty or with cards, and does not scroll sideways at 1280px or at 769px wide.
requirements.why: The real dashboard meets this today and the rebuilt list must keep meeting it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-118, p3-119 and p3-108: fit tests prove no serious or critical axe violations and no sideways scroll on today's dashboard.

requirements.statement: There is a germinal products list at /germinal-products with the h1 'Germinal products', its own Summary counts, the same search, sort, additional filters and tabs pointed at its own path, and a 'Create new' button carrying category=germinal-products.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives each category of animal notification its own list.

requirements.statement: The live animals list shows only live animals notifications: a notification from any other journey that reaches the INS read model never appears on it.
requirements.why: A trader looking at one category must not see another's notifications; the read model aggregates every journey and today records no journey or category.

requirements.statement: Deleted notifications never appear on any list or in a search.
requirements.why: A deleted notification is gone for the trader; both Design Release 2.1 and the real services leave it out.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p3-002 and repo-insbackend-p1-039: both list APIs leave out DELETED notifications, proven against a real database by repo-insbackend-p1-116.

requirements.statement: A newly started notification appears on the list within seconds.
requirements.why: The list is read from an event-populated read model, so it lags writes slightly; a trader must still find their new draft straight away.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p4-002: a newly started notification is found on the dashboard by its reference within the test's 15-second retry.

requirements.statement: A list shows only the notifications of the signed-in trader's organisation, and the list API refuses a caller that does not say which organisation it acts for.
requirements.why: Authentication and data separation are real constraints the prototype cannot express; today every caller of either list API is served every trader's notifications.

requirements.statement: The read model behind the list is filled from the notification events on the queue: one record per notification keyed by its aggregate id, applied only when an event's version is higher than the stored one, with malformed or unknown events rejected.
requirements.why: This is how the list learns about notifications today, and the list depends on it staying in step.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insbackend-p1-074, p1-080 and p1-092: the INS backend upserts one record per notification from the queued events, guarded by aggregateVersion, proven by repo-insbackend-p1-128 and p1-129.

requirements.statement: The list API returns, for each notification, what the card shows: the reference number, status, category, commodity name, arrival date, origin country name, consignee name, consignor name and number of animals or packages, with a missing fact returned as empty.
requirements.why: The card cannot show facts its list API does not return; the INS read model holds only the reference, status, origin code, first commodity name, arrival date and last update.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the INS read model has no category, consignee, consignor, quantity or country name (origin is a code), and the animals backend list item carries commodity, consignor, consignee, origin and transport but no category or quantity of its own.

requirements.statement: The list API filters by category and by tab (the in-progress statuses, drafts, or completed), and reports how many notifications the 'In progress' tab holds.
requirements.why: Each list and tab shows only its own notifications, and the 'In progress' tab shows its count.

requirements.statement: The list API takes a search text and returns every notification whose reference number, commodity, consignee or consignor contains it, ignoring case and surrounding spaces, paged like any other list.
requirements.why: The list's search matches a keyword across those facts; today both list APIs match only one exact, case-sensitive, whole reference and return at most one notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Today referenceNumber is trimmed and matched exactly and case-sensitively against a whole reference; a match is always page 1 of 1, and a miss answers 200 with empty content.

requirements.statement: The list API filters by status and by an arrival-date range (from and to dates, either optional).
requirements.why: The status select and both arrival-date filters need the API to narrow the list; today neither list API has any filter beyond an exact reference.

requirements.statement: The list API sorts by creation date (newest or oldest first) and by arrival date, defaults to arrival date newest first, and breaks ties on a second key so no notification repeats or goes missing between pages.
requirements.why: 'Newest first' and 'Oldest first' order by creation date, which the INS read model does not hold (it sorts on last update), and a single-key sort with ties is unstable across pages.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the INS backend sorts on arrivalDate or lastUpdated (the animals backend on arrivalDate or createdAt), one field only with no tie-breaker, defaulting to arrival date newest first.

requirements.statement: The list API serves 8 notifications a page, numbered from 1, and reports the page, size, number of elements, total elements and total pages.
requirements.why: The list shows 8 a page and builds numbered pagination from the totals.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both list APIs serve 25 a page, set by configuration (NOTIFICATION_LIST_PAGE_SIZE in the INS backend); the response shape and 1-based page already exist.

requirements.statement: The list API answers a bad request, such as a page below 1, with a 400 validation problem response naming the field, and an unexpected failure with a 500 problem response that hides the underlying error.
requirements.why: Callers get a consistent problem-details error from the list API.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insbackend-p1-029 and p1-104: a page below 1 answers 400 'Validation Error' with an errors map keyed 'page', proven by repo-insbackend-p1-118.

requirements.statement: Read-model defects and operational details the design release does not touch stay as they are and go to the report: a non-numeric page likely answering 500, a shared reference likely answering 500, failed events never retried and so lost, no dead-letter queue shown, untested lastUpdated sorts and deletion end to end, the metrics, logging, port, switched-off OpenAPI, template README, empty seed, missing rulings ledger and the absence of a get-one endpoint.
requirements.why: None of these is a difference from Design Release 2.1; the programme does not fix them, so they are reported rather than built.
requirements.deltaNote: Recorded from the INS backend as it is today.

requirements.statement: The prototype's demo data is not built: its seeded notifications and their fixed references, the states it fakes by a notification's position (action required, status changes, delays, inspection, Plants), its placeholder number of animals, its demo consignee and consignor names, its fixed commodity-code look-up, its category guess for unlabelled notifications and its session ordering of drafts, submissions and seeds.
requirements.why: These are demonstration mechanics of the prototype, not rules for the real service, which holds real notifications with their own facts and statuses.

requirements.statement: The prototype's list with no category is not built: its fallback heading 'Live animals and germinal products', its 'By type' select (shown only without a category, hiding Plants) and its uncategorised 'View tasks' and 'View updates' links.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 always reaches a list with a category, so these are never seen.

requirements.statement: The address book lives in the INS frontend at /address-book, reached from an 'Address book' item in the service navigation, and that item is marked active (aria-current) on the list, view and delete pages. 'Log out' stays in the navigation.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts the address book behind the service navigation; DR1's inc-062 ruling already placed the real book in the INS front door rather than the animals frontend.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS frontend serves the list at /address-book (repo-insfrontend-p2-001), its navigation links to it and marks it active on the list, view and delete pages (trace-ins-fit-p2-004, trace-ins-fit-p2-007, trace-ins-fit-p3-069), and the animals dashboard links across to it (repo-tests-p5-001). The navigation's Templates item belongs to the shared layout area.

requirements.statement: A signed-out user opening any address book page is sent to sign in and returned to the page they asked for; a signed-in session with no organisation is refused.
requirements.why: The real address book holds an organisation's records, so it needs an authenticated organisation; the prototype cannot express sign-in.
requirements.deltaNote: Signed-out requests to /address-book and /address-book/add redirect to /auth/sign-in with the path as redirect (trace-e2e-p15-010, trace-e2e-p15-011); a session without an organisation gets 403 (repo-insfrontend-p2-002).

requirements.statement: Address book page titles read '<page heading> - Import notification service - GOV.UK': 'Address book - Import notification service - GOV.UK' on the list, '<address name> - Import notification service - GOV.UK' on the view page and 'Delete this address? - Import notification service - GOV.UK' on the delete page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 titles every page with the GOV.UK suffix and a hyphen separator.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the titles are 'Address book | Import notification service', '<name> | Import notification service' and 'Delete address | Import notification service' (trace-ins-fit-p2-008, trace-ins-fit-p2-037, trace-ins-fit-p3-047): a pipe separator and no GOV.UK suffix.

requirements.statement: The list page's heading is 'Address book'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list's h1 is 'Address book' (repo-insfrontend-p2-003, trace-ins-fit-p2-009).

requirements.statement: Under the heading the list page shows, in large body text, 'Manage your addresses for use across all your import notifications'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's intro wording.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the intro reads 'Manage addresses used across import and export services.' in normal body text (repo-insfrontend-p2-004, trace-ins-fit-p2-010).

requirements.statement: The list page has an 'Add a new address' button (a link styled as a button) to /address-book/add, shown whatever the list holds.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list always shows 'Add a new address' to /address-book/add (repo-insfrontend-p2-010, trace-ins-fit-p2-013).

requirements.statement: On the list page the 'Add a new address' button comes directly under the intro, above the 'Filter addresses' panel and the category tabs.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's order puts adding first and filtering below it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the search form sits between the intro and the 'Add a new address' button (repo-insfrontend-p2-005, repo-insfrontend-p2-010).

requirements.statement: Search and the Type filter sit inside a collapsible 'Filter addresses' disclosure with a chevron, collapsed when the list loads, so the search field is hidden until the user opens it. It is built on the GOV.UK details component, styled to match the design.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 tucks filtering away behind one disclosure.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the search form is always visible with no disclosure (repo-insfrontend-p2-005), and the pages use govuk-frontend components only (trace-e2e-p15-037).

requirements.statement: The search field is labelled 'Search'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the field is labelled 'Search addresses' (repo-insfrontend-p2-005, trace-e2e-p15-023).

requirements.statement: The search field's placeholder is 'Search by name, address or country', and it has no hint.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 guides the search with a placeholder, not a hint.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the code carries a hint 'Search by name, town or city, postcode or country', passed where the input macro most likely does not render it, and no placeholder (repo-insfrontend-p2-006).

requirements.statement: The search field has an icon-only search button whose accessible name is 'Search', in place of a visible 'Search' text button; without JavaScript, pressing Enter in the search field submits the filter form.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's search control.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a primary text button 'Search' submits the form (repo-insfrontend-p2-007, trace-e2e-p9-089).

requirements.statement: Search matches the trimmed text, case-insensitively and anywhere inside a word, against an address's name, type labels, every address line (line 1, line 2, town or city, county, postcode), its transporter approval number and its country name; a blank search is no search.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 searches the whole visible row, so 'Ballymore' or a country finds the entry; today only name, town and postcode match.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the address book API's q matches only name, town or city and postcode (repo-addressbook-p3-032, repo-addressbook-p3-033), and a country is found only when the whole term resolves to a country name, which the INS frontend turns into an OR countryCode filter (repo-insfrontend-p2-009). Case-insensitive, partial, literal, trimmed matching already holds (repo-addressbook-p3-034 to p3-039).

requirements.statement: The address book API keeps its countryCode filter as it is: an exact, trimmed ISO alpha-2 code, ignored when blank, organisation-scoped, leaving out deleted addresses, and combined with q by OR.
requirements.why: The locked contract and ruling cv-048 fix these semantics; nothing in Design Release 2.1 asks to change them.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven by the address book's AddressSearchIT and OperatorServiceTest (repo-addressbook-p3-064 to p3-066, repo-addressbook-p3-074, repo-addressbook-p3-075).

requirements.statement: The address book filter stays a GET form to /address-book carrying category, search and type, and the address book API filters the whole category by q and type and returns 8 a page. Without JavaScript, pressing Enter in the search field, or choosing a type and pressing Enter, submits it. With JavaScript, the page re-requests the list as the user types or changes Type (debounced) and swaps in the table, results line and pagination without a full reload, with no apply button. The same holds locally, in the stub, on the compose stack and in CDP.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 filters live across the whole category with no apply button, and the prototype wins on that behaviour; the real address book is paged on the server and cannot be asked for a whole category, a constraint that overrides only the prototype's way of holding every row in the page (c-169).
requirements.deltaNote: Today search is a server-side GET form submitted by a Search button, and the API answers one server-sized page at a time (repo-insfrontend-p2-005, repo-insfrontend-p2-068, repo-addressbook-p3-010).

requirements.statement: While a search or Type filter is active the results line counts the matches (for example 'Showing 1-2 of 2'), and pagination shows only when the matches run past one page of 8; with JavaScript both update as the list is re-requested.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps the count true to what is shown while filtering and hides pagination unless the matches need it; nothing the server-paged constraint forces changes that (c-169).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the results line already counts only matches after a submitted search (repo-addressbook-p3-047, repo-insfrontend-p2-014), but it does not update as the user types.

requirements.statement: The list is split into four category tabs, in this order: 'Origin and Consignor', 'Destination, Consignee and Importer', 'Transporter' and 'Branch'; each tab is a link to /address-book?category=origin-and-consignor, destination-consignee-importer, transporter or branch, and the selected one is marked.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 groups addresses by what they are used for.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the list is one table with no tabs (trace-e2e-p15-026), and the API has no type or usage filter to split by (repo-addressbook-p3-046). The address type each record carries comes from the add-and-edit area's typed record.

requirements.statement: Each tab panel has its own heading: 'Origin and Consignor addresses', 'Destination, Consignee and Importer addresses', 'Transporter addresses' or 'Branch addresses'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 heads each category's table.

requirements.statement: An address appears on every tab whose category holds any of its types: Origin and Consignor holds place of origin, consignor, consignor or exporter and exporter; Destination, Consignee and Importer holds consignee, importer, place of destination, contact and packer; Transporter holds transporters; Branch holds branch addresses. So an address with several types can appear on more than one tab, and the list API can return one category's addresses.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lists an organisation under each use it is held for.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's record carries no type (repo-tests-p5-095, trace-e2e-p15-082, repo-insfrontend-p2-070) and the list has no type or category filter (repo-addressbook-p3-046).

requirements.statement: With no category in the URL, or an unknown one, the list opens on the Origin and Consignor tab.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's default tab.

requirements.statement: Each tab link goes to page 1 of that category, keeps the current search and drops the Type filter; the filter form carries the selected category as a hidden field so filtering stays on the current tab.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps a search across tabs but not a type, which is per category.

requirements.statement: The legacy category values origin-and-sender and destination-and-receiver are not accepted as aliases.
requirements.why: They exist only so the prototype's older design releases keep working; the real service never used those values, so there are no links to keep alive.

requirements.statement: The filter has a select labelled 'Type' whose first option is 'Select one' (empty value), then options for the current tab only: 'Place of Origin' and 'Consignor' on Origin and Consignor; 'Consignee', 'Importer' and 'Place of Destination' on Destination, Consignee and Importer; 'Commercial' and 'Private' on Transporter; 'Branch Address' on Branch.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 narrows a tab by type.
requirements.deltaNote: Today there is no type filter in the page or the API (repo-addressbook-p3-046).

requirements.statement: The Type filter keeps a transporter whose transporter type (Commercial or Private) equals the choice, and any other address when one of its types equals the choice; the list API takes the type and category so the filter runs over the whole category, still organisation-scoped and without deleted addresses.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's type matching, delivered over the real, paged book.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the list API's only filters are q and countryCode, every path pinned to ACTIVE and the caller's organisation (repo-addressbook-p3-046, repo-addressbook-p3-027).

requirements.statement: Above the table a results line reads 'Showing <start>-<end> of <total>'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list shows 'Showing <from>-<to> of <total>' (repo-insfrontend-p2-014, trace-ins-fit-p2-015).

requirements.statement: When nothing matches, or the book or tab is empty, the list shows 'Showing 0 of 0' and an empty table, with no empty-state or no-match message.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the same table whatever it holds.
requirements.deltaNote: Today an empty book shows 'You have no addresses yet.' and a search with no match shows 'No addresses match "<term>".', each in place of the table and with no results line (repo-insfrontend-p2-012, repo-insfrontend-p2-013, trace-ins-fit-p2-034).

requirements.statement: The list has no 'Clear search' link; the user clears the search field instead.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's filter has no clear control.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a 'Clear search' link to /address-book shows above the results of a search and under a no-match message (repo-insfrontend-p2-013, repo-insfrontend-p2-015).

requirements.statement: On every tab except Transporter the table's columns are Name, Type, Address and Country, then an action column whose header 'Action' is visually hidden.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows what each address is used for.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the columns are Name, Address, Country and the hidden Action, with no Type column (repo-insfrontend-p2-016, trace-e2e-p15-026).

requirements.statement: On the Transporter tab the table's columns are Name, Address, Approval number and Type, then the hidden Action column, with no Country column: the country is the address's last line, the approval number reads like 'RO/BUCHAREST/T1/00092010', and Type is 'Commercial' or 'Private'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows transporters by approval and type.

requirements.statement: In the Name column a name of more than one word is shown on two lines: the first word, then the rest.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's Name cell.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the Name cell shows the name on one line (repo-insfrontend-p2-017).

requirements.statement: In the Address column every stored address line (line 1, line 2, town or city, county, postcode) is shown on its own line, each but the last ending in a comma; blank lines are left out.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the whole address, line by line.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the cell joins only address line 1, town or city and postcode into one comma-separated line, leaving out line 2 and county (repo-insfrontend-p2-018, trace-e2e-p15-027).

requirements.statement: The Country column shows the country's name, not its code.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list looks up the country name, falling back to the code (repo-insfrontend-p2-019, trace-e2e-p15-028).

requirements.statement: The Type column shows the address's type labels joined by ', ', using the list's labels: 'Place of origin', 'Consignor' (for consignor, consignor or exporter and exporter), 'Consignee', 'Importer', 'Place of destination', 'Transporter', 'Branch', 'Contact address' and 'Packer'. These differ in case and wording from the Type filter's options.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 labels uses in sentence case in the table.

requirements.statement: Each row ends with a 'View' link to /address-book/{id}; its accessible name adds the address's name in visually hidden text ('View <name>').
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's row action; the hidden name keeps each link distinct for screen reader users.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list already ends each row with 'View' plus the hidden name (repo-insfrontend-p2-020, trace-ins-fit-p2-021).

requirements.statement: The list shows 8 addresses a page, set through the address book service's server-side page size setting.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 pages at 8; ruling cv-025 keeps page size a server setting, so the setting changes rather than the contract.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the address book pages at 25 because address-book.list.page-size is unset (repo-addressbook-p3-011), and the INS list shows 25 a page (trace-ins-fit-p2-023, trace-e2e-p15-030).

requirements.statement: When there is more than one page, GOV.UK pagination shows a numbered link to every page with the current one marked, 'Previous' except on the first page and 'Next' except on the last; with one page there is no pagination.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list already renders GOV.UK pagination this way (repo-insfrontend-p2-021, trace-ins-fit-p2-024 to p2-029).

requirements.statement: Pagination links keep the category, search and Type filter, and add page only for pages after the first.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps the user's tab and filters as they page.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the links keep q and countryCode and add page only after the first (repo-insfrontend-p2-022); there is no category or type to keep.

requirements.statement: A page number below 1 or not a number shows page 1, and one beyond the last page shows the last page's addresses.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 never shows an empty page for a stale page link.
requirements.deltaNote: A missing, non-numeric or sub-1 page already means page 1 (repo-insfrontend-p2-011), but a page beyond the last gets an empty items list from the API (repo-addressbook-p3-017) while only the label and pagination are clamped (repo-insfrontend-p2-023).

requirements.statement: The list shows the newest address first, with a stable order from page to page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lists the user's latest additions first; the real API already sorts newest first.
requirements.deltaNote: The API sorts by creation time, newest first, ties by id (repo-addressbook-p3-028, repo-addressbook-p3-029); a newly saved address lands in the first row (trace-e2e-p15-031).

requirements.statement: After an add, edit or delete the list shows a GOV.UK success notification banner titled 'Success' above the heading, once: it is cleared when read.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list shows the session's success message once in a 'Success' banner (repo-insfrontend-p2-028, repo-insfrontend-p2-029).

requirements.statement: The success banner stays on the page; it does not hide itself after a few seconds.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's banner stays until the user moves on, so slower readers do not miss it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today client JavaScript hides the banner 3 seconds after load (repo-insfrontend-p2-030).

requirements.statement: After a delete the banner reads '<Name> address deleted', with the name's first letter capitalised and the rest lower-cased (for example 'Green valley farm address deleted'), or 'Address deleted' when the name is blank.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's delete confirmation wording.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banner reads '<name> deleted from your address book', name as typed (repo-insfrontend-p2-031, trace-e2e-p15-035).

requirements.statement: The address book is stored by the address book service and belongs to the organisation: every user signed in to the same organisation sees the same addresses, and one user's additions and deletions show for the others.
requirements.why: Persistence and organisation scoping are real constraints the prototype, which holds the book in one user's session, cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: The service scopes by organisation only, with no user identity (repo-addressbook-p4-003); E2E proves another user in the organisation sees adds and deletes (trace-e2e-p15-077, trace-e2e-p15-078).

requirements.statement: Address book additions, edits and deletions held only in the user's session, with no address book API behind them.
requirements.why: Set aside by c-172: the real book is persisted and organisation-wide.

requirements.statement: No caller can list, read or delete another organisation's addresses: the path organisation must match the caller's organisation header exactly, and any miss, whether unknown or another organisation's, is the same 404, never 403.
requirements.why: Organisation isolation and non-disclosure are real authorisation constraints (rulings cv-010 and cv-040).
requirements.deltaNote: Proven in the address book's AddressScopingIT and IdentityHeaderFilterTest (repo-addressbook-p4-053, repo-addressbook-p4-054, repo-addressbook-p4-059); no E2E spec signs in as a second organisation (repo-tests-p5-097).

requirements.statement: Every address book API call must carry a well-formed Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header (1 to 64 letters, digits, underscores or hyphens); a missing, blank or malformed one is refused with a 400 problem response with no errors map, before any handler runs, and a new address is stamped with that organisation.
requirements.why: The header is the address book's only tenant key.
requirements.deltaNote: IdentityHeaderFilter enforces it on every /organisation/ path (repo-addressbook-p4-006, repo-addressbook-p4-010, repo-addressbook-p4-044).

requirements.statement: The INS frontend calls the address book server-side under /organisation/{orgId}/addresses with the signed-in session's organisation in the Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header and the trace id, and refuses to call it without an organisation.
requirements.why: The address book trusts the header alone, so it must come only from the authenticated session (ruling cv-010).
requirements.deltaNote: The INS client sets the header from the session and fails before sending without one (repo-insfrontend-p2-065, repo-insfrontend-p2-067).

requirements.statement: The address book's trust boundary outside the service: stripping a client-sent organisation header, setting it from the verified session, CDP network policy, and the service's own resource-server authentication.
requirements.why: Platform and deployment controls the Design Release 2.1 programme does not change; it goes to the report as a standing risk nothing in the repo proves.

requirements.statement: The address book service logs each request with the caller's organisation id and no address personal data, logs list requests without the search term, and times the list endpoint and its query as metrics.
requirements.why: Operability without leaking personal data.
requirements.deltaNote: IdentityHeaderFilter and OperatorController already do this (repo-addressbook-p4-036, repo-addressbook-p3-048, repo-addressbook-p3-049).

requirements.statement: The list API (GET /organisation/{orgId}/addresses) returns a camelCase page object with items, page, pageSize, totalItems and totalPages, holds only live addresses, and answers errors as application/problem+json.
requirements.why: The real list contract the INS frontend reads.
requirements.deltaNote: OperatorPageResponse and OperatorListIT (repo-addressbook-p3-018, repo-addressbook-p3-053).

requirements.statement: Reading one address by id returns it with every stored field, including a deleted one with deleted true; only that tells a caller the address was deleted, and a 404 means unknown or not this organisation's.
requirements.why: Notifications keep referring to addresses after they are deleted, so deletion must stay detectable.
requirements.deltaNote: AddressGetIT proves 200 with deleted true for a tombstone and 404 for an unknown id (repo-addressbook-p2-033, repo-addressbook-p2-034).

requirements.statement: Deleting an address removes it from the list and search for everyone in the organisation but keeps it as a tombstone (deleted, name intact, readable by id); delete answers 204, is idempotent, cannot be undone, and is reached in the interface only through the delete confirmation page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 removes the address from the book; the tombstone is the real persistence constraint that stops notifications referencing it from dangling.
requirements.deltaNote: The service soft-deletes and answers 204 idempotently (repo-addressbook-p2-053, repo-addressbook-p2-058); E2E proves the tombstone (trace-e2e-p15-075).

requirements.statement: The address view page is at /address-book/{id}, headed with the address's name, and can be opened directly by its URL.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS view page is served at /address-book/{id} with the name as h1 (repo-insfrontend-p2-032, repo-insfrontend-p2-038).

requirements.statement: The view page's summary list always shows, in this order, 'Name or organisation name', 'Address line 1', 'Town or city', 'Postcode or Zip code', 'Country' (as a name), 'Email address' and 'Phone number'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on these rows.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS view page shows these rows in this order (repo-insfrontend-p2-040, trace-ins-fit-p2-039).

requirements.statement: The view page shows 'Address line 2 (optional)' after Address line 1, and the county row after Town or city, only when they have a value.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 leaves empty optional rows out.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both rows always show, blank when empty (repo-insfrontend-p2-049, trace-ins-fit-p2-041).

requirements.statement: The view page's county row is labelled 'County (optional)'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the row is labelled 'County' (repo-insfrontend-p2-045, trace-ins-fit-p2-042).

requirements.statement: The view page does not show the address's types or uses, and its summary rows have no Change links: the whole address is changed through the Edit button.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS view page has no type row and no Change links (repo-insfrontend-p2-040, repo-insfrontend-p2-050).

requirements.statement: The view page's 'Edit' button, to /address-book/{id}/edit, is a secondary button, beside the Delete button in a button group.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 styles Edit as secondary.
requirements.deltaNote: Today Edit is a primary (green) button-link to /address-book/{id}/edit (repo-insfrontend-p2-051).

requirements.statement: The view page has a red warning 'Delete' button to /address-book/{id}/delete.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS view page has a warning 'Delete' button-link (repo-insfrontend-p2-052, trace-ins-fit-p2-045).

requirements.statement: With no return path, the view page's Back link goes to the address book list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS view page's Back link goes to /address-book (repo-insfrontend-p2-039, trace-ins-fit-p2-047).

requirements.statement: The view and delete pages honour a return query: the view page's Back link goes to it, its Edit and Delete links carry it on, the delete page's Back and 'No, cancel' carry it to the view page, and after a delete the user goes to it unless it is one of the deleted address's own pages, when they go to the list. A return is honoured when it starts with a single / (an INS page), or when it is an absolute URL whose origin exactly equals the configured animals frontend origin, so a user who opened the address from an animals journey page goes back to it; anything else falls back to the list (view page) or the view page (delete page). Locally, on the compose stack and in CDP the allowed origin is each environment's animals frontend base URL; in the INS stub mode only same-origin paths are honoured.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sends the user back to where they opened the address from; the animals frontend is on another origin, a cross-service constraint that extends the prototype's single-/ rule to that one origin and never to any origin (c-170).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the view page's Back always goes to the list and a delete always lands on the list (repo-insfrontend-p2-039, repo-insfrontend-p2-061).

requirements.statement: Opening the view page for an id that is not a live address in the organisation's book (unknown, malformed, another organisation's or deleted) sends the user to the view page's back link (the return path or the list) rather than a 404 page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 redirects a dead address link instead of showing an error.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a malformed id, an unknown or other organisation's id and a deleted address all respond 404 Page not found (repo-insfrontend-p2-033, repo-insfrontend-p2-035, repo-insfrontend-p2-036).

requirements.statement: Opening the delete page for an id that is not a live address in the book redirects to the return path or the list; posting a delete for such an id changes nothing, shows no banner and redirects as a delete would.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 treats a stale delete as a no-op rather than an error.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the delete page and its POST respond 404 when the address is missing or deleted (repo-insfrontend-p2-061, repo-insfrontend-p2-062).

requirements.statement: The address view page showing addresses found outside the book (a notification's consignment, contact or transporter addresses), without Edit or Delete.
requirements.why: Set aside by c-173: those addresses are copies held by the notification service, not the address book, so the INS view page reads the book only.

requirements.statement: When the address book service fails unexpectedly, the list renders the shared recoverable error banner with no table, and the view and delete pages respond with the service error page; each failure is logged.
requirements.why: A real cross-service failure the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list renders 'There is a problem' on failure and the view and delete pages respond 500 (repo-insfrontend-p2-025, repo-insfrontend-p2-037, repo-insfrontend-p2-062).

requirements.statement: The list renders in the wide display column; the view and delete pages in the two-thirds column; every page keeps the skip link and the standard GOV.UK footer.
requirements.why: Today's layout; nothing in Design Release 2.1 changes it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p2-027 and repo-insfrontend-p2-038-m1 set the columns; trace-ins-fit-p2-002-m1 shows the footer.

requirements.statement: The list, view and delete pages have no serious or critical axe violations against WCAG 2.0 A/AA, 2.1 A/AA and 2.2 AA after the changes.
requirements.why: Accessibility is a legal requirement for the service.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS fit suite runs axe on each page and passes today (repo-insfrontend-p2-085, repo-insfrontend-p2-092, repo-insfrontend-p2-096).

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation is served by GET and POST at /address-book/{id}/delete.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree; Design Release 2.1 overrides only this address book view.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS delete page is served at /address-book/{id}/delete by GET and POST (repo-insfrontend-p2-053).

requirements.statement: The delete page's heading is 'Delete this address?'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's heading.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the heading is 'Delete address' (repo-insfrontend-p2-054, trace-ins-fit-p3-046).

requirements.statement: The delete page shows a summary list with one row, 'Address', holding the name, each address line and the country on separate lines, leaving out any line that repeats one already shown (ignoring case) and never the email or phone; with none of those it shows 'Not applicable'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows what is being deleted before the user confirms.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the delete page shows only the address's name, in its question (repo-insfrontend-p2-056).

requirements.statement: Below the summary the delete page says 'Confirm that you want to delete this address.', in place of today's 'Are you sure you want to delete <name> from your address book?'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording; the name now shows in the summary.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page asks 'Are you sure you want to delete <name> from your address book?' with the name in bold (repo-insfrontend-p2-055, trace-ins-fit-p3-048).

requirements.statement: The delete page warns 'This action cannot be undone.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 warns the user; it is true, as the API has no restore.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's page has no such warning (repo-insfrontend-p2-055).

requirements.statement: The delete page's confirm button is a red warning button reading 'Yes, delete'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's button text.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the button reads 'Yes, delete this address' (repo-insfrontend-p2-059, trace-ins-fit-p3-050).

requirements.statement: Beside the confirm button the delete page has a 'No, cancel' link to the address's view page, deleting nothing and showing no banner.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers cancel as a link, not a second button.
requirements.deltaNote: Today cancel is a secondary submit button 'Cancel' (cancel=true) that redirects to the view page (repo-insfrontend-p2-060, trace-ins-fit-p3-051).

requirements.statement: With no return path, the delete page's Back link goes to the address's view page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS delete page's Back goes to /address-book/{id} (repo-insfrontend-p2-057).

requirements.statement: Confirming the delete deletes the address through the address book service and, with no return path, lands on the list, where the address no longer appears and the count drops by one.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS POST deletes through the service and redirects to /address-book, where the row is gone (repo-insfrontend-p2-061, trace-e2e-p15-074).

requirements.statement: The delete form is protected by a CSRF token and posts nothing else.
requirements.why: A real security constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS delete form carries a crumb token (repo-insfrontend-p2-058, trace-ins-fit-p3-068).

requirements.statement: Deleting an address makes no check on whether a notification uses it and shows no in-use warning.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree; the tombstone keeps those notifications' references whole.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS delete proceeds unconditionally (repo-insfrontend-p2-109).

requirements.statement: The INS frontend's in-memory address book stub behaves like the real list: 8 a page, filtering by search, category and Type, and soft-deleting so a deleted address reads back as deleted.
requirements.why: The fit suite runs against the stub, so it must exercise the Design Release 2.1 list rather than today's.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the stub pages at 25, ignores the search term and country code, and deletes outright (repo-insfrontend-p2-078, repo-insfrontend-p2-079, repo-insfrontend-p2-081).

requirements.statement: Every new or changed English string on the list, view and delete pages has a Welsh counterpart, kept marked as an unreviewed machine draft until it has Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
requirements.why: The INS frontend carries Welsh copy for every address book string; leaving the old Welsh would show users a different page in Welsh.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's Welsh copy matches today's English: 'Rheoli cyfeiriadau a ddefnyddir ar draws gwasanaethau mewnforio ac allforio.', 'Chwilio cyfeiriadau', 'Dileu cyfeiriad' and so on (repo-insfrontend-p2-099 to p2-105).

requirements.statement: The tests repo's shared address book fixtures each carry an address type, so they land on the right category tab and the journey parties still find them, and the pre-run reconcile treats a missing or drifted type as drift.
requirements.why: Once the list is split by type, untyped fixtures would sit on no tab and the E2E specs that find them would break.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the 13 shared fixtures are reconciled by name and hold no type (repo-tests-p5-118, repo-tests-p5-121-m1).

requirements.statement: End-to-end specs walk the address book through its own links (list, category tab, search, View, Delete, 'No, cancel', 'Yes, delete') rather than opening view and delete pages by URL, and cover the empty and no-match state.
requirements.why: Today no spec proves the user can reach view or delete from the list, or that search works.
requirements.deltaNote: Every spec opens view, edit and delete by URL (repo-tests-p5-109-m1), and no spec or trace drives search (repo-insfrontend-p2-106, trace-e2e-p15-039).

requirements.statement: The prototype's seeded demonstration addresses (its farms, transporters, three Defra branches, multi-type entries and padding copies) and their ids.
requirements.why: Demonstration data: the real book holds each organisation's own records.

requirements.statement: DR1's own address book screens and the animals frontend's navigation into them.
requirements.why: The DR1 parity backlog is not a source of requirements (the ruling), and inc-062 struck DR1's address book screens; Design Release 2.1 governs the INS book's design.

requirements.statement: Closing the address book service's own test gaps: no test proves the countryCode filter is case-sensitive, nor that q leaves out county, address line 2, phone and email.
requirements.why: A test-coverage gap in a contract this programme does not change; it goes to the report.

requirements.statement: Adding and editing an address happen in the INS front door (trade-imports-ins-frontend) for a signed-in user, saved to the address-book service and scoped to the user's organisation: every address-book call carries the organisation id in the path and the Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header, an address is only ever found inside that organisation, and a submit without an organisation on the session is refused.
requirements.why: The address book moved out of the animals frontend to the INS front door, and organisation scoping is the only guard on whose addresses a user sees.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-002, p3-039, p3-072 and repo-addressbook-p2-094 already serve add and edit from the INS front door, signed in and organisation-scoped.

requirements.statement: Adding an address starts on a new 'Choose an address type' page at /address-book/add, before any address fields, with a 'Back' link to the address book list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks what kind of address is being added first, because that decides the form and the uses offered next.
requirements.deltaNote: Today /address-book/add is the address form itself, with no type step and no back link (repo-insfrontend-p3-001, p3-038).

requirements.statement: The 'Choose an address type' page shows the caption 'Add a new address' above its heading.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.

requirements.statement: The 'Choose an address type' page's heading and page title are 'Choose an address type', and the radio group's legend repeats the heading, visually hidden.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy; the hidden legend names the radio group for screen readers.

requirements.statement: The first address type option is the radio 'Origin or Consignor' with the hint 'Place of origin, Consignor'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 groups place of origin and consignor addresses under one type, worded with 'or'.

requirements.statement: The second address type option is the radio 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' with the hint 'Place of destination, Consignee, Importer'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.

requirements.statement: The third address type option is the radio 'Transporter' with the hint 'Private, Commercial'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.

requirements.statement: The fourth address type option is the radio 'Branch' with the hint 'Branch address'.
