requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.

requirements.statement: The 'Choose an address type' page submits with a 'Continue' button.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.

requirements.statement: Continuing with no address type chosen shows 'Select an address type' inline on the radios and in a 'There is a problem' error summary whose link goes to the first option.
requirements.why: An address type is needed to know which form and uses to show.

requirements.statement: The add remembers the chosen address type between its steps, so coming back to 'Choose an address type' pre-selects it; opening the add afresh, and saving, clear the type, the entered address, the ticked uses and the search, so the next add starts empty.
requirements.why: A two-step add needs the first answer kept while it is in progress and cleared when it ends.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the add is one page that always opens blank (repo-insfrontend-p3-033); there is no in-progress state to keep or clear.

requirements.statement: Choosing 'Transporter' and continuing leaves the address book add and goes to the add-a-transporter pages; reached this way, their 'Back' link returns to 'Choose an address type'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 adds transporters through their own pages, not the address form; the address book record has no transporter category.

requirements.statement: The add-a-transporter page reached from the address book has the caption 'Add a new transporter' and the heading and page title 'Choose a transporter type'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy on the hand-over target.

requirements.statement: The add-a-transporter page shows the warning 'Check the transporter list before adding new transporters to avoid duplicates.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy; it steers users away from duplicate transporters.

requirements.statement: The add-a-transporter page offers the radios 'Private transporter' and 'Commercial' (hint 'This can only be a commercial transporter from Northern Ireland.'), posted as transporterType private or commercial, and a 'Continue' button.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy and options.

requirements.statement: Choosing 'Origin or Consignor', 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' or 'Branch' and continuing goes to the add-details step at /address-book/add/lookup, which posts back to itself.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 flow: these three types use one add-details page whose content depends on the type.

requirements.statement: Opening the add-details step directly with no address type chosen redirects to 'Choose an address type'.
requirements.why: The add-details step cannot be shown without knowing the type.

requirements.statement: The add-details step shows the caption 'Add new address' above its heading, and no notification status banner.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy; the page is the address book's, not a notification's.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the add page has no caption (repo-insfrontend-p3-004, trace-ins-fit-p1-005).

requirements.statement: The add-details step's heading and page title are 'Add address and contact details'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the heading and title are 'Add address details' (repo-insfrontend-p3-003, trace-ins-fit-p1-004).

requirements.statement: The add-details step has a 'Back' link to 'Choose an address type'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the user go back and change the type.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the add page has no back link (repo-insfrontend-p3-038).

requirements.statement: The add and edit pages' browser titles read '<page heading> - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 title format.
requirements.deltaNote: Today titles read '<heading> | Import notification service' (trace-ins-fit-p1-003, p3-003).

requirements.statement: For 'Origin or Consignor' the add-details step shows the address and contact fields straight away with no address search, and a section break separates them from the uses question.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1: origin and consignor addresses are often outside the UK, so they are entered by hand.

requirements.statement: For 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' the add-details step opens with only the address search; the address fields, contact fields and uses question stay hidden until an address is picked or manual entry is chosen, and open already revealed when an address or address line 1 is already present.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1: these are UK addresses, found by search first.
requirements.deltaNote: No real address book page offers an address search today (repo-insfrontend-p5-114).

requirements.statement: Typing in the address search is a free-text type-ahead (not a postcode-then-pick step): matching addresses appear below the field in a list labelled 'Address search results', each shown as 'name, address, country' with the typed text in bold, and a screen-reader announcement gives the number of results (for example '1 result available').
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 search behaviour.

requirements.statement: Picking a search result hides the search, announces 'Selected <name>' to screen readers, reveals the fields and fills address line 1, address line 2, town or city and postcode from the result (composed as c-178 sets out), with country United Kingdom; email address and phone number stay blank for the user, and any field the user types over wins.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 fills the address from the pick and leaves the contact details to the user.
requirements.deltaNote: The dev-only spike maps a lookup result onto the address book's fields but saves nothing (repo-insfrontend-p5-052 to p5-059).

requirements.statement: The address searches find real UK addresses from the address lookup the INS backend serves (GET /address-lookup with find=<term>, carrying the trace id): the lookup stub in the fit suites and on the local stack, the real lookup in CDP dev, and in CDP test, ext-test, perf-test and prod whatever c-217 settles; a failed lookup leaves the user able to enter the address manually.
requirements.why: The prototype's search list is made-up data shipped with the page; the real service must search real addresses through the lookup the spike proved.
requirements.deltaNote: Only the dev/local spike calls the lookup today (repo-insfrontend-p5-067, p5-114).

requirements.statement: For 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' the country is fixed: the Country select holds only 'United Kingdom', pre-selected, and the save stores United Kingdom (GB) whatever is posted.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1: destination, consignee, importer and branch addresses are in the UK.

requirements.statement: The address fields on the add and edit forms sit under the section heading 'Address'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy, the same on both forms.
requirements.deltaNote: Today add headed this section 'Enter address details' and edit has no section headings (repo-insfrontend-p3-005, p3-087).

requirements.statement: Email address and phone number on the add and edit forms sit under the section heading 'Contact details'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy, the same on both forms.
requirements.deltaNote: Today add headed this section 'Enter contact details' and edit has no section headings (repo-insfrontend-p3-005, p3-087).

requirements.statement: On the add-details step the name field is labelled 'Name or organisation'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy; its specs assert the add and edit labels differ.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the add label is 'Name or organisation name' (repo-insfrontend-p3-007).

requirements.statement: On the edit page the name field is labelled 'Name or organisation name'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-ins-fit-p3-005 shows the edit label 'Name or organisation name'.

requirements.statement: The add-details step has no County field.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's add form leaves county out; county stays optional in the record.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the add form asks 'County (optional)' (repo-insfrontend-p3-011).

requirements.statement: The edit page keeps the 'County (optional)' field between 'Town or city' and 'Postcode or Zip code', prefilled from the stored address.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's edit form keeps county.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-ins-fit-p3-011 and repo-tests-p5-103 show the edit page's prefilled 'County (optional)'.

requirements.statement: The add and edit forms ask 'Address line 1', 'Address line 2 (optional)', 'Town or city', 'Postcode or Zip code', 'Country' (a select), 'Email address' and 'Phone number' with the hint 'For international numbers include the country code', and no other field has a hint.
requirements.why: These labels and the phone hint already match Design Release 2.1.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-008 to p3-016 and trace-ins-fit-p1-010 to p1-022 already render these labels and the one phone hint.

requirements.statement: On the edit page 'Email address' comes before 'Phone number', as on the add form.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses one field order for both forms.
requirements.deltaNote: Today edit puts Phone number before Email address (repo-insfrontend-p3-087, trace-ins-fit-p3-005-m1).

requirements.statement: On the add-details step 'Name or organisation', both address lines and 'Email address' are full width, 'Town or city' and 'Postcode or Zip code' are half width, and 'Phone number' is two-thirds width.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 field widths.
requirements.deltaNote: Today phone is half width (repo-insfrontend-p3-019, trace-ins-fit-p1-020).

requirements.statement: The edit page lays its fields out like the add form: the same section headings, order and field widths.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 builds both forms from the same Address and Contact details sections.
requirements.deltaNote: Today edit uses two-thirds text inputs, a width-10 postcode and a default-width country select, unlike add (repo-insfrontend-p3-088, trace-ins-fit-p3-007-m1).

requirements.statement: The Country select lists its countries in alphabetical order, with United Kingdom in its alphabetical place.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sorts the country options alphabetically.
requirements.deltaNote: Today United Kingdom is always listed first (repo-insfrontend-p3-022, trace-e2e-p15-050).

requirements.statement: For 'Origin or Consignor' the Country select opens with United Kingdom selected.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 defaults the country to the United Kingdom.
requirements.deltaNote: Today no country is chosen by default (repo-insfrontend-p3-021, trace-ins-fit-p1-015).

requirements.statement: On the add-details step the Country select's blank first option reads 'Select one'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the placeholder reads 'Select a country' (repo-insfrontend-p3-021).

requirements.statement: On the edit page the Country select has no blank placeholder option, and the stored country is selected.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's edit form offers only real countries.
requirements.deltaNote: Today edit keeps the 'Select a country' placeholder above the stored country (trace-ins-fit-p3-013).

requirements.statement: The countries offered come from the reference data service's country list (each option shows the name and submits its ISO alpha-2 code, stored as given), not from a list held in the address book pages; the stub's four countries are used in stub mode.
requirements.why: Country lists are master reference data that the service takes from MDM, and DR1 already ruled their content is not edited page by page.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-024 and trace-e2e-p15-050 show the list read from reference data and submitted as alpha-2 codes.

requirements.statement: Saving the add or edit form without a name shows 'Enter a name or organisation name', inline and in the error summary, and the address book API's blank-name message says the same.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy; the API's message reaches the user when the service rejects a save.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the message is 'Enter a name' in the frontend and the API (repo-insfrontend-p3-044, repo-addressbook-p1-010).

requirements.statement: Saving without address line 1 shows 'Enter address line 1'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy, already met.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-046 and trace-ins-fit-p1-035 show 'Enter address line 1'.

requirements.statement: Saving without a town or city shows 'Enter a town or city'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy, already met.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-049 and trace-ins-fit-p1-036 show 'Enter a town or city'.

requirements.statement: Saving without a postcode shows 'Enter a postcode or Zip code', and the address book API's blank-postcode message says the same.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy, matching the field's label.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the message is 'Enter a postcode' (repo-insfrontend-p3-052, repo-addressbook-p1-021).

requirements.statement: Saving without a country (or with one not in the list) shows 'Select a country', and the address book API's blank-country message says the same.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy for a select.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the message is 'Enter a country' (repo-insfrontend-p3-055, repo-addressbook-p1-025).

requirements.statement: Saving without an email address shows 'Enter an email address'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy, already met.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-060 and trace-ins-fit-p1-040 show 'Enter an email address'.

requirements.statement: Saving without a phone number shows 'Enter a phone number', and the address book API's blank-phone message says the same.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy, matching the field's label.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the message is 'Enter a telephone number' (repo-insfrontend-p3-057, repo-addressbook-p1-028).

requirements.statement: Address line 2 and county are optional: blank values are accepted and saved as empty.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and the record agree these are optional.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p1-016-m1 and trace-e2e-p15-055 show blank optional fields accepted.

requirements.statement: Add and edit keep today's length limits and email format check, in the frontend and the address book API: name and both address lines 255 characters, town or city and county 100, postcode 12, phone 20 and email 254, each with its '<field> must be N characters or fewer' message, and 'Enter an email address in the correct format' for a malformed email; postcode and phone stay free text.
requirements.why: Validation is a real constraint the prototype cannot express: the record's stored limits and a usable email address.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-045 to p3-063 and repo-addressbook-p1-011 to p1-034 already enforce these limits and the email format.

requirements.statement: On a validation error the add or edit page is shown again (HTTP 400, same URL) with a 'There is a problem' error summary listing every error in field order, each linking to and focusing its field, one message per field shown inline with a hidden 'Error:' prefix, and every value the user entered kept.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and GOV.UK error pattern, already met.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-041 to p3-067 and trace-ins-fit-p1-028 to p1-033 already behave this way.

requirements.statement: When the add or edit page shows errors, its browser title keeps the 'Error: ' prefix.
requirements.why: Screen-reader users learn of the error from the title; the prototype's missing prefix is a gap, not a design choice.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-ins-fit-p1-029 and p3-025 show the 'Error: ' title prefix.

requirements.statement: Every add and edit field is trimmed of surrounding spaces before it is validated and saved, so a field of only spaces counts as empty.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-043 trims every field before validation and saving.

requirements.statement: For 'Origin or Consignor' the uses question's legend is 'What can this address be used for?'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.

requirements.statement: For 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' the uses question's legend is 'Address type'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.

requirements.statement: The uses question has the hint 'Select where this address can be used'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.

requirements.statement: An 'Origin or Consignor' address offers the use checkboxes 'Place of origin' and 'Consignor'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 options.

requirements.statement: A 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' address offers the use checkboxes 'Place of destination', 'Consignee' and 'Importer'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 options.

requirements.statement: A 'Branch' address offers exactly one use checkbox, 'Branch address'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 options.

requirements.statement: The uses are one group of checkboxes (addressUses) showing only the chosen type's uses, with no hint on each option; any posted use that does not belong to the chosen type is ignored.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 behaviour on the add-details step.

requirements.statement: The uses are checked only once the address and contact fields are valid: then, with no use ticked, saving shows 'Select what this address can be used for', linked to the first use option.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 validation order.

requirements.statement: The address-book record and its create, read-one and update API carry the address's uses (every use ticked when it was added: place of origin, consignor, place of destination, consignee, importer, branch address), so the first use gives the address its primary type and its address book type; the locked API contract is updated with the new field.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 records what each address can be used for; the record has nowhere to keep it today, and the DR1 address pickers wait on exactly this typed record.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the record is untyped and the API's request and response carry no type or use (repo-addressbook-p1-001, p1-096, trace-e2e-p9-099).

requirements.statement: The add-details step's primary button is 'Save and continue'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy, already met.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-034 and trace-ins-fit-p1-023 show 'Save and continue'.

requirements.statement: Below the 'Save and continue' button the add-details step has a 'Cancel and return to address book' link (not a button) that goes to the address book without saving.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 makes cancel a link under the button.
requirements.deltaNote: Today 'Cancel and return to address book' is a secondary submit button beside 'Save and continue' that posts cancel=true (repo-insfrontend-p3-036, trace-ins-fit-p1-024).

requirements.statement: Saving a new address from the address book returns the user to the address book list filtered to the new address's type (for example /address-book?category=origin-and-consignor), where it is listed first, with a 'View' link to its own page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the user the address they just added among its kind.
requirements.deltaNote: Today saving returns to the unfiltered list at /address-book (repo-insfrontend-p3-076, trace-ins-fit-p1-054).

requirements.statement: After adding an address the list shows a 'Success' notification banner reading '<name> address added to your address book' ('Address added to your address book' when there is no name).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banner reads '<name> added to your address book' (repo-insfrontend-p3-077, trace-ins-fit-p1-056).

requirements.statement: An added or edited address reads as address line 1, address line 2, town or city, county and postcode joined by commas, leaving out blanks, with the country shown separately.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's formatted address keeps every line the user gave.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the list's Address column shows only address line 1, town or city and postcode (trace-ins-fit-p1-058).

requirements.statement: A saved address can be found by the address book search on its name, its uses, its address and its country.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 makes the uses searchable along with the address.

requirements.statement: Creating an address persists its full record in the address-book service: POST /organisation/{orgId}/addresses answers 201 with a Location header ending in the new id, the address starts ACTIVE (deleted false) with server-set id, organisation and timestamps, and server-owned or unknown fields in the body are ignored.
requirements.why: The prototype keeps addresses only in the session; the real service must persist them.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p2-006 and repo-tests-p5-094 show a created address persisted with its full record.

requirements.statement: Saving an edit fully replaces the address's editable fields through PUT /organisation/{orgId}/addresses/{id}: a cleared optional field is cleared, id, organisation, status, createdAt and expiry are kept, modifiedAt moves on, and the record stays live.
requirements.why: An edit must change the stored address in place, not add a new one.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p2-039 and repo-tests-p5-104 show an edit replacing the record in place.

requirements.statement: An update is refused without change when the body is invalid (400 with per-field errors), the id is unknown, another organisation's or deleted (404 'Address not found'), or another write changed the address first (409 conflict); a stale write can never bring a deleted address back.
requirements.why: Persistence and authorisation constraints the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p2-044 to p2-052 prove these refusals.

requirements.statement: The address-book API answers errors as RFC 9457 problems (application/problem+json, CDP problem types, traceId from x-cdp-request-id, no instance field): a validation error carries a camelCase per-field errors map, a bad request carries none, a 500 never leaks the underlying message.
requirements.why: The frontend maps these shapes to the form, and the shapes are a locked cross-service contract.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p2-073 to p2-092 define and test these problem shapes.

requirements.statement: When the address-book service rejects a save the form is shown again with the service's first message per field and the values kept; any other save failure, or a failure loading the form, shows the recoverable error with the values kept; reference data being unavailable or empty gives a 503.
requirements.why: Cross-service failures the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-026 to p3-029 and p3-068 to p3-069 already handle these failures.

requirements.statement: Outside prod, a new address can be given an expiry (ADDRESS_TTL_DAYS) after which Mongo removes it; updates and deletes keep the original expiry, and prod is protected by two safeguards and keeps addresses indefinitely.
requirements.why: Test data must not build up outside prod while prod data is never expired.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p1-069 to p1-082 and p2-027 to p2-030 implement and test the non-prod expiry.

requirements.statement: The address-book service keeps its API surface and storage as built: the response fields (with deleted derived from status, and status, version and expireAt never returned), camelCase wire names, the hand-authored locked contract checked at build, the org_status_created index, Mongo over TLS with IAM in CDP, operation timers, and integration tests against a real Mongo.
requirements.why: This is the system of record other services depend on; none of it differs from Design Release 2.1 visibly.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p1-045 to p1-068 and p2-067 to p2-102 describe the service as built.

requirements.statement: The edit page's heading and page title are 'Edit address and contact details', with no caption.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the edit heading and title are 'Edit address details' (repo-insfrontend-p3-083, trace-ins-fit-p3-002).

requirements.statement: The edit page at /address-book/{id}/edit opens with the address and contact fields shown and prefilled from the stored address, with no address search.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-085 and trace-ins-fit-p3-006 show every field prefilled.

requirements.statement: The edit page's 'Back' link goes to the return path it was opened with, otherwise to the address's view page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 returns the user to where they came from.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the Back link always goes to the view page; no return path is honoured (repo-insfrontend-p3-084).

requirements.statement: The edit page's buttons are 'Save changes' and a secondary 'Cancel', both submit buttons.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy, already met.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-089 and trace-ins-fit-p3-019 show 'Save changes' and a secondary submit 'Cancel'.

requirements.statement: 'Cancel' on the edit page saves nothing, clears any errors and returns to the return path, by default the address's view page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sends the user back to the address they were looking at.
requirements.deltaNote: Today Cancel goes to the address book list at /address-book (repo-insfrontend-p3-090, trace-ins-fit-p3-039).

requirements.statement: The edit page does not show or change the address's uses: an edit keeps every use the address already has.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps the type off the edit form; the record must not lose uses on edit.

requirements.statement: A valid edit returns the user to the address book list (its default view), which shows the edited values under the same address.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on the destination; the list must show what was saved.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-092 and trace-ins-fit-p3-034, p3-037 show the return to /address-book with the edited values.

requirements.statement: After a valid edit the list shows a 'Success' notification banner reading '<Name> address updated', the name with its first letter capitalised and the rest lower case ('Address updated' when the name is blank).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy, asserted by its specs and traces.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banner reads '<name> updated in your address book' with the name as typed (repo-insfrontend-p3-092, trace-ins-fit-p3-035).

requirements.statement: Opening or saving the edit page for an address that is not in the user's address book (unknown, another organisation's, deleted or a malformed id) redirects to the return path or the address book list without saving.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sends the user back to the list rather than an error page.
requirements.deltaNote: Today these cases show the page not found error (repo-insfrontend-p3-080, p3-081, p3-093).

requirements.statement: Every new or changed English string on the add and edit pages gets a matching Welsh entry, still marked as an unreviewed machine draft that must not ship without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
requirements.why: The address book keeps English and Welsh copy side by side; changing only English would leave Welsh describing the old pages.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's Welsh copy mirrors today's English (repo-insfrontend-p3-114 to p3-120).

requirements.statement: Every add and edit page highlights 'Address book' in the service navigation.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-ins-fit-p1-007 and p3-021 show 'Address book' active.

requirements.statement: The add and edit pages, and their error states, use only GOV.UK Frontend components and have no serious or critical axe violations against WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 A and AA.
requirements.why: Accessibility is a standing quality bar the new pages must keep.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-124 to p3-135 and trace-ins-fit-p1-027, p3-043 show no serious or critical violations.

requirements.statement: The add and edit forms post to themselves with browser validation off and a CSRF crumb, set autocomplete only on email, and are served with the INS security headers and session cookie; the add page is sent with Cache-Control: no-store.
requirements.why: Security and form handling constraints the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-020, p3-031 and trace-ins-fit-p1-025, p1-054-m1 show these protections.

requirements.statement: The edit page is sent without Cache-Control: no-store, unlike the add page, so a browser may cache a page holding an organisation's address and contact details.
requirements.why: Not a Design Release 2.1 difference: a gap in today's service that this programme does not fix; it goes to the report.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-032.

requirements.statement: A notification journey's 'Add a new address' keeps handing over to the INS address book add through today's handshake (journey-type, notification-id, fulfilment-id and handshake-token; only the registered gbn-ag journey; the return URL built on the server; the new address id handed back; cancel returns without one; no address book banner). In journey mode the INS add page shows Design Release 2.1's add-address page, skips 'Choose an address type', opens the 'Add address and contact details' step for the type the role implies with the role's use ticked, and returns through the journey's /address-return to the page each button names: 'Save and select' commits the copy and lands on the Consignment addresses page, 'Save and return to address page' lands on the picker unselected, and 'Cancel and return to hub' saves nothing. The same holds on the compose stack and in CDP.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's journeys add addresses on their own pages, but which service writes the address book is cross-service behaviour the prototype cannot express, so the real address book stays a separate service reached through this handshake while everything the prototype can express about the page follows Design Release 2.1 (c-106).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the handshake opens the single 'Add address details' form with 'Cancel and return to address page' (repo-insfrontend-p3-107, p3-108).

requirements.statement: When the search layout ('Destination, Consignee or Importer', 'Branch') is saved with nothing picked or typed, the six field errors show and the address and contact fields are revealed, so each error summary link leads to a visible field; errors stay on the fields until the next save, and what was typed, the ticked uses and the search text are kept.
requirements.why: An error summary link must reach its field; the prototype's hidden fields are a gap, not a design choice.

requirements.statement: No separate 'What can this address be used for?' usage page (/address-book/add/usage, with a hint on each use and a 'Save address' button) is built; the uses are asked on the add-details step.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 holds this page but never reaches it: it redirects unless a pending address is held, and nothing sets one.

requirements.statement: The prototype's root 'Add address details' lookup page (full UK and EU search list, County field, 'Cancel and return to dashboard', single suggested type, no uses question) is not built as a separate page.
requirements.why: Under Design Release 2.1 it is reached only by the non-DR2.1 journey hand-off; the address book's own add uses the 'Add address and contact details' step.

requirements.statement: Design Release 1's seven address types (Place of Origin to Branch Address with their hints), its 'What is the new address for?' chooser and its add-details form are not built.
requirements.why: The DR1 parity backlog is not a source of requirements; Design Release 2.1's four types and their uses replace DR1's add journey.

requirements.statement: The dev/local-only address lookup spike page (/address-lookup-spike, EUDPA-390) is left as it is: its search form, outcome tags, timings, mapping summary, stub and Welsh draft copy are not changed to match Design Release 2.1.
requirements.why: It is a temporary engineering spike users never reach, not part of any Design Release 2.1 page; the real search reuses its lookup client (req-1218).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-003: registered in dev and local only.

requirements.statement: The INS frontend's shared validators (UK postcode format, vehicle registration, UK phone, number ranges, dates and times) stay unused by the address form.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sets no format rule on postcode or phone, and today's form uses none of these validators; nothing changes.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-121.

requirements.statement: A Manage templates page is served at /templates, with the page title 'Manage templates - Import notification service - GOV.UK' and the H1 'Manage templates'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives users one place to find, use and create notification templates; no real service has templates today.

requirements.statement: Under the Manage templates heading the page shows the line 'Select, manage or create new notification templates'.
requirements.why: The design's introductory copy for the templates list.

requirements.statement: Manage templates has a primary 'Create new template' button (a link styled as a button) to /templates/create?new=1.
requirements.why: The design's way into creating a template.

requirements.statement: Every templates page (Manage templates, Enter template name, the template page, and the delete and discard confirmations) shows the Alpha phase banner 'This is a new service. Help us improve it and give your feedback by email.', the feedback link going to the service's real feedback address rather than the prototype's '#'.
requirements.why: The design shows the phase banner on every templates page; the prototype's dead '#' link is a placeholder.

requirements.statement: On every templates page the service navigation marks 'Templates' as the active item.
requirements.why: Templates is a top-level area of the service in the design, beside the dashboard and address book.

requirements.statement: Manage templates has no Back link: it starts directly with its heading.
requirements.why: It is a top-level page reached from the service navigation or the dashboard.

requirements.statement: The templates are listed under an H2 'My templates'.
requirements.why: The design's heading for the list.

requirements.statement: Above the template cards a results count reads 'Show 1-N of N results' for N templates, or 'Show 0 of 0 results' with none; every template is listed on one page with no pagination control.
requirements.why: The design's results count; it shows no paging.

requirements.statement: Manage templates has a 'Sort by:' select named sort with the options 'Select one' (empty value), 'Newest first', 'Oldest first' and 'Arrival date', preselecting the option that matches the sort value in the address, outside any form and with no apply button; as in Design Release 2.1, choosing an option does not reorder the list.
requirements.why: The design shows the select and never makes it reorder anything; the prototype wins, and neither a DR1 judgement on this list nor a real constraint justifies departing from it (c-185).

requirements.statement: Manage templates has no filter or search, and no empty-state message: with no templates it shows the results count and an empty list.
requirements.why: The design has none of these; the prototype shows only the count when the list is empty.

requirements.statement: The templates list shows the user's saved templates newest saved first, leaving out any template that has been deleted.
requirements.why: The design's list order: a template just saved appears at the top.

requirements.statement: Each template is a card labelled 'Template <title>' that shows the template's category label above the template title, which is an H3.
requirements.why: The design's template card.

requirements.statement: Each template card has a 'View template' link to /templates/<id> and a 'Use template' link to /templates/<id>/use.
requirements.why: The card's two actions in the design.

requirements.statement: Each template card lists, in this order, Commodity (the commodity common names), Origin (the country of origin), Consignee (the consignee's name) and Consignor (the consignor's name), each reading 'Not applicable' when the template has no answer.
requirements.why: The design summarises a template by these four answers so a user can tell templates apart.

requirements.statement: A template's category is 'Germinal products' when its notification holds only germinal products, and 'Live animals' otherwise.
requirements.why: The design labels each template card with its category.

requirements.statement: The templates pages render as the design does, built from GOV.UK Frontend components (summary cards for the template card and the answer cards, the standard caption, heading, input, button and button group) where the prototype wraps them in custom app-dr2-* and app-view-template-page blocks.
requirements.why: The prototype's custom blocks are its own scaffolding; the real services stay inside the GOV.UK Frontend toolbox while matching what users see.

requirements.statement: A success message on Manage templates shows as a GOV.UK success notification banner (role alert) titled 'Success' with the message as its heading, shown once; it does not dismiss itself and stays until the trader leaves or reloads the page.
requirements.why: The design confirms saves and deletions this way; its 5-second auto-dismiss gives way to the accessibility duty (c-006).

requirements.statement: Saving a template shows the banner '<template title> saved to templates' on Manage templates.
requirements.why: The design's confirmation that the template was saved.

requirements.statement: Deleting a template shows the banner '<template title> has been deleted' on Manage templates.
requirements.why: The design's confirmation that the template was deleted.

requirements.statement: Templates are stored by the backend and kept between sessions: a user's list holds only templates really saved, with no seeded example templates.
requirements.why: The prototype keeps templates in the browser session with five seeded examples because it cannot persist; persistence is a real constraint the ruling lets override the prototype.

requirements.statement: A saved template is private to the signed-in user who saved it: it is stored against their user id and organisation and listed under 'My templates', and nobody else sees, uses, changes or deletes it.
requirements.why: The prototype keeps saved templates to the user who made them under 'My templates'; real persistence and sign-in only replace its session with a store keyed to that user (c-184).

requirements.statement: Opening a template that does not exist or has been deleted, on its view, change, use, edit or delete address, redirects to Manage templates.
requirements.why: The design never shows an error page for a missing template.

requirements.statement: 'Create new template' clears any notification in progress, starts template creation and sends the user to the notification type question first; the journey then runs notification type, Enter template name, then the notification questions from Origin of the import.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks the type before the name so the template's questions fit its type.

requirements.statement: In template creation the notification type page asks 'What are you importing?' under the caption 'About the consignment', with radios (name notificationType) offering the same options as the create journey's type question (Live animals, Plants for planting, Potatoes (seed and ware) and Wood products), none preselected, and a 'Continue' button that leads to the template name page; its back link goes to Manage templates and it shows no 'Template' caption yet. Submitting it with no choice shows the page's usual error.
requirements.why: The design's first step of a new template; it offers the same options as the create question, so Germinal products is left off until a real service takes it (c-007). The template-mode error state is not shown, so the notification journey's own error applies.

requirements.statement: The template name page at /templates/create has the caption 'Create a new template', the H1 'Enter template name' and the page title 'Enter template name - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: The design's template name page.

requirements.statement: The template name page has one text input, templateName, labelled by the H1 with a visually hidden label 'Enter template name', and no hint.
requirements.why: The design's single question on the page.

requirements.statement: The template name is optional and unvalidated: the form posts with browser validation off, and a blank name moves on to Origin of the import with no error; there is no length, character or duplicate-name rule.
requirements.why: The design accepts any name, including none.

requirements.statement: A template saved with no name is titled 'Untitled template': the banner reads 'Untitled template saved to templates' and it is listed first with every card field 'Not applicable' when nothing was answered.
requirements.why: The design's fallback name for an unnamed template.

requirements.statement: The template name page has a 'Save and continue' button and a 'Cancel and return to manage templates' link to /templates.
requirements.why: The design's actions on the name page.

requirements.statement: The template name page's back link goes to the notification type page when a type has been chosen, and to Manage templates otherwise.
requirements.why: The design's back navigation from the name page.

requirements.statement: The template name field is prefilled with the name already entered only while the user is part way through creating that template, and is otherwise empty; a saved template's name cannot be changed afterwards.
requirements.why: The design sets the name only at creation and offers no rename.

requirements.statement: Submitting the template name trims it, starts a fresh draft in template-creation mode that keeps the chosen notification type, and opens Origin of the import.
requirements.why: The design's hand-off from the name page into the template's questions.

requirements.statement: A template is answered on the same question pages as a notification, with the same questions, hints and guidance (for example the origin page's country search, region of origin and internal reference, and the commodity page's ITAHC guidance and trade tariff link), each page in template mode showing a 'Template' caption with the template name above the section caption.
requirements.why: The design reuses the notification questions for templates and marks them as a template.

requirements.statement: While a new template is being created, Origin of the import shows the 'Template' caption and name and the caption 'About the consignment', offers only 'Save and continue' (no Cancel link), and its back link returns to /templates/create.
requirements.why: The design's first question page in template creation.

requirements.statement: While a new template is being created, 'What are you importing?' shows the 'Template' caption and name, has a back link to the origin page, and offers 'Save and continue', 'Save and return to overview' and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link to the template's task list.
requirements.why: The design's commodity page actions in template creation.

requirements.statement: In template mode, saving 'What are you importing?' returns to the template's task list instead of going on to the main import reason.
requirements.why: The design lets the user choose which template sections to fill from the task list.

requirements.statement: While a template is being created, the status strip on its task list and question pages shows a grey 'Template' tag followed by the template's name, in place of the draft status and notification reference.
requirements.why: The design marks the task list as a template's.

requirements.statement: A template's task list is headed 'Template tasklist' instead of 'Notification tasklist', and keeps the 'Overview' H1 and the 'Your commodities' figures for animals and packages (0 and 0 before any are entered).
requirements.why: The design's template task list heading and overview.

requirements.statement: A template's task list has five sections and no Documents section or 'Upload documents' task: '1. About the consignment', '2. Description of the goods', '3. Transport and arrival', '4. Consignment parties' and '5. Contact address'.
requirements.why: Documents are specific to one consignment, so the design leaves them out of templates.

requirements.statement: A template's tasks are: Where is this consignment coming from?, What are you importing?, Main import reason, Commodity details, Identification details, Additional details, Arrival details, Transport details, Roles and addresses (hint 'Consignor or Exporter, Consignee, Importer and Place of Destination') and Contact address for this consignment, each linking to its question page with ?from=hub.
requirements.why: The design's template task list.

requirements.statement: Each task on a template's task list shows a status tag: green 'Complete' when answered, blue 'To do' otherwise.
requirements.why: The design shows the user which template sections are filled.

requirements.statement: A template's task list ends with a primary 'Review template' button to the review page and a secondary 'Return to manage templates' button to /templates, in place of 'Review and submit' and 'Return to dashboard'.
requirements.why: The design's template task list actions.

requirements.statement: While a template is being created, the journey skips the upload documents and declaration steps: opening Upload documents redirects to the template's task list, and opening or posting the declaration, or opening the submitted page, redirects to the template review without submitting anything.
requirements.why: A template has no documents and no declaration.

requirements.statement: The template review's back link returns to the template's task list.
requirements.why: The design's back navigation from the template review.

requirements.statement: The template review's Change links go straight to the question pages (for example /origin-of-the-import, /contact-address-for-consignment?from=review), not to /templates/<id>/change/... as on a saved template.
requirements.why: During creation the template is still a draft being reviewed.

requirements.statement: 'Save template' saves the template, even with only some sections answered, and returns to Manage templates with the new template first in the list and the count one higher.
requirements.why: The design lets a user save a partial template.

requirements.statement: Saving a template that is being edited overwrites it, keeping its id, and moves it to the top of the list rather than adding a copy.
requirements.why: The design updates a template in place.

requirements.statement: A new template's id, used in its addresses, is its title in lower case with every run of other characters replaced by a hyphen ('template' if nothing is left), with -2, -3 and on added when the user already has that id.
requirements.why: The design's readable template addresses, such as /templates/arena-aintree.

requirements.statement: A template's date created is set to the day it is saved, and is reset each time it is saved again after a change.
requirements.why: The design shows this date on the template page and updates it on every save.

requirements.statement: A template saves the notification's country and region of origin, internal reference, commodity codes, common names and species, reason for import, purpose in the market, certified for, unweaned animals, storage temperature, animal and package totals and per-species numbers, commodity selections, net weight, package type, animal identification details, port of entry, means of transport, transport identification, transport document reference, the transporter's name, address, country, approval number and type, and the CPH number.
requirements.why: These are the answers the design carries from one consignment to the next.

requirements.statement: A template never holds an arrival date or time, including after a section of an existing template is changed and saved.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 leaves the arrival date out of templates because it differs for every consignment.

requirements.statement: A template saves the place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination and contact address each as answered, shows them on the template page's Addresses card (Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer, Place of destination) and Contact address card as the design renders them, and seeds each back into a notification started from it; the contact address falls back to the place of origin where none was chosen, as the design does.
requirements.why: The real notification persists the parties separately and sends each downstream as its own party, so the prototype's shortcut of copying the place of origin into every party would name the overseas place of origin as the GB consignee, importer and destination: a cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express (c-186).

requirements.statement: The template page at /templates/<id> has the caption 'Templates' above the template's title, which is its H1 and its page title ('<template name> - Import notification service - GOV.UK').
requirements.why: The design's page for one saved template.

requirements.statement: The template page shows 'Date created: <d Month yyyy>' with the template's date created.
requirements.why: The design shows when the template was last saved.

requirements.statement: The template page has a primary 'Use template' button to /templates/<id>/use and a red warning 'Delete' button to /templates/<id>/delete.
requirements.why: The design's actions on a saved template.

requirements.statement: The template page's back link goes to Manage templates.
requirements.why: The design's back navigation from a template.

requirements.statement: The template page has no Edit button or link; the whole-template edit address is reachable only directly.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows no edit action on the template page; sections are changed through their Change links.

requirements.statement: The template page lists the template's answers in the same cards as the notification review, in five numbered sections, '1. About the consignment' (Origin of import, What are you importing?, Main import reason), '2. Description of the goods' (a card per commodity '<common name> (<code>)' with species, Number of animals, Number of packages (when required), the identification details table, and an Additional details card), '3. Transport and arrival' (Arrival details and Transport details), '4. Consignment addresses' and '5. Contact address', with no documents section and a Change link on every card.
requirements.why: The design lets the user check everything a template holds before using it.

requirements.statement: On the template page the Change links go to /templates/<id>/change/<section> for origin-of-the-import, what-are-you-importing, reason-for-import, consignment-details (card header and number-of-animals row), animal-identification-details, additional-animal-details, arrival-details, transporter, roles-and-addresses and contact-address-for-consignment.
requirements.why: The design changes one section of a saved template at a time.

requirements.statement: A success message on the template page shows as a success banner titled 'Success', shown once and staying until the trader leaves or reloads the page; opening the template page abandons any half-finished change to a template.
requirements.why: The design's confirmation of a change, and its way of leaving an unfinished change; its 5-second auto-dismiss gives way to the accessibility duty (c-006).

requirements.statement: Posting to a template's page (/templates/<id>) changes nothing and redirects back to that page.
requirements.why: The prototype answers a post to the page this way, and the specs assert it.

requirements.statement: Following a template's Change link starts a draft seeded from the template in template-editing mode and redirects to that section's question page with ?from=template-review.
requirements.why: The design changes a saved template on the ordinary question pages.

requirements.statement: A Change address for a section that is not one of the template's sections redirects back to the template page.
requirements.why: Only the listed sections can be changed on a template.

requirements.statement: When changing a template section from its page or review, each journey page's only submit button is 'Save and return', beside a 'Cancel' link back to that template's page; this ending takes precedence over the amend ending.
requirements.why: The design's actions when changing one section of a saved template.

requirements.statement: When changing a template section, the question page's back link returns to the template page.
requirements.why: The design's back navigation when changing a template.

requirements.statement: When changing a template section, the question page is prefilled with the template's answers and can be edited; an unanswered optional field is empty, 'Not applicable' being only how the template page shows it.
requirements.why: The design edits the template's existing answers.

requirements.statement: Saving a changed template section saves the template, never a draft notification, and returns to the template's page, which shows the new answer and a success banner headed '<template name> has been updated' ('Template has been updated' when the template has no name); this holds for every section, not only the origin section the traces follow.
requirements.why: The design's confirmation that a template change was saved.

requirements.statement: Opening /templates/<id>/edit starts a draft seeded from the template in template-creation mode and opens the template's task list.
requirements.why: The design's whole-template edit, which reuses the template task list and review.

requirements.statement: Using a template clears any notification in progress, creates and saves a new draft notification seeded from the template, and opens its task list headed 'Notification tasklist' with the status 'Draft' and a new notification reference made the same way as for any new notification.
requirements.why: Using a template is the design's quick way to start a notification from saved answers.

requirements.statement: A notification started from a template uses the normal six-section notification task list, including '4. Documents' and '5. Consignment parties', ending with 'Review and submit' and 'Return to dashboard'.
requirements.why: Once started, it is an ordinary notification.

requirements.statement: The overview of a notification started from a template shows the template's animal and package totals under 'Your commodities'.
requirements.why: The template's numbers carry over.

requirements.statement: A notification started from a template records the template's id and title, but nothing on its task list says which template it came from.
requirements.why: The design keeps the link without showing it.

requirements.statement: Using a template seeds the country of origin, the region of origin ('Yes' with the code when the template has one, 'No' when it does not) and the internal reference (blank when the template has none).
requirements.why: The origin answers carry over.

requirements.statement: Using a template selects the template's commodities and species, sets the notification type from its category, and seeds the commodity selections, animal and package numbers per species, net weight, package type and animal identification details it holds.
requirements.why: The goods answers carry over.

requirements.statement: Using a template seeds the main reason for import, the purpose in the internal market only when the reason is 'Internal market', 'certified for' when the template's value is a valid option (otherwise 'Further keeping'), the storage temperature only when it is a germinal product temperature option, and the unweaned animals answer when valid for the species ('No' when the species have unweaned options and the template has none).
requirements.why: The reason and additional details carry over, falling back to valid answers.

requirements.statement: Using a template seeds the CPH number, port of entry, means of transport, transport identification and transport document reference; it leaves the arrival date empty, so Arrival details and Upload documents show 'To do' on the new notification.
requirements.why: The transport answers carry over; the arrival date and documents are new for every consignment.

requirements.statement: Using a template seeds the transporter's name, address, approval number, type and country into the new notification.
requirements.why: The design saves and shows the transporter's country and, after a template is used, shows the same country again, worked out from the seeded approval number; the real service stores the country as an answer and a private transporter has no approval number, so it carries the saved country across to give the same result (c-187).

requirements.statement: Using a template seeds no documents and starts the notification with no validation errors.
requirements.why: Documents are never part of a template.

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation for a saved template is at /templates/<id>/delete, with the H1 'Delete this template?' and the page title 'Delete this template? - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: The design asks before a template is deleted.

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation shows a one-row summary list keyed 'Name' holding the template's title.
requirements.why: The design names the template being deleted.

requirements.statement: Under the summary the delete confirmation says 'Confirm that you want to delete this template.' and 'This action cannot be undone.'
requirements.why: The design's warning copy.

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation has a red warning 'Yes, delete' button that posts the deletion and a 'No, cancel' link back to the template page, in a GOV.UK button group.
requirements.why: The design's confirm and cancel actions.

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation's back link goes to the template page.
requirements.why: The design's back navigation from the delete confirmation.

requirements.statement: The delete and discard confirmations use the journey layout, not the dashboard layout.
requirements.why: The design renders the confirmation as a journey page.

requirements.statement: Confirming 'Yes, delete' removes the template and returns to Manage templates with the '<title> has been deleted' banner and one template fewer in the count.
requirements.why: The design's result of deleting a template.

requirements.statement: A template being created can be discarded at /templates/discard, which shows the same 'Delete this template?' page and copy, with the Name row holding the name entered ('this template' when none), and a back link and 'No, cancel' link to the template review, and a 'Yes, delete' button posting to /templates/discard.
requirements.why: The design lets a user throw away a template before saving it.

requirements.statement: The discard page is shown only while a template is being created; otherwise opening it redirects to Manage templates, and posting to it changes nothing and returns to Manage templates.
requirements.why: There is nothing to discard outside template creation.

requirements.statement: Confirming discard throws the template away unsaved and returns to Manage templates, list unchanged, with the banner '<template name> has been deleted', or 'Template has been deleted' when no name was entered.
requirements.why: The design's result of discarding a template.

requirements.statement: The prototype's /design-release-2.1 mount and its rule sending anyone not in a Design Release 2 or 2.1 session to the start page are not built; the real services serve the templates pages at their own paths behind their own sign-in.
requirements.why: Version mounting and design-release sessions are prototype mechanics, not part of the design.

requirements.statement: The 'Cancel' link on a template's change page pointing to /templates/<id> without the release prefix is not reproduced; Cancel goes to the template page.
requirements.why: A prototype path slip, not part of the design; req-1358 builds the working Cancel link.

requirements.statement: The prototype's unguarded discard post, which clears any notification in progress and shows a 'has been deleted' banner even when no template is being created, is not reproduced.
requirements.why: A prototype defect, not part of the design; req-1381 guards the post.

requirements.statement: The seeded Arena Aintree region code changing from 'ROI-092032' to 'IE-092032' on re-save is not a templates behaviour to build: it comes from seeded data no real service holds.
requirements.why: Seeded templates are not built (c-183); the region code form belongs to the origin page.

requirements.statement: The prototype's session-only storage and its five seeded templates (Arena Aintree, Rice Lane City Farm, Monk Park Farm, Acorn Farm and Glen Keen Farm, with their answers and the '15 April 2026' fallback date) are not built.
requirements.why: Persistence is a real constraint the prototype cannot express (c-183): real users see only templates they saved.

requirements.statement: Saving a template by a GET to /templates/save is not built: a template is saved only by the 'Save template' form post from the review page.
requirements.why: A state-changing GET bypasses the services' request forgery protection, a real constraint the prototype cannot express (c-188).

requirements.statement: 'Amend this notification' does not leave the page: it opens a confirmation dialog headed 'Amend notification' (a level-1 heading) that asks 'Are you sure you want to change this notification?'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks the trader to confirm before reopening a submitted notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the dashboard card's Amend posts straight away with no confirmation (trace-animals-fit-p3-027).

requirements.statement: The amend dialog's 'Yes, continue' button starts the amendment; its 'No, go back' link-styled button closes the dialog and leaves the trader on the view page, from where 'Amend this notification' can reopen it.
requirements.why: The trader confirms or backs out of amending without losing their place.

requirements.statement: The amend and cancel-amendment dialogs are hidden until opened, are modal dialogs (role dialog, aria-modal) labelled by their heading (the amend dialog also described by its question), and each has a Close (X) button labelled 'Close' for screen readers and an overlay; the Close button, the overlay and the dialog's 'go back' button all dismiss it without acting.
requirements.why: A dialog must be announced and dismissable for keyboard and screen-reader users.

requirements.statement: Confirming an amendment, from the view page or the dashboard card's Amend, takes the trader to the notification's review page (the amend review), not to its overview hub.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 opens an amendment on the review page so the trader sees every answer and its Change link at once.
requirements.deltaNote: Today Amend posts to /notifications/{id}/amend and redirects to the overview hub showing 'Amending' (trace-animals-fit-p3-027, trace-e2e-p14-053, repo-tests-p4-098); the review page is one step further, behind Review and submit (trace-animals-fit-p3-031).

requirements.statement: Amending moves a SUBMITTED notification to AMEND, keeps its reference and original submitted time, stores a full independent snapshot of the submitted content and fulfilments, and records a NotificationAmendmentRequested event carrying the status history and the actor; an unknown reference gets 404 and any status but SUBMITTED gets 400.
requirements.why: The submitted version must survive the amendment so cancelling can restore it and other services see the change.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend amend endpoint already does this (repo-backend-p2-090, repo-backend-p2-094, repo-backend-p2-098), proven end to end (trace-e2e-p14-070).

requirements.statement: Answers changed during an amendment are saved to the notification record (status stays AMEND) as the trader goes, and are not visible as the submitted version until resubmitted.
requirements.why: The real service persists every save; the prototype's session-only amendment cannot express persistence.
requirements.deltaNote: Saving keeps a notification in AMEND (repo-backend-p2-111), and a changed value survives leaving the cancel page (trace-animals-fit-p3-042).

requirements.statement: A notification being amended shows the status tag 'Amend'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the state 'Amend'.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the tag reads 'Amending' (yellow) on the hub, review and cancel pages (trace-animals-fit-p3-029, trace-e2e-p14-031).

requirements.statement: During an amendment, the review page and every question page show an Amend status bar above the caption and heading: the 'Amend' tag, the reference, and a link-styled 'Cancel amend' button that opens the cancel-amendment dialog. Whether the hub's own status line carries it is req-782's question.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader abandon the amendment from wherever they are in it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a 'Cancel amendment' link sits under the review page heading only; the hub and question pages offer no way to cancel (trace-animals-fit-p3-032, trace-animals-fit-p3-029-m1, trace-e2e-p14-055).

requirements.statement: The amend review has no page-header actions (no Amend this notification, no Copy as new), no Import reference numbers section and no Date submitted line.
requirements.why: During an amendment the status bar replaces the view page's header.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's amending view shows no Copy as new or Delete under its heading (trace-e2e-p14-032-m1) and has no Import reference numbers section or Date submitted line.

requirements.statement: The amend review is editable, with a Change link on every card (the first going to the origin of the import), and its Back link goes to the notification's overview hub.
requirements.why: Amending means changing the submitted answers.
requirements.deltaNote: The amending review already has Change links on every card and a Back link to the hub (trace-e2e-p14-032, trace-animals-fit-p3-034).

requirements.statement: While a submitted notification is being amended, each page the overview links to, including a question page opened from the amend review, ends with a primary 'Save and return' button that saves and goes to the amend review (which shows the changed answer), a secondary 'Save and continue' button that saves and goes to the next page, and a link-styled 'Save and return to overview' button, with no cancel link; the posted action values are review, continue and hub. The party pickers, the CPH number page and the permanent address page, which DR1 rule (b) keeps to the primary button outside amend, show 'Save and return' and 'Save and continue' only, without 'Save and return to overview'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader return to the review straight after a change, or carry on.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a Change link opens the question with ?change=1 and saving returns to the notification view with no choice of where to go (trace-e2e-p14-047, repo-tests-p3-079).

requirements.statement: During an amendment, question pages keep the journey's usual Back links (the origin of the import back to the notification type page, arrival details back to the overview hub), not a link to the amend review.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 does not change Back links for an amendment.

requirements.statement: During an amendment, question pages are prefilled with the notification's saved answers and keep their usual copy (for example Arrival details: arrival date at port of entry with a d/m/yyyy date picker, port of entry search, means of transport, transport identification and document reference).
requirements.why: The trader changes only what needs changing.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a Change link during an amendment opens the question with the saved answers (repo-tests-p3-079, trace-e2e-p14-046).

requirements.statement: Continue on the amend review is held while any answer is invalid or incomplete (such as an arrival date outside 7 days back to 6 months ahead): the trader stays on the amend review and, as Design Release 2.1 draws it, no error summary or error message is shown. The draft review's error summary is not carried over to the amend review.
requirements.why: A resubmitted amendment must be complete and valid, and the hold itself meets that constraint; Design Release 2.1 draws the refused Continue as a silent hold and DR1 judged nothing about the amend review, so the prototype wins (c-201).

requirements.statement: Continue on a valid amend review goes to the Declaration page; ticking the declaration and pressing Continue resubmits the amendment.

requirements.statement: Confirming the cancellation discards every edit made during the amendment, restores the submitted content and fulfilments, returns the notification to SUBMITTED with its original submitted time, records one NotificationAmendmentCancelled event, and takes the trader to that notification's view page, read only and showing Submitted.

requirements.statement: Opening or posting cancel amendment for a notification that is not being amended changes nothing and returns the trader to the overall dashboard with no message.

requirements.deltaNote: Today a Submitted notification is redirected to its view page, and any other status to the live-animals dashboard (repo-frontend-p3-079, repo-frontend-p3-087).

requirements.statement: When copy as new, cancel amendment or delete fails to save, the page the trader came from is shown again with HTTP 500 and the recoverable-error banner.

requirements.statement: Copy as new goes straight, with no confirmation, to the new draft's overview hub titled 'Overview', which has no Back link and no banner announcing the copy.

requirements.statement: A copy is a new notification saved at once as a Draft, with its own new reference (same GBN-AG prefix, fresh suffix); the source is unchanged, the copy is independent of it, every copy is distinct, and a NotificationCreated event (carrying the acting user's organisation id to resolve address-book parties) is recorded for the copy only.

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the origin of the import: country of origin, whether a region of origin code is required, and the region of origin code with its suffix.

requirements.deltaNote: The copy mapper keeps them (repo-backend-p2-047) and the copy's origin page comes back prefilled (trace-animals-fit-p2-078).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the internal reference number, in the notification record as well as on the page.

requirements.statement: A copy carries over what is being imported: the commodity (id, code and name), the commodity selections, the selected species and the notification type (worked out from the copied answers when missing).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the main reason for import and its follow-ups: internal market purpose, transhipment destination country, transit exit border control post, transit destination country, and the temporary admission exit date and port of exit.

requirements.statement: Copying a notification that is being amended copies its submitted version, not the edits in progress.

requirements.statement: Copy as new is checked against the version the trader was looking at: if the notification changed since, nothing is copied and the trader returns to where they started (the dashboard or the notification's view page) with the 'The notification has been updated' banner. A stale copy from the view page must land on the view page, not on a missing check-answers page.
requirements.why: A trader must never copy content different from what they saw; the prototype cannot express concurrent edits.
requirements.deltaNote: The token check and banner exist (repo-frontend-p3-074, repo-backend-p2-040), but a stale copy started from the view page redirects to /notifications/{id}/check-answers?staleAction=1, which no route serves (repo-frontend-p3-075-m1).

requirements.statement: A notification being amended can be deleted (from the amend review's Delete button), and the backend's soft-delete API description says DRAFT, SUBMITTED and AMEND notifications can be deleted.

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation page identifies the notification in a GOV.UK summary list with the rows 'Reference number', 'Commodity', 'Number' and 'Origin' (the country of origin).
requirements.why: The trader confirms they are deleting the right notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the delete page has only a heading, one sentence and two buttons (repo-frontend-p3-092, repo-frontend-p3-093).

requirements.statement: The delete page's Commodity row lists each commodity's common name with its species' Latin names in brackets, comma-separated (for example 'Sheep (Ovis Aries), Goat (Capra Hircus)'); for other live mammals each species' common name is used.

requirements.statement: The delete page's Number row shows the total number of packages for a germinal-products-only notification, and otherwise the total number of animals.

requirements.statement: A delete page summary row with no value from the notification falls back to what the dashboard lists for it, and shows 'Not applicable' when that is empty too.
requirements.why: Every row shows something, even for an early draft.

requirements.statement: Below the summary the delete page says 'Confirm that you want to delete this notification.'

requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's button wording.
requirements.deltaNote: Today it reads 'Yes, delete notification' (repo-frontend-p3-095, trace-animals-fit-p3-008).

requirements.statement: Beside 'Yes, delete' the delete page has a plain link 'No, cancel' in the button group, replacing the secondary button 'No, return to dashboard'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording and pattern for not deleting.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the way back is a secondary button-styled link 'No, return to dashboard' (repo-frontend-p3-096, trace-animals-fit-p3-009).

requirements.statement: The delete page's Back link and 'No, cancel' both return to the notification's view page.

requirements.deltaNote: Today both go to the dashboard (repo-frontend-p3-097, trace-animals-fit-p3-010, trace-e2e-p3-063).

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation page shows no journey strip (status tag and reference) above its heading; the summary list identifies the notification instead.

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation page is titled 'Delete this notification? - Import notification service - GOV.UK' with the level-1 heading 'Delete this notification?', serves every deletable status, and can be opened directly by its address.

requirements.statement: Confirming the delete (a POST with the CSRF crumb) soft-deletes the notification: its status becomes DELETED and the record is kept; a repeat is a harmless no-op; a NotificationDeleted (draft) or NotificationSubmissionDeleted (submitted or amending) event is recorded with the actor and organisation id; an unknown reference gets 404.

requirements.deltaNote: Delete already soft-deletes through the backend, idempotently, with the events (repo-backend-p3-033, repo-backend-p3-036, repo-backend-p3-040, trace-e2e-p14-078).

requirements.statement: After 'Yes, delete' the trader lands on the overall dashboard, which shows no banner.

requirements.deltaNote: Today the trader lands on the live-animals dashboard at /live-animals?deleted=1 with a banner (repo-frontend-p3-099, trace-e2e-p3-066).

requirements.statement: The deletion success message reads '<reference> has been deleted' (or 'Notification has been deleted' when the reference is not known), and appears on the live-animals notification list the next time the trader opens it.

requirements.deltaNote: Today the banner reads 'The notification has been deleted.' straight after the delete (trace-animals-fit-p3-018, trace-e2e-p3-068).

requirements.statement: A deleted notification no longer appears in the notification list, and searching for its reference finds nothing.
requirements.why: Deleted notifications are gone from the trader's view.
requirements.deltaNote: The deleted notification already disappears from the dashboard and its search (trace-animals-fit-p3-020, trace-e2e-p3-072).

requirements.statement: Opening or posting delete for a notification the trader cannot reach (unknown reference, or a status that cannot be deleted) changes nothing and returns to the overall dashboard with no message.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 guards the route; the real service must also check the record exists, which the prototype's POST does not.
requirements.deltaNote: Delete already refuses an unknown or non-deletable notification and returns to the dashboard with no banner (repo-frontend-p3-100, repo-frontend-p3-101); which dashboard follows c-198.

requirements.statement: The view page shows the notification's answers in the same six numbered sections and cards as the review page (1. About the consignment to 6. Contact address); the card contents follow the review page's requirements.
requirements.why: One rendering of a notification's answers serves review and view.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's notification view already renders the review page's six numbered sections (trace-animals-fit-p3-051); differences inside the cards are carried by the review page's requirements.

requirements.statement: The backend notification API supports the lifecycle: create gives DRAFT with a minted reference; save keeps DRAFT or AMEND; submit takes DRAFT or AMEND to SUBMITTED and stamps submittedAt; amend takes SUBMITTED to AMEND; cancel-amend takes AMEND back to SUBMITTED; copy reads DRAFT, SUBMITTED or AMEND and makes a new DRAFT; soft-delete makes DELETED. Each write advances the concurrency token, takes an optional actor, and callers from outside carry the API key.
requirements.why: Every action in this area rests on these transitions.
