requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 makes the number of packages a hard stop on that page alongside the number of animals.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the number of packages is asked only on lines whose commodity is on the package-count list and is optional there (repo-frontend-p2-063); the number of animals is already required (repo-tests-p2-015).

requirements.statement: The transit countries step, and its row on the overview, apply only when the means of transport is rail or road; choosing any other means skips the step, removes the row and deletes any saved transit countries. Transit countries are optional to proceed.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 adds the transit countries step only for Rail or Road. The real journey already does this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p2-025 to p2-029: the transit countries page is routed only for rail or road, and changing the means skips it, removes the row and wipes saved countries.

requirements.statement: The animal identification step follows commodity details only when at least one chosen species has identifiers of its own; a consignment with none never reaches the identification page, and a commodity with none gets no panel on it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 adds the identification step only when a selected species has identifier fields. The real journey already does this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p2-014: when no commodity has an identifier type the identification page is never shown; repo-tests-p2-012: a commodity with none gets no panel.

requirements.statement: The additional details step applies to every live-animals consignment because it always asks what the animals are certified for; its unweaned animals question appears only when a commodity line is one that triggers it, such as cattle.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 adds the additional details page whenever it would ask the certification purpose or the unweaned question, and live animals are always asked the purpose. The real journey already does this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p2-034 and repo-tests-p2-035: Additional details always asks the certified-for question, and the unweaned question shows only once a triggering commodity line exists.

requirements.statement: The CPH number applies unless every commodity in the consignment is exempt (horses 0101, and cats, dogs and ferrets 01061900); for cats, dogs and ferrets each animal's permanent address is asked instead of a CPH number.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 brings the CPH number in by commodity code with the same exemptions, and asks a cat's permanent address in its place. The real journey already scopes it this way.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-107 and repo-tests-p2-038: CPH is asked except for exempt codes 0101 and 01061900, and a cats-only consignment shows no CPH row; repo-frontend-p2-108: those codes ask a permanent address instead.

requirements.statement: Each reason for import brings in only its own follow-up questions, revealed on the same page: the purpose for internal market; the exit port and destination country for transit; the destination country for transhipment or onward travel; the exit date and port of exit for temporary admission of horses. Changing the reason deletes the follow-up answers that no longer apply.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 requires a reason's follow-ups once that reason is chosen and walks each branch this way. The real journey already scopes them like this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p2-062, p2-064 and p2-067: Internal market reveals the purpose, Transit reveals the exit details, and changing the reason wipes the saved purpose; repo-frontend-p2-029 to p2-032 scope the destination country, port of exit and exit date.

requirements.statement: Only the transporter details that match the chosen transporter type are kept: switching between commercial and private deletes the other type's details.
requirements.why: Keeping one consistent transporter record is a real persistence constraint the prototype cannot express. The real journey already does this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p2-051 and repo-tests-p2-057: switching the transporter type wipes the other type's saved details.

requirements.statement: An answer to a question that no longer applies is not shown, checked or saved, and any stored value is removed in the same save; when one field of a collection entry leaves scope only that field is wiped.
requirements.why: The real service must not store answers the notification no longer needs: a real persistence and validation constraint that holds whatever the prototype shows.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-143: a conditional field that is out of scope is not shown, validated or saved, and any stored value is removed when it leaves scope.

requirements.statement: A notification's arrival date counts as complete only when it falls between 7 days in the past and 6 months ahead.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 holds the arrival details task back outside that window. The real journey already applies the same window.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p2-075 and trace-e2e-p14-111: the arrival date must fall between one week ago and six months ahead.

requirements.statement: Each journey page carries the caption of the part of the notification it belongs to: 'About the consignment' (origin, what are you importing, main reason for import, identification), 'Commodity details' (additional details), 'Transport and arrival' (arrival details, transporter), 'Movement' (transit countries), 'Add a new transporter' (the add-a-transporter pages), 'Documents' (upload documents) and 'Consignment parties' (roles and addresses, party pickers, CPH number); the overview, contact address, review, declaration and confirmation pages carry none.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's pages carry these captions. The real journey already captions them the same way, except commodity details.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p1-069: the walked pages carry these captions; trace-animals-fit-p1-071: the contact address and review pages carry none.

requirements.statement: The tests repo walks a cattle-by-air notification (identification, the unweaned question and a CPH number) from create to submitted in the Design Release 2.1 step order, checks every overview task reads Complete before review, and checks the review shows the answers given.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 proves this journey end to end. The real suite proves a cattle journey by road in today's step order, which the step-order changes will break.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the full UI journey answers a Bos taurus consignment by road vehicle with transit through France and Belgium, in today's order (repo-tests-p1-166, trace-animals-fit-p1-094), and submits through review and declaration (repo-tests-p2-138).

requirements.statement: A poultry-by-rail notification (Chicken 010511 Gallus domesticus, Transit with an exit port and destination country, transit countries and a CPH number, no identification step) can be walked from create to submitted, and the tests repo proves it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 proves this journey end to end. Today the commodity list offers only Cow, Horse, Cat, Dog and Fish, so poultry cannot be chosen.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the commodity picker offers five commodities (repo-frontend-p2-082), all stub data in the frontend (repo-frontend-p2-112).

requirements.statement: A pet-cats-by-air notification (microchip, passport and tattoo per cat, a companion-animal purpose, and each cat's permanent address chosen on its own page in roles and addresses, one the same as the place of destination and one new) can be walked from create to submitted, and the tests repo proves it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 proves this journey end to end. Today the permanent address is typed in full on the identification form; conflict c-119 settles that it moves to its own page in roles and addresses now.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the cat's permanent address is part of its identifier form (repo-tests-p2-006, repo-tests-p2-010).

requirements.statement: A horse-by-sea notification (temporary admission of horses with an exit date and port of exit, microchip, passport and horse name, a registered equine animal) can be walked from create to submitted, and the tests repo proves it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 proves this journey end to end; no real end-to-end journey walks a horse or temporary admission today.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the journey offers Horse (repo-frontend-p2-086) and the temporary admission horses reason (repo-frontend-p2-026), but no end-to-end test walks them.

requirements.statement: Every new or changed piece of user-facing text has a Welsh version, and the English and Welsh copy keep the same shape.
requirements.why: The real service is bilingual, a real constraint the English-only prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-115: all user-facing text exists in English and Welsh with the same shape.

requirements.statement: Journey changes keep the frontend's standing structure: the obligation model decides what applies and whether it is mandatory, the flow decides page order, task rows decide grouping on the overview, each answer is owned by exactly one page, and the model holds no display copy.
requirements.why: These are the real frontend's recorded rulings on how scope, order and grouping are kept apart; every flow change in this area lands through them.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-171: the model decides scope and mandatory or optional, the journey decides page order, task rows decide grouping.

requirements.statement: The service refuses to start when the journey is not fully configured (flow, obligations, bindings, cookies, field names), and the platform's limits hold: scope rules are code, a page's gate opens when one of its answers is in scope, saves are not transactional across backend projections, and collection positions are not durable ids.
requirements.why: These are real constraints of the platform every flow change runs on.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-090 and repo-frontend-p2-177 to p2-181: the boot-time completeness checks and the platform limits.

requirements.statement: Every changed page passes axe with no serious or critical WCAG 2 A or AA violation on first render and in its error state, and the audited pages keep their Lighthouse thresholds.
requirements.why: Accessibility is a real constraint of a GOV.UK service that the prototype does not check.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-162: every changed page is checked with axe on first render and in its validation-error state; repo-frontend-p2-166: the Lighthouse thresholds.

requirements.statement: A page with validation errors shows a GOV.UK error summary titled 'There is a problem' ('Mae problem' in Welsh) at the top of the content, above the caption and heading, listing one entry per field in field order with the first failing rule's message, each linking to its field. The summary is exposed as an alert and takes focus when the user has just been refused. Each field shows the same message inline, read out with a visually hidden 'Error:' prefix. A page with no errors shows no summary.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows every error this way. The real journey already does.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p2-009 and repo-tests-p2-047: errors show in a 'There is a problem' summary linking each message; repo-frontend-p2-145: each link moves focus to its field.

requirements.statement: Date fields take a date as d/m/yyyy with single-digit days and months allowed, through an MOJ date picker the user can also type into.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's date pickers work this way. The real journey already does.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-081 and trace-e2e-p14-110: a single d/m/yyyy text box with an MOJ date picker.

requirements.statement: The prototype's version mount and session mechanics are not built: the /design-release-2.1 base path, the per-version session nest and its shared keys, path prefixing, override-view fallback and the route and coverage tables that describe them.
requirements.why: They are how the prototype kit hosts several design releases side by side, not behaviour of the real services, which serve live animals under /live-animals and keep notifications and the address book in their own services.

requirements.statement: The prototype's seed shortcuts and fixtures are not built: the /prototype/reason-for-import seed route, the legacy /transport-details redirect, the design release index page, the fixed GBN-AG-26-7K8M2P reference and the seeded dashboard reference mapping, and the submitted view's fixed sample answers.
requirements.why: They exist to demo and test the prototype, not as service behaviour.

requirements.statement: The prototype's mount leaks are not copied: the template Cancel link, the transporter 'View details' links and the document virus check that leave /design-release-2.1 for the root paths.
requirements.why: They are defects of the prototype's version mount, with no counterpart in a service that has one set of paths.

requirements.statement: The germinal products, plants for planting, potatoes and wood products journeys are not built here: their reduced reasons, absent additional details page, per-species donor identification, package and weight totals, and GBN-GP references.
requirements.why: The goal covers the live-animals journey, its dashboard, templates and address book; the other notification types are separate journeys.

requirements.statement: What the Design Release 2.1 traces and specs do not exercise is recorded, not built: page validation before the declaration, the save and cancel return controls, amend, copy and delete, multi-commodity and mixed-species consignments, transhipment, the review's Change links, finished virus scans, the region code and package totals, no-JavaScript searches, and observed but unasserted behaviour such as a cattle animal with only an ear tag staying To do.
requirements.why: These are gaps in the target evidence; nothing in them says what to build differently.

requirements.statement: What today's traces and tests do not show is recorded, not built: backend calls behind the browser, real identity-provider sign-in, where the exits lead from a page in change mode, what the review's Continue leads to in the fit traces, 404 and error pages, no-JavaScript country and port selects, invalid input on 'Save and return to overview', copy as new, cancelling an amendment from the dashboard, the Railway means through the UI, and Change links from review cards other than import details and additional animal details.
requirements.why: These are gaps in the evidence of today's behaviour; each is weighed where its page is built.

requirements.statement: The tests repo's fixture data and seeding mechanics (default test notification, named parties, country and species constants, Yes/No values, field names posted by the seeder, address-book lookups by name) are test scaffolding, not requirements.
requirements.why: They describe how the suite drives the service, not what a user sees; they change only as the journeys they drive change.

requirements.statement: Log out ends the user's session with the service and sends them to Defra ID's sign-out page, headed 'You have signed out'. Opening the dashboard again afterwards asks them to sign in again with their user ID and password. A user who is not signed in and opens /auth/sign-out goes to the service root.
requirements.why: Ending a real session properly is an authentication behaviour the prototype cannot show. It already works and is proven end to end.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p1-041 to p1-046 show Log out reaching Defra ID's signed-out page and the dashboard asking for sign-in again; repo-insfrontend-p4-096 to p4-098 give the INS routes.

requirements.statement: The Manage account navigation item is a placeholder on both frontends: it links to '#', leads nowhere, and is never marked as the current item.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows Manage account as a placeholder with no destination, which is what both frontends do today.
requirements.deltaNote: Both frontends link Manage account to '#' (repo-frontend-p1-013, repo-insfrontend-p4-009, trace-e2e-p15-003), as the prototype does (trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-013).

requirements.statement: The first navigation item, Dashboard, links to the dashboard, which is the service's home, and is marked as the current item on the dashboard pages. On the animals frontend it also stays current on every page inside a notification. A back link that returns to the dashboard goes to that same dashboard home.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 the dashboard is the home: it is the Dashboard item's target and where the back link to the dashboard goes. Both frontends already work this way, each with its own dashboard.
requirements.deltaNote: The animals Dashboard item goes to /live-animals and stays current inside a notification (repo-frontend-p1-010, p1-011, trace-e2e-p9-083); the INS item goes to / and is current there (repo-insfrontend-p4-007). Which frontend owns the dashboard (Rhys's ruling moves it to INS, document-dr1-parity-notes-p1-014) is the dashboard area's to settle; the item follows it.

requirements.statement: The Address book navigation item takes the user to the INS frontend's address book at /address-book, and is marked as the current item on the address book and every page under it. From the animals frontend this is a link to the INS frontend's origin, and a user with no INS session goes through INS sign-in first.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 treats the address book as part of one service. In the real services it is a shared capability in the INS frontend, a cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: The animals item already links out to the INS /address-book (trace-e2e-p9-084), and the INS item goes to /address-book and is current under it (repo-insfrontend-p4-008, p4-013).

requirements.statement: The service navigation items appear only to a signed-in user; a signed-out page shows the service name with no items.
requirements.why: The navigation leads to pages that need a signed-in user. This is a real authentication constraint, and it already works.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-007 and repo-insfrontend-p4-005 hide the items when signed out.

requirements.statement: Every page uses the GOV.UK service navigation component, which shows the service name 'Import notification service' in the navigation bar rather than in the header. On narrow screens the items collapse behind a 'Menu' button, and the navigation landmark is named 'Menu'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the service 'Import notification service' and uses GOV.UK service navigation with the name in the bar. Both frontends already do this.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p1-016 and trace-e2e-p15-001 show the service navigation component carrying the name on both frontends.

requirements.statement: The GOV.UK header logo links to https://www.gov.uk/ on both frontends, and the service name in the service navigation links to that frontend's dashboard home: /live-animals on the animals frontend and / on the INS frontend.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sends both links to its index of design releases, prototype tooling with no counterpart in a real service (req-1681), so it names no real destination; with no DR1 judgement on the header links, the real frontends' targets are the only buildable ones and stand (c-214).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the logo links to https://www.gov.uk/ on both frontends (repo-frontend-p1-005, repo-insfrontend-p4-003), and the service name links to /live-animals on the animals frontend (repo-frontend-p1-006) and to / on the INS frontend (repo-insfrontend-p4-004).

requirements.statement: The prototype's service index at /index is not built: its 'Prototypes' caption, its introduction, its four release cards (Design release 1, Design release 2, Design release 2.1, Testing version) with tags, 'What the journey contains' details and start buttons, and its title without the GOV.UK suffix.
requirements.why: The index is the prototype's own way to choose between design releases. A real service has one live version, so the page has no purpose there. It is prototype tooling, not part of the service the goal brings into line.

requirements.statement: The prototype kit's tooling is not built: the footer's 'Manage your prototype' and 'Clear data' links, and the kit's absence of custom Nunjucks filters and default session data.
requirements.why: These belong to the prototype kit, not to the service the design describes.

requirements.statement: The phase banner's feedback link is an email link to APHAServiceDesk@apha.gov.uk on both frontends, not the prototype's placeholder '#', and no /feedback route or survey URL is invented for it.
requirements.why: DR1 already judged this same difference, a placeholder feedback link in the design: the real link goes to the APHA service desk. That judgement outranks the prototype default.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-017 and repo-insfrontend-p4-017 already mail APHAServiceDesk@apha.gov.uk. The service team has still to confirm that mailbox as the feedback destination (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p1-009); that is for the report, not a build.

requirements.statement: On the animals frontend, every page's browser title reads the page name, then 'Import notification service', then 'GOV.UK', joined by ' - '.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sets no title pattern for its journey pages, so the animals frontend's existing pattern stands.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-001 and trace-animals-fit-p1-001 show the pattern.

requirements.statement: On the INS frontend, every page's browser title reads the page's title, then 'Import notification service', then 'GOV.UK', joined by ' - ', as on the animals frontend.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses one title pattern on every page; the INS frontend's pipe pattern is today's build, not a constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the INS frontend's titles read 'X | Import notification service' (repo-insfrontend-p4-001, trace-e2e-p15-004).

requirements.statement: When a page shows an error summary, its browser title starts with 'Error: ' ('Gwall: ' in Welsh) in front of the whole title, on both frontends.
requirements.why: This is the GOV.UK pattern for telling screen-reader users there are errors, and it already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-002 and repo-insfrontend-p4-002 add the prefix.

requirements.statement: Page content sits in a two-thirds-width column by default, and a page that shows a table or other display content can use the full width.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lays journey pages out in a two-thirds column. Both frontends already default to it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-020 and repo-insfrontend-p4-019 default to two-thirds.

requirements.statement: A page shows a GOV.UK back link labelled 'Back' ('Yn ôl' in Welsh), below the phase banner, only when it supplies a back-link target. No page shows breadcrumbs.
requirements.why: Each page gets one route back (the back link) and one route up (the service navigation). This already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-019 and repo-insfrontend-p4-018 render the back link only when one is set.

requirements.statement: A journey page on the animals frontend names its section in a caption directly above its heading, such as 'About the consignment' above 'Main reason for import'. Where the question legend is visually hidden, the caption still sits directly above the page heading. The dashboard has an extra-large 'Dashboard' caption above its heading, and the overview has no caption.
requirements.why: Section captions already exist on the animals frontend. No source in this area's working set from Design Release 2.1 says otherwise.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p1-007 to p1-012 show the captions as rendered. Each page's own caption wording against Design Release 2.1 belongs to that page's area.

requirements.statement: Where a field's own copy gives no message, the shared default validation messages apply: 'Select a valid option', 'Enter a valid postcode', 'Enter a valid registration number', 'Enter a valid UK telephone number', 'Enter a valid date', 'Enter a real time, like 14:30', 'Enter a whole number', 'Enter N characters or fewer' and 'Enter a number between MIN and MAX'.
requirements.why: These are the fallbacks every page shares. Each page's own messages against Design Release 2.1 belong to that page's area.
requirements.deltaNote: The same defaults exist in both frontends' shared copy (repo-frontend-p1-062 to p1-070, repo-insfrontend-p4-057 to p4-065).

requirements.statement: On the animals frontend, a save that hits a recoverable backend failure re-renders the page with an alert banner titled 'There is a problem' that reads 'Sorry, there is a problem with the service. Your answers on this page have been saved. Try again in a few minutes.' The banner sits at the top of the content column.
requirements.why: Real persistence can fail, which the prototype cannot express. The banner tells the user their answers are safe.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-021 and p1-022 render the banner.

requirements.statement: On the INS frontend, a page whose service call fails is re-rendered with status 500 and a notification banner with role 'alert', titled 'There is a problem' and reading 'Sorry, there is a problem with the service. Try again in a few minutes.'
requirements.why: Real upstream services can fail, which the prototype cannot express, and the user is kept on the page.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p4-020 and p4-021 render the banner.

requirements.statement: On the animals frontend, a form post refused because the notification changed after the page was opened sends the user back to the same page. There an alert banner titled 'The notification has been updated' reads 'This notification was updated since you opened it. Review the details and try again.'
requirements.why: Concurrent edits to a stored notification are a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-023 and p1-024 implement the refusal and banner.

requirements.statement: A page inside a notification can show a strip above its content with the notification's status tag and its reference in bold: blue 'Draft', green 'Submitted', yellow 'Amending' or grey 'Deleted'. The INS layout supports the strip, but no INS page uses it.
requirements.why: This is shared page chrome that already exists. Each page's use of it belongs to that page's area.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-026 to p1-030 render the strip.

requirements.statement: Every page's footer offers 'Privacy', 'Cookies' and 'Accessibility statement' links to the GOV.UK help pages, with the OGL v3.0 licence line and Crown copyright. The service has no cookies page, privacy notice or accessibility statement of its own.
requirements.why: This is the shared footer, and it already exists on both frontends.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-031 to p1-033 and repo-insfrontend-p4-023 to p4-025 render the footer links.

requirements.statement: No page shows a cookie banner.
requirements.why: This is how the service is today. No source asks for a banner.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p1-033 shows no cookie banner on any page walked.

requirements.statement: Pages are in English, with no language toggle. Copy falls back to English, and each copy file has a Welsh twin with the same keys and no empty values. The shared Welsh copy is an unreviewed machine draft that must not ship without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
requirements.why: This is how the shared copy works today on both frontends. Design Release 2.1 has no Welsh.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-034 to p1-036 and repo-insfrontend-p4-028 to p4-030 describe the copy.

requirements.statement: Every page offers the standard GOV.UK 'Skip to main content' link, targeting #main-content.
requirements.why: This is a GOV.UK accessibility requirement, and it already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p1-030 records the link.

requirements.statement: No page shows who is signed in: no email, name or 'signed in as' strip, and no 'Sign out' link apart from the navigation's Log out.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's header and navigation show no signed-in identity, and both frontends already match.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-039, trace-e2e-p1-040 and repo-insfrontend-p4-117 show no identity.

requirements.statement: On the animals frontend, when sign-in fails the user sees a page titled and headed 'Sorry, we are unable to sign you in', asking them to 'Please try again', where 'try again' links to sign-in.
requirements.why: A failed Defra ID sign-in is an authentication case the prototype cannot express, and the page already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-040 and p1-041 give the page.

requirements.statement: On the INS frontend, a failed sign-in shows the unauthorised page: browser title 'Unable to sign in', heading 'Sorry, we are unable to sign you in.' and body 'Please try again.', where 'try again' links to /auth/sign-in. The page has no back link. It is shown when the Defra ID callback fails, the token carries no organisation or fails verification, or the user's role and permissions cannot be loaded.
requirements.why: These are authentication failures the prototype cannot express, and the page already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p4-080 and p4-083 to p4-086 give the page and when it shows.

requirements.statement: An error response is shown as the shared error page with the error's own HTTP status. The page's large heading is the status number, and a paragraph below it, which is also the browser title, reads 'Page not found' (404), 'Forbidden' (403), 'You need to sign in to view this page' (401), 'There is a problem with your request' (400) or 'Something went wrong' (any other). It shows no back link. An error inside a journey set uses that set's chrome; a path under no set uses set-free chrome whose home link is the root.
requirements.why: Real errors are a constraint the prototype cannot express, and both frontends already share this page.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-042 to p1-048 and repo-insfrontend-p4-072 to p4-078 render the page.

requirements.statement: On the animals frontend, the service root / sends a signed-in user to the default set's dashboard, /live-animals.
requirements.why: This is how the animals frontend reaches its home today.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p1-047 records the redirect.

requirements.statement: The shared notification actions read 'Copy as new' and 'Delete'. After a copy, a success message titled 'Notification copied' reads 'A new draft notification has been created.' After a delete, one titled 'Notification deleted' reads 'The notification has been deleted.'
requirements.why: This is shared copy the dashboard and notification pages already use. Comparing it with Design Release 2.1 belongs to the dashboard and notification-actions areas.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-055 to p1-058 give the copy.

requirements.statement: Address pickers offer a shared 'Add a new address' link. When a chosen address is not in the user's address book, the error reads 'The address could not be found in your address book. Select another address or try adding it again.' When the address book cannot be reached, it reads 'The address book could not be reached. Your answers on this page have been saved. Try again in a few minutes.'
requirements.why: This is shared copy the journey's address pickers already use. Comparing the pickers with Design Release 2.1 belongs to the addresses area.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-059 to p1-061 give the copy.

requirements.statement: Sign-in hands off to Defra ID with an OpenID Connect authorisation-code request (scope openid offline_access, query response mode, policy b2c_1a_cui_cpdev_signupsigninsfi), naming each frontend's own serviceId and its own /auth/sign-in-oidc callback. On success, the user's organisation, CRN and name are taken from the token and held in a server-side session.
requirements.why: Real sign-in through Defra ID is an authentication constraint the prototype's sign-in page cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p1-002 to p1-004 and trace-e2e-p15-012 record the handoff.

requirements.statement: After signing in, a user who belongs to more than one organisation is asked by Defra ID to 'Choose your organisation' from radios labelled with each organisation's name and SBI. A user with one organisation never sees that choice. The chosen organisation reaches the service through the sign-in callback, and the user lands on the page they asked for. No page in the service offers a way to switch organisation, and a page that needs an organisation returns 403 when the session has none.
requirements.why: Organisation choice is part of real Defra ID authentication, which the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p15-016 to p15-020 record the single-organisation and multi-organisation paths on the INS frontend.

requirements.statement: Signing in to one frontend signs the user in to the others without asking for credentials again, because Defra ID answers their requests straight away. Each frontend keeps its own session cookie on the shared host (sid for animals, ins-sid for INS, plants-sid for plants, all HttpOnly), so all three sessions are kept side by side. Each service has its own landing page after sign-in.
requirements.why: Moving between the animals journey and the INS dashboard and address book is cross-service behaviour the prototype cannot express. It already works.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p15-111 and p15-113 prove single sign-on and kept sessions across the three frontends. Whether signing out of one ends the others is not proven (repo-tests-p4-111-m1).

requirements.statement: A session is valid only while it is in the server-side cache (Redis when deployed). The session cookie lasts 4 hours and is HttpOnly. An expired token is refreshed when refresh is on, and otherwise the user is treated as signed out. Every route needs a signed-in user unless it opts out.
requirements.why: Real sessions are an authentication constraint the prototype cannot express, and they already work this way.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p1-031 and p1-032 record the cookies, and repo-insfrontend-p4-102 and p4-103 the session rules. What a user sees when a session lapses is not recorded (trace-e2e-p1-062).

requirements.statement: In stub mode the INS frontend signs a user in at once with no sign-in page, as 'Stub User' in the organisation given by an organisationId parameter (default 'stub-org-1'). The stub session lasts four hours, sign-out goes straight to /, and the Defra ID callback and organisation routes do not exist. Stub mode is refused in production.
requirements.why: This is how the INS frontend runs locally and in its own browser tests. It is part of today's real authentication set-up.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p4-106 to p4-113 give the stub mode.

requirements.statement: Every form post must carry a valid CSRF token (except under /health, /assets and /public). Every page carries the token in a csrf-token meta tag, every form has a hidden 'crumb' input, and the CSRF cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite Strict.
requirements.why: Protection against cross-site request forgery is a real security constraint, and it already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p1-033-m1 and repo-insfrontend-p4-114 to p4-116 show the token.

requirements.statement: The animals frontend sends a Content-Security-Policy on its pages, redirects and sign-in callback. It limits scripts, styles, fonts, images and the base URL to its own origin (plus one hashed inline script), lets forms post to itself and the address book origin, and forbids framing and plugins. It also sends Strict-Transport-Security for a year, X-Frame-Options DENY, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, X-Download-Options noopen, X-XSS-Protection and Cache-Control no-cache.
requirements.why: Security headers are a real constraint the prototype cannot express, and they already exist.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p1-052 to p1-060 record the headers.

requirements.statement: Security-header and cookie defects found on the way are not fixed by this programme: the CSP's connect-src lists 'wss' without a colon, the animals frontend sends no Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, COOP or COEP header, and the animals and plants frontends share one 'crumb' CSRF cookie on localhost.
requirements.why: These are problems in today's services that bringing the services up to Design Release 2.1 does not touch. They go to the report.

requirements.statement: The Defra ID stub's own pages are not changed by this programme: its sign-in page ('Sign in using Government Gateway', user ID and password, 'Help signing in', the 'I have forgotten my password' placeholder, the CRN error message and its non-standard error summary), its title, phase banner and doubled service name, its signed-out page and its own security headers.
requirements.why: The stub stands in for Defra ID and is not one of the programme's repos. Its defects go to the report.

requirements.statement: The tests repo's accessibility suite holds every scanned page to WCAG 2.2 AA. It runs axe with the wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and wcag22aa tags and fails on any violation, attaching a report per page. Only justified upstream or not-owned defects are excluded: govuk-frontend's conditional-reveal aria-expanded and the sign-in stub's error list. The suite scans selected states, tagged @a11y.
requirements.why: Every page this programme changes must keep passing this suite. It already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p6-001 to p6-020 define the suite.

requirements.statement: The accessibility suite walks the live-animals journey from the dashboard to the submitted page and scans every journey page, both on initial load and with its answers filled.
requirements.why: This is the existing end-to-end accessibility proof of the journey. Each page Design Release 2.1 changes must still pass it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p6-021 and p6-042 define the two walks.

requirements.statement: The accessibility suite scans the error summary state on the origin, CPH number, arrival details, transited countries and declaration pages, and the edit address details page.
requirements.why: This is the existing accessibility proof of the shared error summary on journey pages.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p6-054 to p6-060 define the scans.

requirements.statement: The accessibility suite also scans the import reason reveals, the private transporter pages, the commercial transporter register, the dashboard (populated, sorted, searched, paged, and at 320 by 568 and 568 by 320), review, submitted review, confirmation, the cancel-amendment and delete confirmations, the copied-address edit page, the contact page and the sign-in page.
requirements.why: This is the existing accessibility proof of the rest of the animals service.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p6-062 to p6-087 define the scans.

requirements.statement: The animals frontend's own browser tests check that a captioned page and the dashboard with its service navigation have no serious or critical WCAG 2 A or AA violations. They exclude govuk-frontend's conditional-reveal false positive. The INS frontend checks every page's initial render and validation-error state against WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 AA.
requirements.why: These are the existing in-repo accessibility checks that a navigation or layout change must keep passing.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p1-013 and p1-026 record the passing checks.

requirements.statement: Gaps in today's accessibility proof are not closed by this programme. The INS dashboard, sign-in and address book have no WCAG scan in the tests repo. The dashboard's copy action, the amending overview and an uploaded document are not scanned. Only five pages' error states are scanned, and only the dashboard at narrow viewports. No INS browser test proves sign-out, the unauthorised page, the error page or the banner and footer links.
requirements.why: These are coverage gaps in today's suites, not differences from Design Release 2.1. They go to the report.

requirements.statement: The tests repo's security suite runs a traffic-driven OWASP ZAP scan of the animals frontend, animals admin, INS frontend, animals backend and address book API. Playwright drives real signed-in journeys through it: sign-in and sign-out on both frontends, change mode, reveals, dashboard search, sort and paging, document upload, amend, copy, cancel and delete, submission, and the INS address book lifecycle. The run fails on any FAIL-rated alert, a capped scan or an unreached context. The active scan is refused on CDP.
requirements.why: Every route this programme adds or changes must be driven through this scan to be attacked. The suite already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p6-090 to p6-123 define the suite.

requirements.statement: Gaps in today's security scan are not closed by this programme. Plants has no security specs. The accepted path of the address book hand-off is not attacked. The animals copied-address edit page is not driven. The INS dashboard is in the scan only as a bare GET.
requirements.why: These are coverage gaps in today's suite, not differences from Design Release 2.1. They go to the report.

requirements.statement: The tests repo signs each worker in once and reuses the session. Its sign-in and cross-service tests start with no stored session. It keeps the sign-in password out of traces, and it sends only internet-bound calls through the CDP proxy.
requirements.why: Any new end-to-end proof of sign-in or navigation has to work within these existing suite rules.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p1-182 and p4-110 give the session rules.

requirements.statement: The INS frontend serves a fixed list of routes, all behind sign-in: the dashboard at /, and the address book list, add, view, edit and delete pages. It also serves /health, /auth/* and static files, plus a dev-only address lookup spike. It owns no journey, notification editing, upload or event publishing, and no database. Its target direction is to become the front door for every journey.
requirements.why: This is the shell that the dashboard, templates and address book pages Design Release 2.1 changes are added to.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p4-119 and p4-124 list the routes.

requirements.statement: Each INS dashboard row links out to the animals frontend, which owns that notification: to /notifications/{reference}, or to .../notification-view when it is submitted. Only the animals journey is linked today.
requirements.why: This is how the INS dashboard hands off across services today. Design Release 2.1's dashboard is weighed in the dashboard area.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p4-127 and p4-128 give the links.

requirements.statement: The INS dashboard at / is not scoped to the user's organisation: a signed-in user sees every organisation's notifications. This area does not fix that.
requirements.why: Organisation scoping of the dashboard is an authorisation defect owned by the dashboard area and an existing security ticket, not a layout or sign-in change. It goes to the report.

requirements.statement: The INS address book always sends the signed-in organisation to the address book API, and refuses to call it with none. Its ids are 24-character hex, and an unknown or deleted id gives 404. API field errors are mapped back to the form. Only the nine validated address fields are saved. The country list comes from reference data with GB first. A success banner shows once. A journey hand-off (journeyType, notificationId, fulfilmentId, handshakeToken) returns to the animals frontend for 'gbn-ag'.
requirements.why: These are the real persistence, validation and authorisation rules behind the address book that the navigation leads to. The address book area weighs its pages against Design Release 2.1.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p4-136 to p4-145 give the rules, and the smoke tests p4-180 to p4-182 prove them.

requirements.statement: Every change to the INS frontend follows its build rules. It stays in the govuk-frontend toolbox and keeps its four import boundaries. Each new page gets a URL builder, a route-list entry, English and Welsh copy with tests, unit tests mocked only at the network boundary, a browser test with axe checks and a Lighthouse audit. Format, lint, unit and browser suites must all pass, with cross-repo branches sharing one name. Every outside call is measured.
requirements.why: Templates and the navigation change land in the INS frontend, and these are the rules it holds every change to.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p4-158, p4-163 and p4-163-m1 state the rules.

requirements.statement: Drift in the INS frontend's documentation and dependencies is not fixed by this programme. The workspace page names INS_MODE and AUTH_STUB_MODE where the repo uses STUB_MODE, and Vite where the repo uses webpack. It also calls the README template text when the README now describes the service. Some code imports Joi without declaring it as a dependency.
requirements.why: These are housekeeping defects, not differences from Design Release 2.1. They go to the report.

requirements.statement: DR1 judgements that meet no Design Release 2.1 difference in this area build nothing here. These are the section-caption rows, the navigation row's details, the return-control rename and rule (b) on which pages end with the return controls, and the animals admin app keeping its own 'Sign out'. Each stands only where its own area finds the real frontend and Design Release 2.1 clashing on that same difference.
requirements.why: The owner's ruling makes the DR1 parity backlog a source of judgements, never of requirements. Nothing is built because DR1 says so on its own.

requirements.statement: The list's 'Status updated' glance card shows a live count for the category: the notifications whose status changed in the past 24 hours, matching the Status updated list its link opens.
requirements.why: The count is only useful if it agrees with the drill-down page, and it depends on outcomes the authorities set after submission.
requirements.blockedBy: The authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sends post-submission outcomes (action required with its reason, inspection required, delayed, completed) back to the notification record; no such feed exists today, so no real notification can be counted as needing action or as status-updated.

requirements.statement: The germinal products list shows only germinal products notifications.
requirements.why: A trader looking at one category must not see another's notifications; no service creates a germinal products notification yet, so this waits on that journey.
requirements.blockedBy: A germinal products notification journey and its dashboard must exist, with its notifications reaching the INS read model; no service builds one today and this programme covers the live-animals journey (as req-979).

requirements.statement: A germinal products notification's card shows its quantity as 'Number of packages', from the notification's package count.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 counts germinal products in packages, not animals.
requirements.blockedBy: A germinal products notification journey and its dashboard must exist, with its notifications reaching the INS read model; no service builds one today and this programme covers the live-animals journey (as req-979).

requirements.statement: On a germinal products notification's card the commodity is the species then the product type, separated by a comma, such as 'Cattle, Semen'.
requirements.why: Germinal products need the product type as well as the species to say what is coming.
requirements.blockedBy: A germinal products notification journey and its dashboard must exist, with its notifications reaching the INS read model; no service builds one today and this programme covers the live-animals journey (as req-979).

requirements.statement: A completed notification's status 'Completed' is plain styled text, not a tag.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses a tag only for statuses that ask something of the trader; no completed status reaches the service until the authorities' outcomes do (req-1082).
requirements.blockedBy: The authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sends post-submission outcomes, completed among them, back to the notification record; no completed status reaches the service today (as req-1082).
